items.title: Halley: A Predictive Control Plane for Optical AI Data Center Networks
items.description: Halley is a predictive control framework for AI data center optical networks that improves effective throughput and reduces capacity needs by forecasting failures and controlling resources with formal guarantees.

items.title: liangjianshu/multimodal-image-retrieval
items.description: 多模态检索实战：意图识别、Prompt 工程、Qwen LoRA、EmbeddingGemma 2 与 InfoNCE 对比学习。含真实演示、自有数据接入、训练评测及 RAG 检索组件学习指南。
items.ai_summary: Open-source practical project for multimodal image retrieval, featuring intent recognition, Qwen LoRA fine-tuning, and embedding comparison learning.

items.title: Multi-layer Indexer: Overlapping Selection and Attention in DeepSeek Sparse Attention
items.description: A multi-layer indexer reuses adjacent layers’ token selections to overlap indexer scans with attention, improving long-context decode throughput when combined with cross-layer indexer reuse while maintaining accuracy.

items.title: Why Pay for Long Reasoning When Rewrite Do Trick? Causal Effects of Reasoning History Compaction on Future Generation and Agent Cost
items.description: Rewriting reasoning histories into compact state records reduces future reasoning length and token costs in open-weight models without retraining.

items.title: cxcscmu/IdeaTaste
items.description: IdeaTaste - A benchmark for research taste: let LLM agents propose research ideas, then check how many of them the research area actually went on to do.
items.ai_summary: Benchmark for evaluating the research taste of LLM agents by comparing their generated proposals against subsequently published papers.

items.title: RainariesFire54079/cs2-resp-wallhack-2026
items.description: Reveal every enemy position in CS2 with real-time ESP wallhack and 2D radar, showing health, armor, C4, and dropped weapons.

items.title: TAC-CoT: Tool-Empowered Implicit Chain-of-Thought via Interleaving Explicit Tokens
items.description: TAC-CoT replaces explicit reasoning traces with compact latent segments while preserving textual tokens for tool interactions, improving agentic accuracy and reducing computation.

items.title: zaxiu88888/issue-rag
items.description: RAG over GitHub issues, with a hand-reviewed eval set and an audit of the judge itself. Reports the interval, not just the best number.
items.ai_summary: Retrieval-augmented question answering system for GitHub issue trackers that evaluates generation quality and audits its own scoring judge.

items.title: GameVerse: A Minute-Scale Gameplay Dataset for Long-Horizon Interactive World Modeling
items.description: GameVerse is a large-scale gameplay dataset with minute-long sequences and event-aligned annotations that improves long-horizon interactive world modeling.

items.title: Hybrid Computer Use: A Unified Programmatic, Semantic, and Visual Interface for General Agents
items.description: Hybrid Computer Use unifies programmatic, accessibility-based, and visual interaction channels to improve agent efficiency and success on complex desktop tasks.

items.title: MatterSeek
items.description: MatterSeek

items.title: PrunaAI/P-H3-Image
items.description: Text-to-image model from PrunaAI. 444 downloads and 131 likes so far.

items.title: Monitor Accuracy Isn't the Answer: A Decision-Value Framework for Evaluating AI Agent Restart Monitors
items.description: Classification accuracy and true-positive and false-positive rates alone do not determine whether restarting an AI agent improves success.

items.title: baidu/ERNIE-5.5-Flash-Base
items.description: Text generation model from baidu. 13 downloads and 180 likes so far.

items.title: unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF
items.description: Vision-language model from unsloth. 1.2M downloads and 1.4k likes so far.

items.title: relayworkslab/relayworks-recovery
items.description: Resume failed AI agent jobs from their last checkpoint instead of restarting them. Completed work is kept and verified, a specialist finishes only the rest, and you pay in USDC on Solana (x402) after you accept the result.
items.ai_summary: RelayWorks Recovery is an engine that resumes interrupted AI agent jobs from their last verified checkpoint instead of restarting them entirely.

items.title: Everything is an AI scam now
items.description: Trending on Hacker News from davidralphlewis.co.uk. 134 points and 53 comments.

items.title: Gauge – Open-Source CLI to recursively improve your docs
items.description: Hi HN, I’m Evan from Gauge. We’re open-sourcing our CLI to recursively improve your docs for coding agents. The CLI includes a local execution backend, so you don't need an account to try it.
items.ai_summary: Open-source command-line interface that recursively tests and improves developer documentation, skills, and Model Context Protocol servers for AI coding agents.

items.title: Qualcomm Cloud AI 100 Ultra – 150W AI Accelerator Card with 128GB at 548GB/s
items.description: Trending on Hacker News from qualcomm.com. 134 points and 54 comments.

items.title: From Pixels to Actions - Towards Native Vision-Language-Action Policies
items.description: NEO-VLA eliminates fixed visual encoders to let action policies access evolving visual representations across network depths, improving manipulation robustness.

items.title: A Framework for Context Enrichment and Selective Robustness in LLM Social Agents
items.description: Researchers use large language models as agents in social simulations, where agents are prompted with observations and background information intended to shape their actions.
items.ai_summary: Framework that uses controlled context enrichment and selective robustness as a validation criterion to evaluate LLM social agents and identify reliable behavioral patterns.

items.title: FlowReconBench: Accuracy, calibration and cost of learned and classical flow reconstruction from sparse sensors
items.description: Reconstructing full flow fields from sparse sensors requires prior assumptions about unmeasured regions and physical variables. Yet it remains unclear when learned models outperform classical estimators and which aspects of their predictions can be trusted.
items.ai_summary: Benchmark that evaluates ten learned and five classical methods for reconstructing full flow fields from sparse sensors across laminar, turbulent, and 3D regimes.

items.title: BEAKER: An Expert-Curated Benchmark for Embodied Brains in Self-Driving Chemical Laboratories
items.description: Self-Driving Chemical Laboratories (SDCLs) are moving chemical experimentation toward embodied automation, where machines must perceive laboratory scenes, reason about experimental states, and act under physical, procedural, and safety constraints.
items.ai_summary: Expert-curated benchmark containing 1,000 question-answer samples across 11 task types to evaluate multimodal large language models for self-driving chemical laboratories.

items.title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
items.description: FrontierPhysics is an end-to-end benchmark of 56 expert-designed physics tasks that evaluates AI agents on literature review, research planning, experimentation, and manuscript production using deterministic verifiers and expert rubrics.

items.title: Perceptive Humanoid Motion from Simulation
items.description: Humanoid robots have the potential to automate a wide range of physical tasks.
items.ai_summary: Humanoid autonomy system powered by a pipeline that synthesizes vision-language-motion data across procedural homes to acquire physical skills and transfer zero-shot to the physical world.

items.title: Ripple-65B Preview: U.S. Open-Weight SOTA on Agentic Coding
items.description: Trending on Hacker News from ricursive.com. 274 points and 99 comments.
items.ai_summary: Ripple-65B Preview is a dense open-weight language model pretrained on 12 trillion tokens that delivers high performance on agentic coding tasks.

items.title: Reinforcement Learning Enables Scaling Generalist Robot Policy Improvement
items.description: The introduction of generalist robot policies has enabled a single, large model to learn to perform a variety of tasks from a vast pre-training corpus.
items.ai_summary: Reinforcement learning approach that enables generalist robot policies to achieve multi-task, online self-improvement and boost performance across diverse deployment tasks simultaneously.

items.title: Motion-guided Contrastive Regularization For Latent World Models
items.description: JEPA-style world models learn action-conditioned latent dynamics without reconstructing observations, but distributional regularization alone does not ensure that their representations preserve information needed for control.
items.ai_summary: Motion-guided contrastive regularization method for latent world models that compares predicted latent transitions with episode candidates to prevent static collapse and improve planning success.

items.title: Occlusion for Free: Detecting Occlusion from the Disagreement Between Two Monocular Distance Cues
items.description: Knowing that a pedestrian is occluded is useful to a robot even when the detector cannot recover the hidden pixels, but occlusion estimators are normally trained on occlusion annotations that deployment settings rarely have.
items.ai_summary: Method that detects heavy pedestrian occlusion using the disagreement between apparent height and monocular metric depth without requiring any training or occlusion labels.

items.title: Procedural Adversarial Learning
items.description: For many computer vision tasks, neural networks can be trained to produce a low average error, yet they still fail on seemingly simple scenes. Reducing these failures requires first finding them, but they may not be in a fixed dataset.
items.ai_summary: Procedural adversarial learning framework that searches the input space of a procedural generator using zeroth-order optimization to find difficult test instances and reduce worst-case errors in computer vision models.

items.title: Dull, Dirty, Dangerous? Working Conditions and the Limits of Occupational AI Exposure
items.description: Automation is often justified as relief from dull, dirty, and dangerous work. I examine how these conditions relate to occupational AI exposure using 21 O*NET items across 754 US occupations.
items.ai_summary: Study examining how item groupings and occupational characteristics shape the interpretation of occupational AI exposure estimates across various US jobs.

items.title: Adaptive Multi Mode: Budget-Aware Routing of Optimizers By Online Landscape Probes
items.description: The best classical optimizer for a continuous black-box problem depends on its budget and landscape. Existing routers decide from the dimension and budget, past improvement or features fitted to one benchmark, and few test an optimizer's implicit assumptions online.
items.ai_summary: Adaptive Multi Mode framework that dynamically routes a continuous black-box optimization budget among multiple engines using online probes of problem landscapes.

items.title: SpecCompact: Accelerating LLM Agent Context Compaction with Slot-Parallel Semantic Speculative Verification
items.description: LLM agents use context compaction to manage growing interaction histories, but summarizing long histories with large models can introduce substantial delays. Compaction therefore requires balancing information retention against latency.
items.ai_summary: SpecCompact is a framework that accelerates LLM agent context compaction through slot-parallel semantic speculation using a fine-tuned small drafter and target model verification.

items.title: Learning to Decode Linear Codes with Generalized Belief Propagation Network
items.description: Error correcting codes are a fundamental component of communication systems, enabling reliable data transmission over noisy channels. Recently, neural decoders have demonstrated notable performance gains over classical iterative algorithms.
items.ai_summary: Generalized Belief Propagation Network is a neural decoder for linear codes that preserves message-passing symmetry and uses cascaded variable-node updates to achieve lower bit error rates.

items.title: PixelSpline: Continuous Space-Time Video Super-Resolution via Endpoint-Anchored Shared Pixel Trajectories
items.description: Existing continuous space-time video super-resolution methods often infer motion from only two endpoint frames and model the two motion directions independently, making them vulnerable to ambiguous correspondence and inconsistent trajectories.
items.ai_summary: Continuous space-time video super-resolution framework that uses endpoint-anchored pixel trajectories to warp endpoint colors and align features for consistent motion reconstruction.

items.title: On Turn-Level Best-of-N Sampling for Scaling LLM Agents
items.description: In this work, we evaluate a simple inference-time scaling approach based on \textit{turn-level best-of-N sampling} (\method) for large language model (LLM) agents on complex, long-horizon tasks.
items.ai_summary: Turn-level best-of-N sampling inference-time scaling approach that uses a generator-selector framework to improve accuracy and consistency in LLM agents on complex tasks.

items.title: CounterFactual Retrieval for Evidence-Aware Individual Animal Identification
items.description: Automated identification of individual animals is moving from small curated studies toward shared benchmarks and reusable foundation models.
items.ai_summary: Counterfactual Foreground Retrieval is an evaluation protocol that uses different view masks to determine whether animal identification models rely on actual animal features or background shortcuts.

items.title: Balancing hierarchical representation and quantization: A performance trade-off in text embeddings
items.description: Hierarchical text embedding models offer variable-length representations, while quantization reduces numerical precision; both aim to improve computational efficiency. This work is an empirical benchmark study of how these two orthogonal, already-established techniques interact.
items.ai_summary: Empirical benchmark study investigating the performance trade-offs of combining hierarchical text representations with numerical quantization to improve embedding storage efficiency.

items.title: CompressionBench: How can your coding agents compress LLMs?
items.description: Recursive self-improvement requires AI systems to improve the models and infrastructure used by subsequent systems. LLM compression offers a concrete efficiency objective: retain a pretrained model's behavior within a smaller model storage budget.
items.ai_summary: Framework called CompressionBench that evaluates how coding agents autonomously compress large language models to improve inference storage efficiency.

items.title: LongBanana: An Expert-Verified Benchmark for Long-Context Multi-Reference Image Synthesis
items.description: We introduce LongBanana, to our knowledge the first expert-designed and expert-verified benchmark for long-context multi-reference image synthesis in the age of agent-driven image generation.
items.ai_summary: Benchmark called LongBanana that evaluates expert-verified, long-context multi-reference image synthesis tasks for agent-driven image generation systems.

items.title: Regression with Many Generated Controls
items.description: We consider linear regression when some covariates are endogenous, a variable sufficient to control for endogeneity exists but is latent, and the practitioner can generate many proxies for the latent control.
items.ai_summary: Methodology for linear regression with latent endogeneity that uses multiple proxy variables generated by AI and machine learning methods to consistently estimate parameters without validation data.

items.title: Visual Token Routing: Learning to keep tokens that matter
items.description: Computer-use agents (CUAs) have recently achieved superhuman performance on several long-horizon benchmarks. However, their computational cost limits their use in long-horizon tasks and real-time domains such as video games.
items.ai_summary: Training framework called Visual Token Routing that uses a spatio-temporal router to select relevant visual tokens, reducing computational costs for computer-use agents.

items.title: Trainspotting: Learning Object-Centric 3D Reconstruction from Found Photos
items.description: State-of-the-art feedforward reconstruction models perform poorly on in-the-wild object-centric photo collections. They are trained largely on single-session object captures whose images vary in viewpoint while the object and its environment remain nearly fixed.
items.ai_summary: Dataset called Trainspotting containing Wikimedia Commons objects and photos to improve object-centric 3D reconstruction and camera pose estimation in feedforward models.

items.title: Persona Perspectives: Adopting Viewpoints Reorganizes Representations in LLMs
items.description: Common methods for monitoring features in large language models (LLMs) such as linear probes and sparse autoencoders (SAEs) assume that features maintain a consistent representation across contexts.
items.ai_summary: Study demonstrating that prompting large language models to adopt political personas systematically alters their internal representations and safety-relevant evaluation metrics.

items.title: Navigating Disagreement Among Criteria for Evaluating Explanation Faithfulness
items.description: Faithfulness requires that algorithmic explanations accurately reflect the model's behavior. Yet existing operationalizations of faithfulness can disagree about whether the same explanation is faithful, leaving developers and auditors to choose among conflicting evaluations.
items.ai_summary: Analytical framework for evaluating explanation faithfulness that locates operational disagreements in model claims, comparisons, and aggregations to help auditors navigate conflicting criteria.

items.title: Where to Connect? Boosting MLLMs via Dynamic Gated Pathways across ALL ViT and LLM Layers
items.description: A central yet under-explored question in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) is where to connect---how visual information from a hierarchical vision encoder should be wired into the layer-wise semantics of a large language model.
items.ai_summary: Routing mechanism called Dynamic Gated Pathways that establishes all-to-all connections between vision encoder and language model layers to improve multimodal model performance.

items.title: Thermally Conditioned Time-Series Forecasting of Grain Growth in Polycrystalline Materials
items.description: Grain growth during heat treatment strongly affects the microstructure of polycrystalline materials and, consequently, their mechanical properties.
items.ai_summary: Recurrent neural network framework that incorporates thermal descriptors to forecast grain size distributions and growth dynamics in polycrystalline materials under non-isothermal conditions.

items.title: ServerBench: How can your coding agents design specialized LLM serving systems?
items.description: Large language model (LLM) coding agents develop software through experimentation, offering an opportunity to design the serving systems supporting their own operation.
items.ai_summary: Benchmark called ServerBench that evaluates coding agents on designing and optimizing specialized, verified large language model serving systems based on latency and GPU cost.

items.title: Same Layout, Different Count: What Number Words Do Past Ten in Text-to-Image Models
items.description: Ask SD3.5-Medium for twelve of an object and then, from the same starting noise, for twenty-five. The picture keeps its layout, but the count changes about as much as it would under a new random seed, and in no consistent direction.
items.ai_summary: Researchers evaluate how five open text-to-image models handle number words beyond ten objects, finding that layout and object count often decouple past this threshold.

items.title: Before You Continue: Evaluating Time-Sensitive Safety Awareness in Conversational Assistants
items.description: Large language model (LLM) assistants increasingly help users with everyday activities that involve time-dependent constraints. However, users may not mention these constraints in later requests, requiring assistants to recognize and adjust their advice accordingly.
items.ai_summary: Researchers introduce TASC, a benchmark to evaluate whether conversational large language models apply time-dependent constraints when responding to user requests.

items.title: Context-Aware Autoregressive Image Generation for Emerging Reasoning Properties
items.description: Autoregressive image generation has recently emerged as a competitive visual generation paradigm, yet its generation order is often predefined or heuristic, such as next-patch prediction, random-order prediction, or one-step generation for specific scales.
items.ai_summary: Researchers propose a context-aware autoregressive image generation framework that dynamically determines the next token location based on global context and local information to improve structural robustness and reasoning capabilities.

items.title: Context--Answer Metamodels: Forecasting LLM Activations Before the First Answer Token
items.description: Under stochastic decoding, a single context can elicit many different answers from a language model. Characterizing this variation typically requires many expensive autoregressive rollouts, each revealing only one realization.
items.ai_summary: Researchers introduce context-answer metamodels that map context activation sequences to forecast mean-pooled answer activations and rollout variability in language models before the first token is generated.

items.title: LooM: Loop-Invariant Memory for Causal Encoder-Decoder Language Models
items.description: Looped Transformers increase effective depth by re-executing shared layers, but three limitations hinder their adoption: memory grows with the loop count, compute can only be adjusted in whole-block steps, and the loop count is hard to change after training.
items.ai_summary: Researchers propose LooM, a loop-invariant memory method for causal encoder-decoder language models that uses shared layer execution with a fixed-size cache to provide variable compute budgets at deployment.

items.title: Alignment Myopia in Generative AI
items.description: Current generative AI alignment relies on a myopic paradigm that prioritizes immediate conversational satisfaction.
items.ai_summary: Researchers propose a paradigm shift toward long-horizon alignment in generative AI that accounts for how persistent human-AI interaction shapes long-term human well-being and avoids adverse outcomes like cognitive atrophy.

items.title: Enabling AWS Cloud FPGA Development Using High-Level Vitis HLS
items.description: We present a toolchain for development of ML models on AWS EC2 F2 cloud FPGA infrastructure from high-level language, implementing a complete Vitis HLS to HDK bridge to AFI workflow that has been absent from the academic literature despite eight years of AWS FPGA availability.
items.ai_summary: Researchers present an end-to-end development toolchain and methodology using high-level Vitis HLS to implement machine learning models on AWS cloud FPGA infrastructure.

items.title: Systolic Linear Attention: Co-Designing Tile-Grouped Gated Delta Attention for TPUs
items.description: Gated-delta linear attention layers such as Gated DeltaNet (GDN), Kimi Delta Attention (KDA), and GDN-2 are tuned for GPUs, where small tensor-core tiles and fast vector registers make per-channel decay rescaling and sequential in-block solves cheap.
items.ai_summary: Researchers propose Systolic Linear Attention, a hardware-co-designed attention layer that reshapes gated delta attention around Google TPU matrix units to achieve faster training and pre-training speeds.

items.title: Rules, Traces and Routing Statistics: Training and Calibration Data for Open Models on ARC-AGI-2
items.description: We study which training and calibration data help three open models solve ARC-AGI-2 tasks when the solver runs offline on four L4 GPUs for at most 12 hours. We compare data offline on public tasks and report 189 runs on the 120 hidden semi-private tasks.
items.ai_summary: Researchers study the impact of training data and offline inference procedures on open models solving ARC-AGI-2 tasks, showing significant performance gains from targeted fine-tuning and inference optimizations.

items.title: GFlowQEC: Generative Flow Networks that Learn to Sample Quantum LDPC Codes
items.description: Choosing a quantum error-correcting code for a real device means scoring candidates with circuit-level simulations so slow that only a few hundred can be run. So every evaluation counts, and a search is judged by how many good codes it finds per paid evaluation.
items.ai_summary: Researchers introduce GFlowQEC, a generative flow network method that learns to sample quantum LDPC codes to efficiently discover high-scoring codes despite slow circuit-level simulations.

items.title: Open-HumanScale: An Open Recipe for Scaling Human and Robot Experience for Embodied Foundation Models
items.description: Egocentric human video offers a scalable source of manipulation priors for robot learning, yet translating raw data scale into generalizable robot policies demands rigorous data curation and training recipes.
items.ai_summary: Open-HumanScale introduces an open recipe and a 50,000-hour egocentric video corpus to scale pretraining for robot learning, achieving high success rates on simulation and physical benchmarks.

items.title: SAUCE: Summary Analysis Using Conversation Entailment
items.description: With the growing need for evaluating Large Language Models (LLMs) and their applications to speech, challenges persist in summarizing and evaluating conversations that lack a clear end goal.
items.ai_summary: SAUCE is a reference-free evaluation pipeline for cross-lingual conversational speech summarization that measures summary accuracy and fact coverage through text entailment.

items.title: Evolutionary Design of Interpretable Spatial Descriptors for Structure-Property Relationship Discovery
items.description: Structure property prediction is a classical task in machine learning, ranging from molecular activity and materials properties to local functional responses measured in microscopy.
items.ai_summary: Evolutionary design of interpretable spatial descriptors optimizes spatial partitions and pooling operations using a genetic algorithm to improve structure-property relationship discovery in image-based regression tasks.

items.title: LLMs Don't Know What They Know: Benchmarking Temporal Self-Knowledge for Financial Backtesting
items.description: Financial backtests of large language models (LLMs) are meaningful only if the model did not already know the outcomes it is asked to predict.
items.ai_summary: FinDendro is a benchmark of 2,226 dated U.S. facts used to demonstrate that large language models cannot be certified leak-free for financial backtesting through self-reporting or stated knowledge cutoffs.

items.title: Measuring Risk, Not Harm: Detecting Psychological Harm Risk Factors in LLM Conversations
items.description: Psychological harms from interactions with large language models cannot be monitored directly because they may emerge over repeated interactions and depend strongly on subjective individual user context.
items.ai_summary: Measuring risk rather than harm, a response-level behavioral risk-factor detection framework provides a scalable measurement layer for longitudinal psychological-safety monitoring in large language model conversations.

items.title: Task-Efficient Agent Evaluation Using Cached Traces
items.description: Efficient benchmarking estimates a system's full benchmark performance from a small number of task executions. Standard approaches rely solely on the binary correctness of executions from a collection of already-evaluated reference systems.
items.ai_summary: Task-efficient agent evaluation uses LLM-extracted summary embeddings of execution traces to predict new system performance and reduce benchmarking errors.

items.title: ConDR: Conservative Reachability through Neural Hamilton-Jacobi Subsolutions
items.description: Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) Reachability identifies the unsafe states of a dynamical system from which it can be forced into failure under worst-case disturbance. However, classical grid-based solvers scale exponentially with state dimension.
items.ai_summary: Conservative DeepReach is a neural Hamilton-Jacobi reachability method that learns a subsolution to ensure computed unsafe sets contain true system failures for safe control.

items.title: Message-passing graph persistence
items.description: Message-passing graph neural networks (GNNs) are limited in expressive power by the one-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman test.
items.ai_summary: Message-Passing Graph Persistence is a family of topological descriptors that incorporates graph neural network message passing into filtrations to improve graph classification and regression.

items.title: VA-TDM: A Unified View for Improving Few-Step Diffusion Models by Velocity Adversarial Distillation
items.description: Velocity Adversarial Distillation and trajectory-aware supervision enable high-quality few-step diffusion and flow generation with state-of-the-art results.

items.title: Transforming Integer Grids to Spatial Intuition: Perception, Not Planning, Governs ARC-AGI-3
items.description: Sample-efficient fluid intelligence requires agents that rapidly form working models of unfamiliar interactive environments. ARC-AGI-3 tests this across uninstructed visual games scored by Relative Human Action Efficiency, which penalizes exploratory waste quadratically.
items.ai_summary: SARBLOH is an open-weight agent that uses a zero-parameter spatial perception engine and code-as-action runtime to rapidly model unfamiliar interactive visual environments on ARC-AGI-3.

items.title: Ranking Agreement Does Not Reveal Paragraph-Edit Agreement in Two Released Paper Acceptance Predictors
items.description: A fast acceptance classifier could select revisions for a slower evaluator. We ask whether agreement on existing papers supports that use.
items.ai_summary: Acceptance predictors for academic papers show that agreement on original paper rankings does not translate to agreement on paragraph-edit scores.

items.title: Fundamental Limits of Coherent Imaging in The Presence of Atmospheric Turbulence
items.description: We study the fundamental limits of jointly estimating the signal amplitude and the atmospheric phase distortion in complex-valued multi-look coherent imaging, where the measurements are corrupted by multiplicative speckle and additive Gaussian noise, all looks share a known…

items.title: FedFiOT: Fisher-Weighted Optimal Transport for Model Merging in One-Shot and Few-Round Federated Learning
items.description: One-shot and few-round federated learning (FL) reduce communication burden by constructing a global model within one or a few communication rounds, but often achieve lower performance than conventional multi-round FL.
items.ai_summary: Fisher-weighted optimal transport framework called FedFiOT aligns neurons and aggregates models in one-shot and few-round federated learning to overcome client drift and heterogeneity.

items.title: Semantic Residual Vector Quantization for Sign Language Generation
items.description: Sign language generation (SLG) maps written sentences into signing motion while preserving both lexical content and fine-grained articulation.
items.ai_summary: Semantic Residual Vector Quantization framework for sign language generation breaks down sentence translation into a two-level process moving from semantic content to detailed kinematic motion.

items.title: Regularization vs. Convolution in Kernel-Based Hypothesis Testing
items.description: The maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) test is a popular nonparametric test on general domains. Two lines of work have studied its optimality through structurally different approaches.

items.title: WISE: An Agentic Framework for Whole-page Multimodal Search Experience Attribution
items.description: Algorithm-driven services, including search, recommendation, and advertising, rely on multi-stage model pipelines. While research prioritizes model optimization, post-deployment monitoring focuses on operational reliability.
items.ai_summary: Agentic framework named WISE diagnoses system quality issues in industrial search by discovering user-facing problems and tracing their origins back to underlying algorithmic components.

items.title: Benchmarking Fine-Grained Visual Reasoning for Remote Sensing in Urban Management
items.description: Fine-grained visual reasoning is essential for remote sensing in urban management, yet remains underexplored in the evaluation of multimodal large language models (MLLMs).
items.ai_summary: Benchmark called UMBench evaluates fine-grained visual reasoning for urban remote sensing tasks and shows that an evidence-first chain-of-thought method improves multimodal model performance.

items.title: Route First, See Later: Enabling Vision Agents to Reason Scientifically by Separating Routing Policy from Action Spaces
items.description: Scientific image-analysis workflows require agents to select among diverse capabilities like description, detection, counting, and segmentation.
items.ai_summary: Extensible architecture named ZETA separates routing policy from action execution in scientific vision agents to improve reliability and auditability during image-analysis workflows.

items.title: Continual Classification Beyond the Kernel Regime: Harnessing the Sparsity Bias of L2 Regularization in Diagonal Linear Networks
items.description: We study logistic regression for continual learning with linear predictors in a high-dimensional statistical setting.
items.ai_summary: Weighted variant of L2 regularization for diagonal linear networks extends beneficial sparsity bias to continual learning, yielding faster convergence when learning from sparse teachers.

items.title: EvoWorld: Towards Out-of-Sight World Evolution in Generative Video Models
items.description: Generative video models are increasingly used as visual world simulators, yet their primary strength lies in rendering plausible pixels rather than reasoning about how a world should evolve.
items.ai_summary: Brain-renderer collaboration framework called EvoWorld uses a vision-language model to reason about state transitions and guide a video renderer in generating causally consistent world evolution.

items.title: TailSteer: Trajectory-Tail Steering for Drift-Resistant Multi-turn Image Editing
items.description: TailSteer, a final-stage training framework, reduces cumulative visual drift in multi-turn editing by keeping early denoising dynamics close to the base model and learning tail-focused preservation corrections from on-policy rollouts, preserving pretrained generative and…
items.ai_summary: Training framework called TailSteer improves drift-resistant multi-turn image editing by concentrating preservation corrections near the trajectory tail of on-policy denoising rollouts.

items.title: Coupled Scene Graph Anticipation: When With-Constraint Recall Hides Structural Inconsistency
items.description: Scene Graph Anticipation (SGA) predicts object relationships in future video frames.
items.ai_summary: CoupledSGA proposes a relationship interaction graph and structural consistency loss for video scene graph anticipation to prevent mutually exclusive object relationship predictions.

items.title: Smartphone-Aided VR Exergames for HIIT: Gamifying Fitness with Real-Time Pose Estimation
items.description: This paper introduces an innovative virtual reality (VR) exergame system designed to gamify High-Intensity Interval Training (HIIT) workouts through 11 predefined combo moves, including squat-punch combinations, bilateral arm strikes, and diagonal stretch combos.
items.ai_summary: Smartphone-Aided VR Exergames for HIIT introduces a virtual reality exergame system using smartphone pose estimation and large language models to provide real-time workout assessments.

items.title: ConceptARC at Scale: Studying Conceptual Understanding in Reasoning Models
items.description: Large reasoning models (LRMs) perform well on challenging benchmarks, yet it remains unclear whether they form generalizable abstractions across conceptually related reasoning tasks.
items.ai_summary: ConceptARC at Scale introduces a task generator and a 1,600-task dataset to evaluate abstract reasoning and conceptual understanding in large reasoning models.

items.title: Template Gap Reconstruction for Shell Output Simulation with Small Language Models
items.description: Small language models offer a compact basis for shell simulation without executing submitted commands, but full-output decoding requires them to predict recurring utility structure alongside content that varies across executions.
items.ai_summary: Template gap reconstruction uses reusable output literals with autoregressively generated gaps to improve shell output simulation fidelity and reduce token generation in small language models.

items.title: Turns Matter: Advancing Streaming Video RL via Turn-Level Credit
items.description: TurnWise improves streaming video understanding by assigning turn-level credit and balancing decision weights in group relative policy optimization.

items.title: Dexterous Robotic Hands in the Foundation-Model Era: A Full-Stack Survey of Hardware, Data, Cross-Embodiment Transfer, Learning, and Evaluation
items.description: Dexterous robotic hands are increasingly coupled to large-scale human data and foundation models, yet progress in hardware, representation learning and evaluation is often assessed separately.
items.ai_summary: This paper surveys advancements in dexterous robotic hands from hardware and data collection to cross-embodiment transfer, learning, and evaluation.

items.title: Symmetry Breaking at the Edge of Stability via Central Flow Analysis
items.description: Continuous symmetries in neural networks lead to conserved quantities that are invariant under gradient flow, such as layer balancedness in linear and ReLU networks.
items.ai_summary: This study uses central flow dynamics to analyze how gradient flow conservation laws evolve and break at the edge of stability in neural networks.

items.title: Reasoning over Non-Parametric Memory in Multilingual LLMs: A Cognitive-Based Analysis of Relational Knowledge
items.description: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) assumes that language models can reason over relations stated in their context rather than fall back on associations memorized during pretraining.
items.ai_summary: Rel-Bloom is a multilingual diagnostic benchmark used to evaluate evidence-conditioned relational reasoning and non-parametric memory in language models.

items.title: Energy-Guided Transport for Projection-Free Physics-Informed Flow Matching
items.description: Deep generative models, particularly Flow Matching frameworks, have emerged as powerful tools for synthesizing complex physical systems.
items.ai_summary: Energy-Guided Transport introduces a training-free framework that applies a continuous dissipative force via automatic differentiation to guide generative physics models toward physical constraints.

items.title: Beyond the principle-practice gap: Responsible AI as situated epistemic and ethical practice
items.description: Responsible AI scholarship has found that ethical principles are frequently not reflected in AI design and development.
items.ai_summary: This paper examines how institutional and professional conditions shape ethical practices and agency in the design and governance of AI systems.

items.title: ALTO: African and Levantine Tech-Facilitated Gender-Based Violence Corpus
items.description: Tech-facilitated gender based violence (TFGBV) is a pervasive online harm affecting women and gender minority groups through its many direct and covert forms.
items.ai_summary: ALTO is a community-led multilingual dataset of tech-facilitated gender-based violence instances in Levantine Arabic, African French, and Swahili for improving harm detection models.

items.title: Where It Breaks: Diagnosing Perception, Memory, and Decision Failures of a Vision-Language Agent in Pac-Man
items.description: Training an agent to play Pac-Man with only up, down, left and right actions raises a basic question: when performance is poor, what should be improved? Difficulty can arise from reading the screen or from choosing actions over a long sequence.
items.ai_summary: Vision-language agent study in Pac-Man investigates perception and policy failures, showing that textual board representations dramatically improve maze completion rates.

items.title: Agent-Driven Generative Priors for Pathology Image Synthesis and Segmentation
items.description: Deep learning methods for pathology are constrained by the limited availability and high cost of large-scale pixel-level annotations.
items.ai_summary: Three-stage pathology framework integrates automated screening, generative representation learning, and lightweight adaptation to achieve state-of-the-art semantic segmentation performance.

items.title: PINR-ESI: Physics-Informed Self-Supervised Implicit Neural Representation Framework for EEG Extended-Source Imaging
items.description: EEG extended-source imaging aims to localize active cortical regions and characterize their spatial extent, yet supervised inverse networks typically depend on synthetic EEG-source pairs and may be sensitive to synthetic-to-real mismatch.
items.ai_summary: Physics-informed self-supervised implicit neural representation framework performs EEG extended-source imaging without paired source labels or simulation-based supervised pretraining.

items.title: Don't Replace, Complement: A Detector-Agnostic Subspace Signal for Near-OOD Detection
items.description: Post-hoc out-of-distribution (OOD) detection is mature on far-OOD yet remains weak on near-OOD.
items.ai_summary: Per-class Low-dimensional sUbspace Signal is a targeted score fused additively with base detectors to consistently improve near-out-of-distribution detection performance.

items.title: LifeVal: Evaluating AI Model Performance on Personalized Agentic Consumer Tasks
items.description: We introduce LifeVal, a benchmark evaluating AI model performance on personalized agentic consumer tasks.
items.ai_summary: LifeVal is a consumer task benchmark evaluating personalized AI digital superassistant performance across valuable life tasks.

items.title: Sekai: Incremental Event Memory for Generalized Reasoning Video Segmentation
items.description: Online reasoning video segmentation (Online RVS) requires a model to segment query-referred objects as a video streams in, using only the frames observed so far.
items.ai_summary: Sekai is an online framework with structured memory and a memory-grounded decoder that significantly outperforms existing online reasoning video segmentation methods.

items.title: SecureGARD: Dynamic Ontology-Guided Governance for Secure Tool-Using LLM Agents
items.description: Tool-using large language model (LLM) agents translate model outputs into consequential actions, turning indirect prompt injection into an execution-security problem.
items.ai_summary: SecureGARD is a dynamic ontology-guided governance framework that achieves a zero percent attack success rate against indirect prompt injections in tool-using LLM agents.

items.title: Do unlearning algorithms learn the right features?
items.description: Machine unlearning is commonly evaluated with standard post-deletion metrics that compare an unlearned model to one retrained on the remaining data. Such snapshot evaluations can conceal consequential differences in the features the two models encode.
items.ai_summary: Feature recovery measure evaluates machine unlearning methods, revealing that models passing standard metrics often fail to recover retrained features.

items.title: Self-Directed Apple Tasting
items.description: We study the classical apple-tasting setting, a partial feedback model in which the learner observes the true label only when it predicts $1$. A combinatorial characterization for the rates of this problem in the online adversarial setting has been studied by Raman et al. (2024).
items.ai_summary: Study of the self-directed apple-tasting setting establishes a tetrachotomy on the expected minimax number of mistakes for online learners based on specific dimensions.

items.title: AgentTrustCI: Build-Time Policy, Grounding, and Trajectory Tests for Java LLM Agents
items.description: Infrastructure security does not establish whether an LLM agent selected an allowed tool, grounded its answer in tool output, or followed a required workflow.
items.ai_summary: AgentTrustCI is a Java and JUnit 5 testing framework that expresses application-layer policy, grounding, and trajectory checks for LLM agents over recorded traces.

items.title: CardioDrift: Automatic Cardiac Motion Tracking on a 3D Atlas Mesh via Shape-aware Coherent Point Drift with Slice Shift Correction
items.description: Automatic cardiac motion tracking from cine cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging is essential for quantifying myocardial motion abnormalities associated with cardiovascular disease.
items.ai_summary: CardioDrift is an automatic, atlas-based probabilistic framework that tracks subject-specific cardiac motion on a 3D atlas mesh to quantify myocardial motion abnormalities.

items.title: Where Search Agents Go Off the Rails: Graph-Grounded Step-Level Verification
items.description: Search-augmented reasoning systems can reach correct answers while making errors in intermediate steps. Reliable auditing must check whether evidence $D$ covers the question $Q$, reasoning $T$ addresses $Q$, and $T$ is grounded in $D$.
items.ai_summary: GraphRail is a verification system that represents requirements, evidence, and reasoning as structured claims to audit search-augmented reasoning systems without a generative judge.

items.title: Fingerprinting the Dispatchers behind Distributed Model Extraction
items.description: API distillation campaigns try to hide model-stealing traffic by splitting requests across thousands of load-balanced accounts, which standard content classifiers often miss.
items.ai_summary: Request timing analysis can forensically rank accounts used in distributed model extraction campaigns by revealing underlying dispatching strategies like round-robin counters or key-shuffling pools.

items.title: Beyond accuracy: what AI assurance needs to establish in public services
items.description: Public bodies increasingly rely on AI-produced evidence, including classifications, summaries and assessments. These outputs can inform policy decisions and service delivery, making their reliability a matter of public accountability.
items.ai_summary: Evaluations of GPT-4o configurations classifying political questions reveal that output consistency and high accuracy do not guarantee alignment with human coding or correctness.

items.title: Detecting Silent Action-Interface Mismatch with Calibrated Relational World Models
items.description: A robot action can satisfy shape and range constraints yet carry the wrong semantics: axes may be permuted, signs inverted, rotations rescaled, or gripper polarity reversed.
items.ai_summary: Learned state-action-effect relations serve as offline contracts for detecting silent action-interface mismatches in robots and ranking their likely fields.

items.title: Dynamical State-Space Diffusion for Spatiotemporal Prediction
items.description: Diffusion models for temporal prediction typically corrupt each future frame with independent noise, leaving temporal dependence entirely to the denoiser. We propose Dynamical State-Space Diffusion (DSSD), which learns the temporal structure of the corruption process itself.
items.ai_summary: Dynamical State-Space Diffusion is a temporal prediction model that learns the temporal structure of the noise corruption process using stable diagonal state-space models.

items.title: OpenAI to acquire Pierre Computer Company
items.description: https://twitter.com/pierrecomputer/status/211799903617518818...

items.title: Replicability, Reproducibility, and Robustness in Political and Social Science Research with Large Language Models
items.description: This chapter addresses the central reproducibility problem of research with large language models. LLM output is probabilistic and varies across models and versions, which can have significant effects on downstream statistical results.
items.ai_summary: A probabilistic standard and stacked ensemble of open-weight models are introduced to address reproducibility problems and improve estimation precision in LLM social science research.

items.title: Human Motion Prediction via Continual Prior Compensation
items.description: Human Motion Prediction (HMP) aims to predict future human poses at different moments according to observed past motion sequences.
items.ai_summary: Continual Prior Compensation is a temporal continual learning framework that progressively trains human motion prediction models across varied temporal moments to prevent short-term learning interference.

items.title: Uncertainty-Driven Efficient Communication for UAV-Based Collaborative Perception
items.description: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based collaborative perception enables multiple agents to share complementary perceptual information, overcoming limitations such as occlusion and limited sensing range.
items.ai_summary: UCP is an uncertainty-driven framework that uses observational and discriminative uncertainty estimates to optimize inter-agent communication for UAV-based collaborative perception.

items.title: TestBED: An Open-Source Toolkit for Bayesian Experimental Design
items.description: Bayesian experimental design (BED) is a principled framework for intelligent data acquisition with applications across a wide range of scientific and industrial domains.
items.ai_summary: TestBED is a general-purpose, open-source toolkit that decomposes Bayesian experimental design into modular components to facilitate method implementation, comparison, and benchmarking.

items.title: Trick-or-Treat: Adversarial Evaluation of Multimodal Medical Reasoning with Synthetic Images
items.description: We used medical image synthesis to create a challenging multimodal evaluation framework that exposes hallucination behaviors in frontier models.
items.ai_summary: Evaluation framework called Trick-or-Treat pairs real chest radiographs with synthetic clinical photographs to expose hallucination behaviors in multimodal frontier medical models.

items.title: Noise-regularized training of quantum circuit Born machines under a finite shot budget
items.description: Quantum circuit Born machines (QCBMs) can learn distributions that are hard to sample from classically, but their value depends on generalizing from finite training data. Here, we study how hardware noise affects this generalization.
items.ai_summary: Quantum circuit Born machines training framework called GENIE uses noise-regularized training with capped error mitigation and held-out data to optimize generalization under a finite shot budget.

items.title: Does Frontier AI Strengthen Cyber Defense? Evidence from Project Glasswing
items.description: Defenders and attackers race to find the same software flaws.
items.ai_summary: Study of Project Glasswing shows that early access to frontier AI model Claude Mythos Preview helped tech firms find and fix significantly more software vulnerabilities before attackers exploited them.

items.title: From Certified Pairs to a Certified Hub: Reasoner-Checked Crosswalks for the Information Exchange Standard
items.description: A national digital twin was conceived as an ecosystem of twins connected through mappings to a common foundation, but the roadmap that promises to confirm those mappings are valid never says what valid means.
items.ai_summary: Logic-based alignment repair and reasoning techniques are applied to the Information Exchange Standard to construct valid, coherent, and conservative crosswalks and hubs for a national digital twin.

items.title: Interactive World Simulation with Cosmos for Physical AI
items.description: We present a shared framework that adapts Cosmos world foundation models for real-time interactive world simulation in Physical AI.
items.ai_summary: Shared framework adapts Cosmos world foundation models to provide real-time interactive world simulation for training and evaluating Physical AI agents and applications.

items.title: Learning to Track Cells from Sparse Annotations in 3D Time-Lapse Microscopy
items.description: Reconstructing cell lineages from 3D time-lapse microscopy requires distinguishing cell motion from division and inferring temporally consistent connections.
items.ai_summary: Cell tracking pipeline integrates sparse annotations, motion and correspondence features, and joint event selection to accurately reconstruct cell lineages in 3D time-lapse microscopy.

items.title: Dimension-Free Private Mean Estimation is Impossible Without the Covariance
items.description: We study the limits of differentially private Gaussian mean estimation when the covariance matrix is unknown. Prior work shows that when the covariance $Σ$ is known, the optimal sample complexity can depend only on its spectrum, rather than on the ambient dimension $d$.
items.ai_summary: Research establishes new lower bounds demonstrating that differentially private Gaussian mean estimation cannot achieve dimension-free sample complexity or error bounds when the covariance matrix is unknown.

items.title: From Reconstruction to Imputation: Test-Time Optimization for Missing Time-Series Channels
items.description: Complete sensor-channel failures create a difficult form of time-series missingness: local interpolation is unavailable, and deploying a separately trained imputer for every failure pattern may be impractical.
items.ai_summary: Test-time optimization method converts a frozen sequence reconstructor into an imputer by treating missing time-series entries as optimization variables that minimize reconstruction error on observed coordinates.

items.title: Alternatives to Shallow Autoencoders for Collaborative Filtering
items.description: Collaborative filtering (CF) is a cornerstone of recommender systems and plays a relevant role in many modern applications. CF uses user-item interaction data to discover future preferences.
items.ai_summary: Hybrid collaborative filtering models that incorporate user-user information outperform standard shallow autoencoders on well-known recommendation system benchmarks.

items.title: Verifier-Guided Self-Consistency: Test-Time Reasoning with Imperfect Generators and Verifiers
items.description: Large language models can solve many multi-step reasoning problems, but their reasoning remains brittle: plausible intermediate steps often lead to incorrect answers.
items.ai_summary: Stochastic decoding framework called Verifier-Guided Self-Consistency combines step-level correctness and future-outcome estimates to guide language model reasoning and improve multi-step accuracy.

items.title: Time-Division Multiplexing: The Operational Rhythm and Temporal Organization Layer of Digital Life
items.description: Continual agents must handle urgent interaction while retaining alternatives, replaying errors, and committing safe long-term changes.
items.ai_summary: Time-Division Multiplexing framework introduces a temporal organization layer with phase-tagged micro-epochs and nested clocks to help continual agents balance urgent interactions, error replaying, and long-term changes.

items.title: The Behavioral Rate of Fine-Tuning: Compression as a Measure of Useful Information
items.description: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) adapts a frozen language model through a compact learned update, making it a natural setting for asking how much information fine-tuning needs to write.
items.ai_summary: This framework defines an operational behavioral rate to measure the minimum serialized size of a compressed LoRA adapter needed to preserve fine-tuning performance across different base models.

items.title: A trust layer for fast pedestal-stability surrogates: calibrated error bars, out-of-distribution alarms and few-shot recalibration
items.description: Machine-learning surrogates of linear peeling-ballooning stability now run in milliseconds, but they are mostly deployed as point estimators: they do not say how wrong they may be, or when a query lies outside what they were trained on.
items.ai_summary: A model-agnostic trust layer for linear peeling-ballooning stability surrogates provides conformal error bars, out-of-distribution alarms, and few-shot recalibration to improve reliability in fusion device design.

items.title: SpikePose: Lightweight Video Human Pose Estimation
items.description: Efficient video human pose estimation must balance localisation accuracy, motion quality, and energy cost. We present SpikePose, a lightweight video pose estimator that pairs a frame-reset, single-step spiking encoder with motion-aligned heatmap memory (MAM).
items.ai_summary: SpikePose is a lightweight video human pose estimator combining a single-step spiking encoder with motion-aligned heatmap memory to reduce arithmetic energy consumption by 91.4% compared to equivalent analog networks.

items.title: BudgetSplat: Budget-Controllable Generalizable Gaussian Splatting
items.description: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting enables efficient generalizable novel view synthesis, but existing pixel-aligned methods often generate highly redundant Gaussian primitives, causing the final representation size and rendering cost to grow rapidly with image resolution and…
items.ai_summary: BudgetSplat is a budget-controllable feed-forward framework that adapts 3D Gaussian Splatting representations to user-specified preservation ratios by jointly optimizing importance, spatial coverage, and cross-view redundancy.

items.title: Thermodynamics-Informed Learning Captures Hierarchical Hydrogen-Bond Networks in Deep Eutectic Solvents
items.description: Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) offer a tunable platform for lignocellulose refining, but their solvation behavior depends on multicomponent hydrogen-bond networks rather than individual constituent properties.
items.ai_summary: TiNN is a thermodynamics-informed neural network that hierarchically models hydrogen-bond networks and free-energy pathways to predict deep eutectic solvent solubility and accelerate solvent screening.

items.title: Signed, Sealed, Leaked: Trust Beyond Signature for MCP Toolchains
items.description: AI agents rely on third-party tools, such as Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, whose publishers can be authenticated and whose execution can be restricted by runtime security policies.
items.ai_summary: Germline execution runs Model Context Protocol tool invocations in ephemeral, data-free copies to bound potential information disclosure and prevent unauthorized data leaks from signed third-party tools.

items.title: Finite-width shift of the edge of chaos in deep neural networks
items.description: Deep neural networks train best when they are initialised at the edge of chaos, the critical line in the plane of weight and bias variances on which the distance between two inputs neither grows nor shrinks with depth.
items.ai_summary: This study derives the finite-width shift of the edge of chaos in deep neural networks using a random walk model, yielding a new initialization rule that places networks directly on their critical line.

items.title: Ask HN: What's your current AI agentic setup?
items.description: I'm curious how people on HN are using AI day to day, and came up with a list of questions I thought could be interesting to know. No need to answer every question of course, just wanted to get a gut feel how people are using AI.

items.title: One Scale, Four Texts: Gaps, Overlaps and Silent Repairs in Published Grading Schemes
items.description: Category systems often reach their users as text, and readers apply them with tacit repairs. We ask what such a text determines once the repairs are removed, using diabetic retinopathy grading, where one international scale circulates in several documents.
items.ai_summary: An analysis of four published diabetic retinopathy grading texts using an SMT solver and OWL reasoner reveals widespread gaps, category omissions, and conflicting clinical classifications across different guideline versions.

items.title: From Fixed Defaults to Calibrated Activation Policies for Long-Term Time-Series Forecasting
items.description: Long-term time-series forecasting supports decisions in energy, transportation, and other applications where reliable predictions are needed beyond the observed data.
items.ai_summary: A calibrated selection policy for long-term time-series forecasting learns from prior training runs to adapt activation functions and their locations to specific tasks, reducing mean squared error.

items.title: LungMend: A Healthy-Only Latent Diffusion Shape Prior for Lung Mask Correction in Severe Tuberculosis CT
items.description: Lung segmentation models such as R231 are widely used, but they fail on severe tuberculosis (TB) CT: cavities and consolidations look like non-lung tissue and are left out of the mask.
items.ai_summary: LungMend is a latent diffusion post-processing model that uses healthy anatomy to correct missing lung structures in severe tuberculosis CT masks. Keyword: LungMend.

items.title: RAGAM-AI: A Hybrid Reinforcement Learning based Agentic approach powered by Generative AI for Edge Resource Management
items.description: Resource management for distributed edge networks hosting different services has been handled efficiently using Reinforcement learning (RL). Reward generalization in complex workflows is still an open issue within the RL realm.
items.ai_summary: RAGAM-AI is a hybrid framework combining reinforcement learning and generative AI to optimize multi-access edge computing resource allocation and manage reward generalization.

items.title: Addition by Subtraction: Toward Mitigating Fragile Safety Alignment in Large Language Models
items.description: Large language models (LLMs) undergo safety alignment to prevent harmful generations, yet they remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks.
items.ai_summary: Addition by Subtraction is a fine-tuning method that removes safety-critical neurons and uses preference optimization to strengthen large language model safety alignment against jailbreaks.

items.title: Adapting Sleep Foundation Models for Dense Sleep Spindle Localization
items.description: Adapting sleep foundation models to dense electroencephalography (EEG) event localization is challenging because multi-second representations may not preserve sufficient temporal detail for precise boundary recovery.
items.ai_summary: Local sleep spindle localization method adapts a frozen SleepFM encoder with a local time-frequency pathway to preserve spectral content and sub-token temporal detail.

items.title: When Do Summaries Become Instructions? Unsupported Policy in LLM Agents' Self-Written Handoff Summaries
items.description: Long-running LLM agents compact their context, replacing most history with a summary.
items.ai_summary: Audit framework investigates how long-running large language model agents write self-generated handoff summaries containing unsupported policy restrictions and authorizations.

items.title: MKD2World: A Typed Spatial MarkDown World Model For Web Agents
items.description: Graphical user interface (GUI) agents can improve decision-making with world-model foresight, provided that predicted states accurately reflect post-action interfaces. Existing state representations fail to jointly capture interface layout, UI semantics, and explicit locations.
items.ai_summary: MKD2World is a spatial markdown world model for desktop web agents that serializes interface elements to predict post-action states and improve decision-making.

items.title: Using Experience Twice: Dynamic Process Rubrics for Privileged Token-Level Credit Assignment
items.description: Agent trajectories often contain both successful decisions and failed attempts, yet optimization with sparse trajectory-level rewards struggles to identify which critical decisions should be reinforced or suppressed.
items.ai_summary: Online Rubric Self-Distillation is a reinforcement learning method that derives natural-language process rubrics from trajectory differences to provide fine-grained token-level supervision.

items.title: EvoOPD: Evolving Privileged Information Strategies for Black-Box On-Policy Distillation
items.description: Proprietary language models exhibit strong reasoning and coding capabilities, but their output distributions are inaccessible, making fine-grained distillation methods that rely on teacher logits difficult to apply directly to black-box models.
items.ai_summary: EvoOPD is a black-box on-policy distillation method that adapts teacher feedback strategies to match a student model's evolving learning needs.

items.title: Spatially and Compositionally Controlled Multimodal Glioblastoma MRI Synthesis with Latent Diffusion
items.description: Glioblastoma exhibits substantial heterogeneity in tumour morphology and composition across MRI modalities, often making available clinical datasets highly unbalanced in terms of patient pathologies.
items.ai_summary: Two-stage latent diffusion model framework generates controllable 2D glioblastoma MRI scans and tumour segmentation maps conditioned on spatial location and composition.

items.title: From Admission to Retention: Predicting Durable Offspring in Quality-Diversity Search
items.description: Automated failure discovery can be framed as a diversity problem: the objective is to expose distinct ways a system fails rather than a single critical adversarial case.
items.ai_summary: Study on quality-diversity search evaluates pre-reproduction signals to predict durable offspring persistence versus temporary archive entry in automated failure discovery.

items.title: Deliberate Latent Reasoning for Sequential Recommendation
items.description: Sequential recommenders are widely applied in real-world scenarios to model user preferences and behavior patterns based on user interactions.
items.ai_summary: DESRec is a sequential recommendation framework that uses personalized latent reasoning and a self-distillation mechanism to improve user preference modeling and item ranking accuracy.

items.title: IDSISA: Influence-Distilled Sharded Training for Efficient Machine Unlearning
items.description: Machine unlearning removes the influence of specific training examples to comply with privacy regulations. Full retraining gives strong guarantees but is computationally prohibitive at scale; approximate methods are efficient but lack formal guarantees.
items.ai_summary: IDSISA is a machine unlearning method that uses influence functions and cross-shard distillation to remove training data influence while maintaining model utility and deletion guarantees.

items.title: EmoReward: Self-Evolving Reward Calibration for Emotional Video Generation RL
items.description: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) has advanced generative model post-training in verifiable domains such as code and mathematics, but evaluating video quality, especially emotional expression, often depends on subjective aesthetics and has no uniquely correct target.

items.title: Dialect Matters: A Dialect-Aware Baseline for Igala-English Machine Translation
items.description: The massive permeability of intelligent systems in every sphere of human activities have greatly enhanced clarity, ease of work, and increased general global understanding which has significantly awaken the use of intelligent systems by all users.
items.ai_summary: Researchers present a dialect-aware baseline for Igala-English machine translation that uses a new dataset to demonstrate that mixed-dialect training improves translation performance and fairness.

items.title: An Interaction-Aware Decision Framework for FDIC-Assisted Distressed Bank Acquisitions: Empirical Evidence from the FDIC Failed-Bank Panel and the SVB-First Citizens Case
items.description: Acquirers of failed banks weigh acquisition value, regulatory protection, risk, buyer strength, and execution difficulty jointly, because each signal's meaning depends on the others: high non-performing loans matter less when government loss sharing absorbs the losses.
items.ai_summary: The Spider Network Filtering Framework uses graph-inspired interaction rules to help evaluate and make decisions regarding the acquisition of distressed banks assisted by the FDIC.

items.title: Nowcasting Future Performance for Population Pruning in Survival-of-the-Fittest Training
items.description: Training high-performing neural networks often involves evaluating populations of candidate models with varying hyperparameters, architectures, or random seeds.
items.ai_summary: Researchers introduce a nowcasting method that uses intermediate training checkpoints to predict future model accuracy, enabling more efficient pruning of candidate models during training.

items.title: ElecLoad: Adaptive Electricity Load Forecasting Guided by Multiple Events
items.description: Accurate electricity load forecasting provides critical decision support for energy procurement, generation scheduling, and supply-demand balancing, contributing to the economic efficiency and operational reliability of power systems.
items.ai_summary: ElecLoad is a context-aware agent that analyzes multiple events to adaptively organize and refine electricity load forecasting by partitioning the forecast horizon into segments.

items.title: NaijaFacts: A Framework for Disentangling Language from Knowledge in Facts about Nigeria
items.description: Multilingual benchmarks for African languages mostly translate generic questions into local languages, measuring linguistic competence but not whether models know facts about Africa.
items.ai_summary: NaijaFacts is a benchmark for Nigerian factual and statistical questions that helps distinguish between a model's linguistic competence and its actual knowledge of African topics.

items.title: CRESiST: Self-Enhancing Explorative Policy Learning for Simultaneous Speech Translation
items.description: Simultaneous Speech Translation (SimulST) requires balancing translation quality and latency. While Large Language Models (LLMs) excel in offline translation, current LLM-based SimulST systems predominantly rely on prefix-incremental generation.
items.ai_summary: CRESiST is an end-to-end speech translation framework that uses an interleaved read-write architecture and an actor-critic policy to optimize quality and latency in streaming translation.

items.title: Tools Need Not Speak in Text: Latent Context Compression for Agents
items.description: Large language model (LLM) agents typically append raw tool outputs to their context. Over multi-step interactions, long and noisy observations incur substantial context overhead and dilute the agent's attention to task-relevant information.
items.ai_summary: Coca-Cola is a latent context compression model that reduces token consumption and runtime for LLM agents by compressing tool observations into decision-critical latent tokens.

items.title: Signed but Steerable: Measuring and Closing the Text-Vector Integrity Gap in Offline Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.description: Offline retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) on edge devices is updated through signed knowledge packs that carry text and precomputed embedding vectors. A signature proves who published a pack, not that its vectors encode its text. We study this text-vector integrity gap.
items.ai_summary: Researchers analyze the integrity gap in offline retrieval-augmented generation and propose a verification method for quantization codes to prevent attackers from manipulating retrieval results.

items.title: LibriSpeech-Real-QA: A Benchmark for Streaming Question Answering
items.description: Most speech large language models (SLMs) still process speech in an offline manner. They only start responding after they receive the complete speech segment.
items.ai_summary: LibriSpeech-Real-QA is a dataset and benchmark for evaluating how speech large language models perform real-time question answering on streaming audio inputs.

items.title: FPTR: Feasibility-Preserving Transactional Refinement for Deadline-Constrained Joint Beam and Resource Allocation
items.description: Short-interval wireless schedulers must return a complete, feasible beam-and-resource allocation before each execution deadline, and a late or invalid output gives no utility in the current control cycle.
items.ai_summary: FPTR is a refinement method for wireless schedulers that maintains a feasible beam-and-resource allocation while meeting strict execution deadlines for improved traffic performance.

items.title: Risk-Sensitive Non-Parametric and Kernel Bandits
items.description: We study non-parametric bandits in which arms are evaluated using Cumulative Prospect Theory (CPT) rather than expected reward.
items.ai_summary: Non-Parametric CPT Bandits is an optimistic algorithm for continuous action spaces that enables risk-sensitive decision-making without increasing the order of regret.

items.title: Model Merging Does Not Require Uniform LoRA Ranks
items.description: Model merging combines separately fine-tuned experts into a single model without retraining. Standard practice trains every expert at the same LoRA rank, which couples the rank choice across experts even though each domain has its own best rank.
items.ai_summary: Researchers demonstrate that model merging can achieve higher accuracy by assigning different LoRA ranks to experts based on their specific domain requirements.

items.title: Object-independent evaluation of small-data astronomical image classifiers: architecture, representation, and acquisition shortcuts
items.description: Reported performance in small astronomical image datasets can reflect object reuse, field-of-view differences, acquisition settings, and catalogue-derived properties as well as astronomical morphology.
items.ai_summary: A study of astronomical image classification shows that model performance is influenced by image context, acquisition settings, and catalogue-derived properties of physical objects.

items.title: What Does Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning Really Improve in LLM Agents?
items.description: While multi-turn agentic reinforcement learning (RL) excels on long-horizon tasks, its performance gains remain highly sensitive to interaction constraints.

items.title: ArcRAG: Agentic Compositional Retrieval over Knowledge Graphs
items.description: Graph-based retrieval-augmented generation (GraphRAG) answers questions by retrieving over a knowledge graph built from a corpus.
items.ai_summary: ArcRAG is a retrieval framework that enables effective multi-hop question answering over knowledge graphs without requiring co-design between retrieval and graph construction.

items.title: The Alignment Tax Is Graded: Task-Selective Capability Loss Under Length-Normalized DPO with SFT Retention
items.description: Setting. This is an empirical characterization study; we propose no new method and run no comparisons against alternative objectives.
items.ai_summary: A study on fine-tuning language models reveals that alignment training causes task-selective capability loss, with some tasks degrading significantly more than others.

items.title: A 3D foundation model unifying CT interpretation and segmentation
items.description: Radiologists interpret computed tomography (CT) scans by jointly determining what a finding represents and where it lies in three-dimensional (3D) anatomy.
items.ai_summary: HoloCT is a 3D foundation model that improves CT scan interpretation and lesion segmentation by jointly modeling clinical text and spatial anatomical data.

items.title: How many sorted projections determine n points in k dimensions?
items.description: Let $d_1,\dots,d_m$ be directions in $\mathbb{R}^k$, where $k\ge 2$. A multiset $X$ of $n$ points of $\mathbb{R}^k$ projects to the $m$ multisets of numbers $\{\{x\cdot d_j : x\in X\}\}$, or equivalently to the $m$ sorted lists of these numbers.
items.ai_summary: Researchers prove that a logarithmic number of sorted projections is sufficient to uniquely determine a set of points in higher-dimensional spaces.

items.title: Microdroplet Generator Surrogate Enhancement and Inverse Design Through an Uncertainty-Guided Framework
