items.title: From Autonomous Agents to Cognitive Symbionts: Toward AI-Augmented Human Intelligence
items.description: Physical AI should include AI-augmented human intelligence via lifelong cognitive symbionts that close cognitive gaps through sensing, context retention, and proactive assistance, requiring embedded governance.
items.ai_summary: Conceptual framework proposing cognitive symbionts as lifelong personal AI companions designed to augment human intelligence.

items.title: Aligning Language Models with General Preferences: An Empirical Study of Direct Nash Optimization
items.description: Direct Nash Optimization (DNO) aligns a language model to a general preference function by approximating the Nash equilibrium of a two-player preference game.
items.ai_summary: Direct Nash Optimization aligns language models with general preferences by approximating a Nash equilibrium through iterative on-chain sampling and contrastive updates.

items.title: PolicyIK: High-Precision Inverse Kinematics for Robot Arms with Reinforcement Learning
items.description: Inverse kinematics (IK) converts end-effector pose commands into joint motion, and many vision-language-action (VLA) policies rely on it to act on a given arm and to transfer across embodiments.
items.ai_summary: PolicyIK is a goal-conditioned reinforcement learning policy that provides high-precision inverse kinematics for robot arms to execute end-effector commands.

items.title: GUILD: Guided Iterative Data Collection for Imitation Learning
items.description: Imitation learning policies in robotics are trained on datasets collected through costly real-world teleoperation. Often, the data-collection process is unguided, relying on the teleoperator's intuition, resulting in data that contributes little to overall policy performance.
items.ai_summary: GUILD is a guided data collection method that uses vision-language models and predictive data attribution to iteratively curate high-quality datasets for imitation learning.

items.title: Visibility-Aware Reference Generation for Benchmarking Visual 3D Reconstruction in Vegetation-Rich Environments
items.description: Reliable evaluation of visual 3D reconstruction and depth estimation in vegetation-rich outdoor environments is limited by the scarcity of geometric ground-truth data and the cost of complete scanner surveys.
items.ai_summary: Visibility-Aware Reference Generation is a LiDAR-based pipeline that generates depth maps and visible reference point clouds to benchmark 3D reconstruction in vegetation-rich environments.

items.title: GSCV++: Lightweight 3D Gaussian Splatting Sequence Compression via Standard Video Codecs
items.description: This paper presents GSCV++, a lightweight pipeline for 3D {G}aussian {S}platting (GS) sequences {C}ompression with standard {V}ideo codecs.
items.ai_summary: GSCV++ is a lightweight pipeline for compressing 3D Gaussian Splatting sequences using standard video codecs by improving preprocessing, mapping, and compression configurations.

items.title: Suppressing Misaligned Behaviors in Language Models, Durably
items.description: Undesired model behaviors can emerge or re-emerge at any stage of training. Once observed, how effectively can we suppress them?
items.ai_summary: Prefix-Expanded Adversarial Reinforcement Learning is a reinforcement learning variant that suppresses misaligned language model behaviors by augmenting rollouts with intermediate states.

items.title: Reading Why: Born-Measured Attention with Exact Word Evidence on Light and Qubits
items.description: When a language model answers, we can usually only estimate why. We build a transformer in which every step is a Born measurement - attention $|\langle q|k\rangle|^4$ normalised over each row, a measured product in place of the feed-forward nonlinearity, and a Born readout.
items.ai_summary: Born-Measured Attention is a transformer architecture that replaces standard attention and nonlinearities with Born measurements to compute exact word evidence and class probabilities.

items.title: OpenBrain: An Auditable Generated-Label Release for Whole-Brain MRI Parcellation
items.description: Automatic tools can now generate whole-brain MRI parcellations at cohort scale, but generated-label releases often provide little evidence about which cases are reliable enough to reuse.
items.ai_summary: OpenBrain is a confidence-aware release of whole-brain MRI parcellations that provides auditable case records and a reference-free reliability panel for quality filtering.

items.title: Agnostic Learning by Imitating
items.description: Given a class of machine learning models and sample access to a data distribution with binary labels, which computational task is harder: training a discriminative model that distinguishes positive and negative labels as well as the best member of the class, or training a…
items.ai_summary: Researchers prove that training a discriminative classification model and training an indistinguishable generative model are computationally equivalent tasks in learning theory.

items.title: Adversarial Speculative Reasoning Improves Long Horizon Agents
items.description: Speculative decoding can be trained to reject critical reasoning tokens so they are verified by the target model, reducing numerical noise and improving long-horizon agent accuracy without altering the target model.
items.ai_summary: Adversarial Speculative Reasoning trains draft models to be rejected at critical decision points to improve the long-horizon reasoning and coding accuracy of large language model agents.

items.title: A Circuit for In-Context Learning
items.description: In-context learning (ICL) lets a pretrained language model perform a task specified by demonstrations in its prompt, with no parameter updates. With arbitrary labels the model must acquire a mapping it cannot have memorized, so the learning happens within a single forward pass.
items.ai_summary: Researchers map the internal computational circuit that enables transformers to perform few-shot in-context learning with arbitrary labels in a single forward pass.

items.title: Weight-space programming for auditing clinical decision networks
items.description: Machine learning models in radiotherapy are commissioned by testing them on cases with known answers, which may not reveal a shortcut that the test cases share with the training data.
items.ai_summary: Study demonstrates that a frontier language model can successfully audit and repair clinical neural networks by directly analyzing and modifying their raw weights.

items.title: MedPhysBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Language Models on Medical Physics Calculations and Error Detection
items.description: Medical physicists turn a prescription into a delivered dose and check one another's calculations, because one error in a beam calibration or a monitor-unit (MU) calculation can affect every patient treated with it.
items.ai_summary: MedPhysBench is a new benchmark featuring calculation generators and error detection tasks to evaluate language models on medical physics workflows.

items.title: A simple adaptive accelerated optimistic dual averaging method for unconstrained convex optimization in $p$-norm geometry
items.description: Efficient preconditioning plays an important role in large-scale first-order optimization.
items.ai_summary: Researchers propose an adaptive accelerated optimistic dual averaging method for unconstrained convex optimization that uses low-cost p-norm geometry preconditioning.

items.title: CATF: A Manager-Worker Framework for Context-Aware Time-Series Forecasting
items.description: We study context-aware time-series forecasting, in which a single target variable is predicted from its own history and a set of contextual variables, such as weather and calendar information.
items.ai_summary: CATF is a manager-worker framework for context-aware time-series forecasting that uses a Transformer manager to hard-route inputs to specialized worker models.

items.title: PyRUA-DataFarm: LLM Agent as a Cost-Efficient Teleoperator for Real-Ready Robot Data
items.description: A coding agent automates robot demonstration generation by simulating tasks, rendering photorealistic videos, and producing deployable training data at lower cost than teleoperation.
items.ai_summary: PyRUA-DataFarm uses a coding agent and simulation to generate synchronized, real-ready robot demonstration data at a low cost without requiring physical teleoperation.

items.title: HARP: Training-Free Dual-Profile Agentic Communication for LLM-Based Recommendation
items.description: In LLM-based recommendation, memory acts as a user-level agent in a memory-augmented backbone. Yet users and items remain asymmetric: only the user is given a structured profile; it enters a bandwidth-limited reranker prompt; and it is frozen after warmup.
items.ai_summary: HARP is a training-free agentic communication framework for LLM-based recommenders that uses symmetric item profiles and retrieval-time homophily to improve recommendation performance.

items.title: MDSKILL: Learning to Internalize Skill Memory through Multi-View Distillation for Efficient Dynamic Agent Self-Evolution
items.description: Skill memories encode past experiences as textual prompts to improve reinforcement learning (RL) for self-evolving agents.
items.ai_summary: MDSKILL is a multi-view distillation approach that organizes skill memories into functional views to improve agent self-evolution and reinforcement learning.

items.title: $Φ$asmaNet: A Staged Spectral Token-Refinement Architecture for Fast Gravitational-Wave Signal-to-Noise Ratio Prediction
items.description: Quantifying selection effects in gravitational-wave population studies requires millions of costly signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) calculations.
items.ai_summary: PhiasmaNet is a compact neural architecture that uses staged spectral token refinement to predict gravitational-wave signal-to-noise ratios orders of magnitude faster than conventional methods.

items.title: You don't need long context
items.description: Frequent context compaction preserves task accuracy across long-horizon and long-input tasks, suggesting that long-context language models may be unnecessary and motivating semantic state space models.
items.ai_summary: Study demonstrates that language models can maintain high task accuracy on long-horizon and long-input tasks by using frequent context compaction instead of relying on long-context windows.

items.title: LoopVQ: Sub 1-bit KV Cache Quantization for Looped Transformers
items.description: Looped transformers are a parameter-efficient alternative to standard transformers for language modeling. By reapplying the same layers across multiple loop steps, recent looped language models match the performance of non-looped models several times their size.
items.ai_summary: LoopVQ is a KV cache vector quantization method for looped transformers that jointly codes channels of multiple loop steps to reduce decode latency and memory bottlenecks.

items.title: How I use AI (Oct 2026)
items.description: Trending on Hacker News from ben.stolovitz.com. 131 points and 112 comments.

items.title: Universal Hardness From Masking Channels
items.description: We prove a broad learning-theoretic generalization of the celebrated hardcore lemma concerning the average-case complexity of computing a Boolean function (Impagliazzo, 1995).
items.ai_summary: Masking channels-based universal hardcore lemma framework certifies the hardness of learning non-Boolean functions by choosing the right fidelity via convex duality.

items.title: GSBR: Geometric Support Behavior Regularization for Online RL
items.description: Regularizing online reinforcement learning (RL) toward a pretrained base policy can improve sample efficiency and learning stability, but regularization that is too restrictive limits how much the policy can improve.
items.ai_summary: Geometric Support Behavior Regularization penalizes actions by their distance from a base policy's support to improve online reinforcement learning success rates and throughput in robotics.

items.title: Wonder 4: A Mixture-of-Experts Recipe for Image Quality Enhancement
items.description: A real photograph is often blurry, grainy, compressed, scratched, and low-resolution at the same time. Each defect has its own severity and its own place in the image. The corrections for these defects conflict with each other.
items.ai_summary: Wonder 4 is a mixture-of-experts image quality enhancement model that corrects multiple simultaneous photograph defects in specific regions without using degradation classifiers or extra modules.

items.title: Personas Are Not People: Identity as State, Not Attribute
items.description: Synthetic populations, large sets of simulated people, are increasingly used in place of real people to pretest surveys, simulate users and communities, and evaluate AI systems.
items.ai_summary: Identity-as-state analysis proves that fixed-persona language model simulations cannot reproduce context-specific human behavior, and proposes a new evaluation criterion.

items.title: Low-Density 3D Point Cloud Classification
items.description: 3D point cloud classification, a task in computer vision, has recently gained substantial interest due to its extensive applications across various domains such as augmented and virtual reality, robotics, and autonomous driving.
items.ai_summary: LD-PointNet++ is an optimized architecture for classifying low-density 3D point clouds, maintaining consistent high accuracy across varying density levels.

items.title: False Reassurance in LLM Severe-Weather Guidance: A Replayable Evaluation Against Real NWS Alerts
items.description: An LLM assistant that cannot see official severe-weather alerts may tell users that conditions are calm while a warning is active. We call this false reassurance and measure it by replaying 117 frozen cases built from real U.S.
items.ai_summary: Replayable evaluation against real National Weather Service alerts measures false reassurance in LLM severe-weather guidance and demonstrates the effectiveness of real alert access.

items.title: Knowingly Wrong: Training LLMs Against Their Own Beliefs can Induce Misalignment
items.description: Fine-tuning a large language model (LLM) on harmful data in a narrow domain, such as bad medical advice, can make it broadly misaligned. How realistic this risk is remains unclear, since models are very rarely fine-tuned on explicitly harmful data in practice.
items.ai_summary: Fine-tuning language models on data they believe to be false can induce broad internal inconsistency and misalignment across tasks without significant loss of general capability.

items.title: Anchored Rank-Adversarial Fine-Tuning Pretrained Visual Place Recognition Models
items.description: Visual place recognition (VPR) localises a camera by retrieving similar geo-tagged images, and current foundation-model VPR models are accurate across cities, seasons and illumination, but not robust to adversarial perturbations: under a white-box attack on the ranking at an…
items.ai_summary: Anchored rank-adversarial fine-tuning (ARAFT) improves the adversarial robustness of visual place recognition foundation models while preserving clean accuracy.

items.title: YANAMI: A Large-Scale Multimodal Dataset and Benchmark for Multiturn Stateful Interaction
items.description: YANAMI introduces a large-scale multimodal dialogue dataset and benchmark for stateful interaction, requiring models to track and realize evolving dialogue states across turns, and reveals that current unified multimodal models still struggle with this task.

items.title: Möbius: A Unified Motion-Language Model Bridging Understanding and Generation
items.description: We aim to build a truly unified motion model that can understand, generate, and edit human motion within a single framework.
items.ai_summary: Mobius is a unified motion-language model that operates directly on continuous frame-level raw motion to support motion understanding, generation, and editing within a single framework.

items.title: Beyond Accuracy: What Language-Subspace Interventions Capture, Remove, and Improve
items.description: Language-subspace interventions aim to improve multilingual reasoning by suppressing language-related components in mid-layer activations.
items.ai_summary: Language-subspace interventions aim to improve multilingual reasoning by suppressing language-related components in mid-layer activations, but evaluation shows they rarely improve joint accuracy without damaging response-language fidelity.

items.title: Conformal Prediction at Performative Equilibrium: The Price of Performativity
items.description: Conformal prediction gives finite-sample coverage when calibration and test points are exchangeable, but exchangeability can fail when deployment changes the data distribution.
items.ai_summary: Conformal prediction in performative settings establishes a phase transition at sensitivity L=1, proving that finite-sample procedures cannot guarantee equilibrium-valid coverage when L is greater than or equal to 1.

items.title: De Rham cohomological architectures for PINNs and PDEs with topological holes
items.description: We attempt to alleviate failure modes of classical physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) in scenarios of topological pathologies corresponding to punctures, holes, poles, and voids by introducing de Rham cohomological augmentations, or Hodge-de Rham PINNs.
items.ai_summary: Hodge-de Rham PINNs introduce de Rham cohomological augmentations using the Hodge-Morrey-Friedrichs decomposition to solve physics-informed neural network failures in scenarios with topological holes.

items.title: Route Anything: A Study of Model and Policy Routing for General-Purpose AI Systems
items.description: Route Anything is a framework for dynamically selecting and coordinating specialized AI models and policies across diverse tasks to improve performance and efficiency.

items.title: The Geometry of Ignorance: Detecting Suppressed Knowledge in LLMs through Activation Fragmentation
items.description: Evaluating whether a large language model (LLM) genuinely knows a concept remains a fundamental problem, since behavioral metrics can be fooled by suppression: a model that refuses to answer may still harbor recoverable knowledge.
items.ai_summary: Activation fragmentation measures the geometric coherence of hidden-state differences between concept queries and paraphrases to detect suppressed parametric knowledge in large language models without using attacks.

items.title: iGC: Antibody Optimization via Reinforcement Learning over a Learned Somatic Hypermutation Prior
items.description: Antibody affinity maturation is a natural optimization process in which B cells acquire mutations through somatic hypermutation (SHM), undergo selection for improved antigen binding, and iteratively evolve toward higher affinity.
items.ai_summary: iGC is a two-stage reinforcement learning framework that models somatic hypermutation priors and optimizes antigen binding to improve computational antibody affinity maturation.

items.title: Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
items.description: Naive on-policy RL is often bottlenecked by the capabilities of the base model --- insufficient coverage can result in an inability to learn from certain rewards. At the same time, rewards in modern post-training systems often come from rich textual sources, e.g.
items.ai_summary: Targeted guidance combines on-policy self-distillation with per-criteria reinforcement learning to improve hard-to-optimize agentic behaviors using per-turn textual feedback.

items.title: Gaussian Partitioning for Reliable Learning of Multi-Index Models
items.description: We introduce Gaussian partitioning, an algorithmic primitive for distributions smooth with respect to a Gaussian. It partitions space into polyhedral regions so that almost all mass lies in thin strips restricting a few orthogonal directions.
items.ai_summary: Gaussian partitioning is an algorithmic primitive that divides space into polyhedral regions to efficiently agnostically learn complex Boolean multi-index models under smooth input marginals.

items.title: JHiMA-WebRL: A Joint Hierarchical Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Long-Horizon Web Tasks
items.description: Multimodal web agents have shown promising capabilities for interacting with websites through graphical user interfaces (GUIs), yet realistic web tasks often require long-horizon, multi-step planning that remains challenging for monolithic policies.
items.ai_summary: JHiMA-WebRL is a joint hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning framework that couples a task decomposer and an actor to improve long-horizon web navigation tasks.

items.title: NovoCRF: Globally Normalized De Novo Peptide Sequencing on a Prefix-Mass Lattice
items.description: De novo peptide sequencing has moved from dynamic programming over hand-designed or generative scores to large transformers that learn the task end to end.
items.ai_summary: NovoCRF is a conditional random field model for de novo peptide sequencing that uses exact global normalization over mass-feasible peptides on a prefix-mass lattice.

items.title: Going Deeper With Memories
items.description: DeepMem is a causal multiscale byte-level architecture that uses invertible subband transforms and fast weight memory to compress sequences for efficient reasoning while preserving exact byte identity via lossless carriers and attention-based super-resolution decoding.
items.ai_summary: DeepMem is a causal multiscale byte-level language model architecture that separates semantic compression from exact byte preservation to reduce computational costs while maintaining strong performance.

items.title: Logarithmic Regret for Alternating Mirror Descent
items.description: Alternating online mirror descent (AltOMD) is a simple learning rule for zero-sum games, which improves upon simultaneous OMD numerically and theoretically.
items.ai_summary: Alternating online mirror descent achieves an O(log(T)) regret bound for two-player zero-sum bilinear games, resolving an open question in learning theory.

items.title: Shrinkage prior for implicit generative models
items.description: Implicit generative models based on deep neural networks have revolutionized many scientific fields, from weather research to language generation. They successfully model complex random objects arising in real-world problems.
items.ai_summary: A sample-efficient training mechanism uses shrinkage priors and generalized Bayes inference to improve parameter estimation in implicit generative models.

items.title: Post-stratified importance sampling
items.description: Importance sampling is a building block of modern statistical computing, but the weighted estimate is prone to high or infinite variance. Moreover, its empirical standard error is often unreliable, leaving importance sampling without practical uncertainty quantification.
items.ai_summary: Post-stratified importance sampling reformulates high-dimensional weighting into one-dimensional probabilistic models to improve estimation accuracy and uncertainty quantification.

items.title: ARLoop: Fully-Open Pre-trained Looped Transformers with Attention Residuals
items.description: Looped transformers increase effective depth by repeatedly applying a shared set of transformer layers, offering a parameter-efficient way to scale computation.
items.ai_summary: ARLoop is a looped transformer architecture that uses attention residuals to improve performance and parameter efficiency in large language model pretraining.

items.title: Diagnosis by Composition: Detecting and Localizing Unseen Diseases by Composing Learned Radiological Findings
items.description: Deep models for radiological diagnosis are typically trained to predict disease labels directly from images, which limits them to diseases seen during training and makes their decisions hard to interpret in radiologists' terms.
items.ai_summary: Diagnosis by composition is an interpretable radiological framework that detects and localizes unseen diseases by combining learned finding maps according to clinical guidelines.

items.title: Regret-based Characterization, Information Limits, and the Sample Complexity of Auditing Adaptive Policies
items.description: A policy can earn its performance by where it locates on average or by reacting to information. For any Markov policy $π$ in a finite-horizon MDP, let $ν$ be its open-loop marginal, which plays $π$'s average action distribution at each step.
items.ai_summary: A new method characterizes the adaptivity gap and sample complexity of auditing Markov policies in finite-horizon MDPs using information-theoretic bounds.

items.title: Post-Inference Model Chaining: A Problem Statement and a Model-based Bootstrap for Training End-to-End Digital Twins
items.description: End-to-end digital twins can be constructed by fitting separate stage models and connecting them after inference.
items.ai_summary: A model-based bootstrap technique reduces relative mean bias and improves coverage when training end-to-end digital twins through post-inference model chaining.

items.title: Learning curves in natural and artificial systems
items.description: A general mathematical model of experience formation is considered, in which the learning level is defined as the probability that the next value of the uncertainty factor has already been mastered and not forgotten.
items.ai_summary: A mathematical model of experience formation derives how situation occurrence distributions shape learning curves in both natural and artificial systems.

items.title: PLANTEUR: A Crop-Type Segmentation Benchmark for Tropical Regions
items.description: We introduce PLANTEUR, a benchmark for crop-type mapping from satellite images in the French overseas territories.
items.ai_summary: Planteur is an open-source crop-type segmentation benchmark featuring multi-sensor satellite image sequences across multiple tropical regions for cross-territory evaluation.

items.title: Fairness Metrics based on the AUC in Clinical Predictive AI
items.description: Fairness evaluation of clinical prediction models for binary outcomes often involves fairness metrics that compare the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC, or c-statistic) across subgroups.
items.ai_summary: An evaluation of AUC-based fairness metrics in clinical prediction models highlights limitations from non-collapsibility and recommends reporting a comprehensive AUC matrix.

items.title: Fusing Earth observation embeddings and spaceborne terrain with meteorological forcing for flood peak depth prediction from high-water marks
items.description: Flood peak depth on normally dry land governs damage and risk to life, but is observed only sparsely, by post-event high-water mark (HWM) surveys, and depth derived from satellite flood extent is produced after the event and inherits the vertical error of the digital elevation…
items.ai_summary: A cross-modal fusion network uses spaceborne terrain, foundation model embeddings, and meteorological forcing to predict flood peak depths from field observations 6 hours ahead of the peak.

items.title: Physics-informed traditional and generative Mori-Zwanzig-reduced models for multiscale systems
items.description: Model reduction via the Mori-Zwanzig (MZ) formalism is well understood for coarse-grained representations constructed from standard basis functions such as Fourier functions.
items.ai_summary: A reduced-order modeling framework uses bases discovered by physics-informed machine learning and the Mori-Zwanzig formalism with fluctuation-dissipation and generative closures to improve predictions of multiscale systems.

items.title: Privacy for Free in Efficient Agnostic Halfspace Learning
items.description: We provide the first computationally efficient, differentially private algorithms for agnostically learning halfspaces.
items.ai_summary: Computationally efficient, differentially private algorithms for agnostically learning halfspaces match non-private sample complexity across three distinct learning settings.

items.title: Multi-Objective Generative Optimization via Expected Hypervolume Fine-Tuning
items.description: Scientific discovery requires plausible designs spanning useful trade-offs among competing properties: a molecule with strong binding affinity, for example, may be difficult to synthesize.
items.ai_summary: Hypervolume Fine-Tuning adapts a pretrained generative model to maximize the expected hypervolume of its samples, jointly improving candidate quality and trade-off coverage for scientific design tasks.

items.title: Diffusion Plug-in Priors for Self-Supervised Ultrasound Video Restoration
items.description: \textit{Objective:} Ultrasound videos are limited by hardware-constrained spatial resolution and signal-dependent speckle, while paired low- and high-resolution acquisitions for supervised restoration are rarely available.
items.ai_summary: UltraDiff uses a frozen pretrained diffusion model as a plug-in prior alongside a speckle-aware data fidelity term to jointly super-resolve and despeckle ultrasound videos without paired training data.

items.title: TAQ-MOTR: Tracking-Aware Detection Query Formation for End-to-End Multiple Object Tracking
items.description: Tracking-by-propagation (TBP) methods perform end-to-end multi-object tracking by propagating track queries across frames, jointly handling detection and identity association without heuristic post-processing while naturally modeling temporal information.
items.ai_summary: TAQ-MOTR uses a pre-decoder hybrid query generator that conditions detection queries on trajectory states to discover untracked objects and provide complementary evidence for occluded objects in multi-object tracking.

items.title: Empirical Bayes Flow Matching for Continuous Cryo-EM Heterogeneity
items.description: We address the problem of learning generative priors over high-dimensional latent variables from indirect, noisy observations, with a focus on continuous heterogeneity in cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM).
items.ai_summary: Empirical Bayes Flow Matching uses a Monte Carlo stochastic approximation Expectation-Maximization framework to learn generative priors directly from indirect observations, enabling continuous heterogeneity recovery in cryo-electron microscopy.

items.title: Robust Reconstruction of Power Lines from Incomplete Mobile and Aerial LiDAR Data
items.description: Accurate vegetation-encroachment assessment and risk mitigation require electric utilities to accurately locate and characterize distribution-network assets, including poles and power lines, and distinguish among medium-voltage, low-voltage, neutral, and telecommunication lines.
items.ai_summary: An automated reconstruction method combining scaled density-based clustering, robust polynomial fitting, and iterative fragment merging recovers individual power lines from incomplete mobile and aerial LiDAR data.

items.title: Ensembles of Random Partition-Based Models under Covariate Shift
items.description: Distribution shifts, including covariate shifts, are ubiquitous in real-world applications of machine learning.
items.ai_summary: New discrepancy measures of covariate shift severity extend the risk theory of partition-based kernel estimators to ensembles, showing that larger ensemble sizes achieve minimax-optimal risk convergence rates under severe covariate shifts.

items.title: Factorized MLLM Embeddings for Composed Image Retrieval
items.description: FactEmbed improves composed image retrieval by decoupling query understanding from embedding construction through factorized latents that simulate visual modifications before retrieval.
items.ai_summary: FactEmbed decouples compositional query comprehension in composed image retrieval by using factorized latents to simulate intended visual modifications through an intermediate target imagination objective.

items.title: From Natural Images to Medical Scans: Transferability of Diffusion Models for Medical Image Generation
items.description: Transfer learning from natural images is standard in supervised and increasingly adopted in self-supervised medical image analysis, but its role in generative modelling, and in particular diffusion denoisers, remains underexplored.
items.ai_summary: Transfer learning from natural images using diffusion denoisers consistently improves medical image generation fidelity by leveraging shared spatial structures across domains.

items.title: Stepsize modulation for cross entropy from local quadratic optimization
items.description: Two methods are presented that perturb a given learning rate schedule in stochastic gradient descent with cross entropy loss. Both methods use an extra forward pass to estimate various derivatives of the minibatch loss.
items.ai_summary: Two stepsize modulation methods perturb stochastic gradient descent schedules using local quadratic optimization to reduce cross-entropy loss faster and increase training monotonicity.

items.title: Provably Learning Mixtures of Linear Experts
items.description: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models are widely deployed in modern machine learning. However, few convergence guarantees exist for gradient-based training of MoEs: the objective is nonconvex, and even simple mixtures trap first-order methods in spurious local optima.
items.ai_summary: A novel global convergence guarantee for gradient EM training of mixture-of-expert models demonstrates that random initialization and polynomial iterations can successfully train these networks.

items.title: What Does the Model See? Representation Validity in Multimodal LLM-Based Video Analysis
items.description: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) allow social scientists to analyze video at scale, but researchers must decide which parts of a video to provide as input.
items.ai_summary: Evaluating multimodal large language models on video analysis tasks reveals that input representation validity varies significantly by construct and requires empirical validation.

items.title: OperAItor: An Agentic Framework for Fault-Tolerant Operation of Chemical Processes
items.description: OperAItor, an open-source framework for developing and evaluating large language model agents for supervisory fault management in chemical processes.
items.ai_summary: OperAItor is an open-source agentic framework that integrates process monitoring and safety checks to provide fault-tolerant supervisory control for chemical processes.

items.title: PadLoc: Training-Free Floor-Plan Localization by Sparse Geometric Matching
items.description: We propose PadLoc, a training-free localization back-end that places a moving sensor within a known floor plan.
items.ai_summary: PadLoc is a training-free floor-plan localization back-end that uses sparse geometric matching and Bayes filtering to accurately place moving sensors within known maps.

items.title: AgentAM: An AI Agent for Spatter- and Defect-Aware Process Optimization in Laser Powder Bed Fusion
items.description: Predictive models for laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) are rarely used on the shop floor because querying them requires programming and model-specific knowledge.
items.ai_summary: AgentAM is a large language model agent that provides natural-language access to predictive simulations for defect-aware process optimization in laser powder bed fusion.

items.title: Learning Behaviorally Relevant Dynamics in Multimodal Neural Recordings
items.description: Multimodal neural data can enable a more complete understanding of brain dynamics underlying behavior.
items.ai_summary: BREM-NET is a nonlinear multimodal dynamical model that fuses disparate neural recordings with behavioral data to accurately separate behaviorally relevant brain dynamics.

items.title: When Self-Verification Hurts: Calibrated Answer Repair for Financial Question Answering
items.description: Financial question answering can fail even when a model extracts a plausible number from the supplied evidence: the answer may attach it to the wrong entity, period, unit, or accounting concept.
items.ai_summary: Calibrated Answer Repair is a targeted financial question-answering method that balances evidence verification and bounded editing to improve accuracy while lowering token costs.

items.title: Basin2Vec: Learning Basin-Centric Embeddings for Scalable Hydrological Modeling
items.description: Reliable streamflow prediction across time and in ungauged basins requires representations that capture hydrologically relevant basin characteristics.
items.ai_summary: Basin2Vec is a self-supervised framework that learns compact basin-centric embeddings from hydroclimatic data to improve streamflow prediction in ungauged regions.

items.title: RoboTryOn: Synthesizing Dexterous Robot Demonstrations from Human Videos via Virtual Try-On
items.description: RoboTryOn translates human demonstration videos into robot videos to train control policies without real robot demonstrations, improving success rates and reducing data collection costs.
items.ai_summary: RoboTryOn converts human demonstration videos into target robot videos using virtual try-on techniques, improving policy learning success rates on novel manipulation tasks without real robot demonstrations.

items.title: Perturb, Repair, Verify: Self-Play Vision-Language Verifiers for Compositional Understanding
items.description: Vision-language verifiers judge whether an image faithfully matches a textual description, yet existing training pipelines typically rely on static supervision from stronger external judges or curated hard-negative data.
items.ai_summary: PROVE is a self-play framework that trains vision-language verifiers through a perturb-verify-repair loop using a shared multimodal backbone to improve compositional understanding and visual-detail robustness.

items.title: Macrocanonical Generator Networks: Data-Efficient Neural Surrogates for Amortized Physics Simulation
items.description: Many scientific simulations are computationally expensive, limiting their use in simulation-based inference, uncertainty quantification, and decision making.
items.ai_summary: Macrocanonical generator networks use neural surrogates to match multiscale statistics of stationary physical processes, generating new realizations significantly faster than traditional simulations while preserving realistic fluctuations.

items.title: Asynchronous Robot Policies
items.description: Scaling vision-language foundation models has significantly advanced generalist robot manipulation, but the increased model scale introduces computational latency that degrades real-time physical reactivity.
items.ai_summary: Asynchronous Robot Policy decouples semantic reasoning from low-level action generation using asynchronous processes, enabling real-time robot reactivity and higher success rates in manipulation tasks.

items.title: Catalyzing Interactive HTML Generation Capabilities via High-Fidelity Reinforcement Learning
items.description: Generating HTML from natural-language specifications is an important application of code large language models (LLMs). Despite producing renderable pages, current models often fail to ensure functionality and visual quality during actual interaction.
items.ai_summary: WebCatalyst is a browser-interaction reinforcement learning framework that uses a game-level GUI assessor, visual anchor, and action-trace credit to improve interactive HTML generation capabilities.

items.title: Creating Power Flexibility in Datacenters via Query Routing
items.description: The growing energy requirements of large language model inference highlight the need for datacenters to support safe grid operation by providing power demand flexibility, while maintaining service for interactive workloads.
items.ai_summary: Dynamic query routing across language model instances provides datacenter power demand flexibility up to 16% of total consumption while maintaining service for interactive workloads.

items.title: GM League Arena: An Interactive Long-Horizon Task Benchmark Based on Professional Sports League Management
items.description: Long-horizon decision-making under sustained competition requires large language models (LLMs) to balance immediate investment with future resource needs.
items.ai_summary: GM Bench evaluates the long-horizon decision-making and management capabilities of large language models by tasking them with managing professional sports teams across multiple seasons under resource constraints.

items.title: When Cell Crops Share a Parent: Measuring and Isolating Acquisition Leakage in Cervical Cytology Benchmarks
items.description: Public cervical cytology benchmarks release many cell crops cut from far fewer microscope fields or slides and are often split at the crop level, so test cells share acquisition parents with training cells.
items.ai_summary: Crop-level splitting in cervical cytology benchmarks artificially inflates accuracy due to shared acquisition parents, demonstrating that parent-disjoint splits are necessary for accurate evaluation.

items.title: Beyond Foundation Models: PFN Priors Improve Tabular Hyperparameter Optimization
items.description: Synthetic priors have so far served one purpose: pretraining tabular foundation models. We ask whether the same priors can improve conventional tabular models, which are trained from scratch on each dataset.
items.ai_summary: PriorTune meta-tunes hyperparameter configurations on synthetic tasks derived from prior data, improving the performance of conventional tabular models without extra inference cost.

items.title: Meta$^2$: Precomputing Reusable Knowledge for Online Harness Evolution in Long-Horizon Agents
items.description: Harness optimization improves long-horizon agents by refining the prompts, tools, memory, and hooks around a frozen model.
items.ai_summary: Meta2 learns reusable textual meta-skills offline to guide online harness evolution for long-horizon agents, enabling adaptive prompting and tool use during task execution.

items.title: A Random Matrix Analysis of Symmetric Tensor Unfolding
items.description: We study a fundamental problem in machine learning: partial recovery of a planted signal $\boldsymbol{v} \in \mathbb{S}^{n-1}$ from a spiked tensor $\boldsymbol{\mathsf{X}} = λ\, \boldsymbol{v}^{\otimes p} + \boldsymbol{\mathsf{Z}}$, where $\boldsymbol{\mathsf{Z}}$ has…
items.ai_summary: Random matrix theory analysis of symmetric tensor unfolding reveals a sharp phase transition for partial recovery and shows that unfolded symmetric tensors spectrally behave like standard Wigner matrices.

items.title: From Opinions to Commitments: Unstable Assignments and Silent Choices in AI-Mediated Proposals
items.description: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being used to turn citizens' opinions into collective proposals. These proposals can make assignments: who should act, what must be done, how much one should spend and by when.
items.ai_summary: An empirical evaluation of four large language models acting as mediators demonstrates that prompt variations and reordering frequently produce unstable collective proposals with hidden assignments and excluded views.

items.title: PAC Learning with Multiple Correct Answers
items.description: We study PAC learning when each example comes with a set of at most $\ell$ correct labels and a prediction is correct if it belongs to this set.
items.ai_summary: A theoretical study of PAC learning with multiple correct answers proves that demonstrations are significantly harder than full label sets or bandit feedback, establishing precise sample complexity bounds and learnability conditions.

items.title: High-fidelity training-free photovoltaic module mapping from multi-view UAV imagery
items.description: High-fidelity photovoltaic (PV) module mapping requires complete instance recovery and accurate delineation.
items.ai_summary: Multi-View PV Module Mapper is a training-free framework that couples vision foundation models with UAV photogrammetry to automatically generate high-fidelity, geometrically accurate maps of individual photovoltaic modules.

items.title: Solving the Nonlinear Westervelt Equation in Ultrasound Propagation Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks
items.description: Modeling the nonlinear acoustic wave propagation in biological tissues needs accuracy, especially in ultrasound imaging and therapeutic applications.
items.ai_summary: Physics-Informed Neural Networks utilizing a sinusoidal activation function successfully solve the nonlinear 1D Westervelt equation for ultrasound propagation across linear, shock-dominated, and dissipation-dominated scenarios.

items.title: Do Ray-Traced Cities Make a Better Channel Prior for an Unseen Site? A Pre-Registered Study in Simulation, and a Test on Measured Channels that Reverses It
items.description: Channel estimators at a newly deployed base station usually start from 3GPP stochastic channel models, which describe no particular street.
items.ai_summary: A pre-registered study comparing ray-traced city channel priors with stochastic models finds that simulated channels overestimate performance, while measured environments show traditional 3GPP models often outperform ray-traced priors.

items.title: The Right Source Is Not Enough: Understanding History Interference in Speech-LLM Memory
items.description: Speech large language models retain audio history to support multi-turn conversations. Yet remembering an event does not ensure that its information is used only when relevant.
items.ai_summary: Controlled experiments on speech large language models reveal that irrelevant historical audio causes errors by directing computations toward competing answers, demonstrating that source-role identification alone does not prevent history interference.

items.title: Towards an Optimal Control Foundation of Early Exits - Turnpikes and ResNets
items.description: The feed-forward propagation through neural networks is crucial for training and inference.
items.ai_summary: An optimal control analysis of ResNets proves that jointly optimizing loss functions for output and intermediate layers induces the turnpike phenomenon, bounding the required layer depth independently of overall network depth.

items.title: Distributed Linear Bandits for Freshness-Aware Preprocessing in MEC-Enabled Digital Twin Networks
items.description: Digital twins (DTs) require timely updates from Internet of Things (IoT) devices to accurately represent the state of the corresponding physical systems, but transmitting large data volumes can compromise freshness.
items.ai_summary: A freshness-aware framework for MEC-enabled digital twin networks uses a distributed linear bandit algorithm to optimize CPU allocation across task classes, reducing preprocessing delay while meeting age-of-information requirements.

items.title: Beyond Multi-Index Models: Learning Intersections of Degree-2 PTFs
items.description: We give an algorithm for PAC learning intersections of $k$ degree-2 polynomial threshold functions over $R^d$ under a Gaussian distribution.
items.ai_summary: A PAC learning algorithm for intersections of degree-2 polynomial threshold functions over a Gaussian distribution achieves classification error using time and samples with a dimension exponent independent of the accuracy parameter.

items.title: From AutoResearch to Continual AutoResearch: Do Agents Learn Across Tasks?
items.description: Autoresearch has shown that agents can autonomously write code, run experiments, and iteratively improve machine learning solutions.
items.ai_summary: Continual AutoResearch is an open-ended framework that evaluates persistent and reset autonomous agents across multiple task families to measure research efficiency and performance.

items.title: Label-Preserving Fourier Domain Adaptation with Generative-AI and Real Style Donors for 3D Mitral Valve Segmentation
items.description: Accurate segmentation of the mitral valve from three-dimensional transesophageal echocardiography (3D TEE) is severely restricted by the scarcity of publicly available expert- annotated volumetric datasets.
items.ai_summary: Fourier Domain Adaptation uses generative AI images as style donors to improve the boundary and surface segmentation of 3D mitral valve datasets.

items.title: Workload-Static Optical Circuit Switching For Scalable LLM Inference Decode
items.description: LLM inference decode executes fine-grained collectives whose latency directly limits per-user interactivity, yet scale-up fabrics are still built from electronic packet switches designed for training.
items.ai_summary: Workload-static optical circuit switching is a network design that configures circuits once per deployment to improve LLM inference decode interactivity and energy efficiency.

items.title: Molecular Prior Networks
items.description: Predicting affinity between small molecules and their protein targets remains one of the central problems in drug discovery.
items.ai_summary: Molecular Prior Networks is a transformer-based affinity modeling approach that predicts small molecule and protein target binding in a single forward pass without task-specific training.

items.title: Characterizing the vertical continuity of fuel strata based on TLS point clouds Gaussian decomposition and overlap metrics
items.description: Vertical forest structure influences fire behavior by regulating understory-to-canopy fuel connectivity, yet operational fuel-type models represent this complexity through discrete classes that only indirectly capture vertical continuity.
items.ai_summary: Gaussian decomposition applied to terrestrial laser scanning point clouds characterizes the vertical continuity and fuel strata of forest structures for fire behavior analysis.

items.title: Dual-VaDE: Efficient and Robust Prototype Learning via Variational Dual-Domain Mixture Priors
items.description: In this paper, we propose Dual-VaDE, an unsupervised generative framework for learning interpretable anatomical prototypes from unlabeled medical images.
items.ai_summary: Dual-VaDE is an unsupervised generative framework that uses a dual-domain Gaussian mixture prior to learn interpretable anatomical prototypes from unlabeled medical images.

items.title: The Platonic Brain: Representational Convergence in EEG Foundation Models
items.description: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) predicts that artificial neural networks converge on shared representations as scale and performance increase. We test whether these predictions hold for representations of the human brain with EEG foundation models.
items.ai_summary: EEG foundation models demonstrate that higher decoding performance leads to stronger cross-family and global semantic alignment with language models.

items.title: LatentTriad: Pre-Action Risk Representations for Malicious Agent Skill Detection
items.description: Large language model agents are increasingly extended with reusable skills, but untrusted skill content can induce operations outside the user's task.
items.ai_summary: LatentTriad is an execution-free skill screening method that detects malicious large language model agent behaviors by analyzing hidden states formed during prefill.

items.title: Sparse Anchors for Visual Multi-Session Registration in Changing Environments
items.description: Repeated robotic monitoring requires localization across visits to the same environment, even if the environment changes. Such changes can substantially reduce persistent visual content, and repetitive structures can lead to incorrect cross-session correspondences.
items.ai_summary: Sparse Anchors is a visual multi-session registration method that combines absolute pose constraints with relative-pose information to localize robots in changing environments.

items.title: Manifold Embedding of Deep Image Features for Image Matching via Neural Adjoint Maps
items.description: Estimating semantic correspondences between different object instances of similar categories in real-world images is a fundamental challenge in computer vision.
items.ai_summary: Neural Adjoint Maps is a zero-shot image matching method that uses deep image feature manifold embeddings and functional maps to estimate dense semantic correspondences.

items.title: CRONOS: Benchmarking Non-Episodic Reinforcement Learning for Robotic Manipulation
items.description: Reinforcement learning (RL) is promising for adapting robot policies to unstructured real-world environments.
items.ai_summary: CRONOS is a simulation benchmark for reinforcement learning fine-tuning of vision-language-action models under non-episodic scene resets, useful for studying and improving long-horizon robotic manipulation.

items.title: Data informed Ansatz Selection for Variational Quantum Circuits
items.description: Choosing a variational quantum circuit (VQC) usually means searching over ansatze and depths, and training each candidate. We give three rules that fix these choices from the data and the gate set alone, before any training.
items.ai_summary: A data-informed ansatz selection framework provides three rules using dataset Fourier coefficients, quantum Fisher information matrices, and Pauli-Z readouts to configure variational quantum circuits without grid searches.

items.title: Trajectory Evaluation via Rollout-Free World Model for End-to-end Autonomous Driving
items.description: Although existing candidate trajectory evaluators have substantially improved end-to-end planning accuracy, their underlying mechanism remains suboptimal.
items.ai_summary: RFWorld is a rollout-free world model for end-to-end autonomous driving that uses a shared scene memory with sparse spatial readout to evaluate candidate trajectories efficiently without recursive rollout errors.

items.title: Dataset Recommendation for Heterogeneous and Dynamic Scholarly Graphs via Multimodal Representation Learning
items.description: Researchers struggle to find relevant datasets amid the growing volume of data across repositories and scholarly publications.
items.ai_summary: MM-SAN is a heterogeneous multimodal graph representation learning method that combines topology-aware and text-based embeddings to recommend relevant datasets for research publications within scholarly knowledge graphs.

items.title: VIGOR: Visual Gain Ordering for Hallucination Mitigation in Multimodal Discrete Diffusion Language Models
items.description: Multimodal discrete diffusion language models (dLLMs) generate responses through iterative mask prediction and offer a promising alternative to autoregressive large vision-language models.
items.ai_summary: Visual Gain Ordering is a training-free inference strategy for multimodal discrete diffusion language models that reorders masked positions using counterfactual visual evidence to mitigate hallucination and improve reasoning.

items.title: FloMo: 3D Scene Flow as a World Action Model Intermediate for Learning from Human Video
items.description: Pretrained video generation models distill internet-scale motion priors into robot policies, but full video is a redundant signal for action prediction.
items.ai_summary: FloMo is a 5-billion parameter video-generation model fine-tuned to predict 3D scene-flow and action tokens, useful for efficiently transferring video pretraining knowledge to robot control policies.

items.title: Do Agentic Policies Need to Look at Every Step? Geometric Abstraction for Reasoning and Action
items.description: Recent multimodal language models can reason directly about robot scenes, but it is unclear whether they need to repeatedly reinterpret raw visual observations at every step of an interaction.
items.ai_summary: A geometric abstraction method represents scene geometry via typed symbolic references and compact textual checkpoints, reducing repeated multimodal queries while improving multi-step robot manipulation completion.

items.title: Ablating Design Choices for Protein Ensemble Generators Across Structural Regimes
items.description: Generative models of protein conformational ensembles inherit much of their design from structure prediction for folded proteins. Ordered and disordered proteins, however, occupy distinct structural regimes, and we investigate how design choices hold up across them.
items.ai_summary: A minimal flow-matching model and ablation study reveals that training data composition is the primary constraint for generative protein ensemble models across different structural regimes.

items.title: On the Learnability of Footwear Robustness: Footstep Recognition Under Unseen Conditions
items.description: Footstep patterns, captured using pressure or force-sensitive walkways during natural walking, offer a convenient and passive approach to biometric recognition.
items.ai_summary: BiStepNet is a novel deep learning architecture that decomposes spatial and temporal identity cues to enable robust zero-shot footstep biometric recognition across previously unseen footwear conditions.

items.title: Effects of Parton Pair Correlations on Direct-Photon Yields and Elliptic Flow in Heavy-Ion Collisions
items.description: Direct photons escape heavy-ion collisions with little rescattering, carrying information from the full emission history. Yet describing the measured direct-photon yield and the sizable elliptic flow $v_2$ together remains a long-standing challenge.
items.ai_summary: A physics analysis demonstrates that connected correlations between emitting partons in heavy-ion collisions raise direct-photon yields toward experimental data and increase elliptic flow at intermediate transverse momentum.

items.title: Positional Encoding is All You Need for Scalable Equivariance Constraint Relaxation
items.description: Equivariant neural networks incorporate known symmetries of the data, such as permutations, rotations, or translations, directly into their architecture, often improving sample efficiency and generalization.
items.ai_summary: Positional Encoding-based constraint relaxation is a novel method that efficiently relaxes equivariance constraints during training to improve performance without significant computational overhead.

items.title: ALBI: LLM-Guided Inductive Logic Programming via Iterative Generate-Test-Constrain Refineme
items.description: We introduce ALBI (Agent for Learning By Induction), a neuro-symbolic ILP framework that replaces the ASP-based hypothesis generator in the Learning from Failures (LFF) paradigm with a Large Language Model (LLM), while retaining SWI-Prolog as a formal verifier.
items.ai_summary: Agent for Learning By Induction is a neuro-symbolic framework that combines Large Language Models with Prolog to generate and verify logic programs with robust reasoning performance.

items.title: ToolSpace: Scaling Tool-Centric Environment Synthesis for Long-Horizon Agents
items.description: ToolSpace constructs realistic multi-environment tool-use benchmarks by mining execution traces, clustering tool compositions, and validating tasks through replayable state-aware random walks.

items.title: Federated Transfer Learning for Medical Image Classification under Mixed Skew
items.description: Deep learning in medical imaging is constrained by data scarcity and by privacy regulations that make centralizing patient data across institutions impractical.
items.ai_summary: Personalized Aligner Federated Pretrained is a framework that uses client-specific feature alignment modules on a pre-trained backbone to improve accuracy and cross-client equity in medical image classification.

items.title: Whose Effect Is It? How Objectives Inflate Learned Subspace Interventions
items.description: Interpretability often locates concepts by copying part of a language model's state from one input into another (activation patching). A larger output change counts as stronger evidence that this part carries the concept.
items.ai_summary: This paper proves that learned subspace interventions often exceed the effect of the whole network state due to optimization objectives rather than cleaner concept isolation.

items.title: Comparing model representations and fitting methods for port-Hamiltonian system identification
items.description: Port-Hamiltonian models describe physical systems by separating stored energy, dissipation and external inputs. Learning such models from data requires a choice of representation and fitting method.
items.ai_summary: This study compares various neural, analytic, and hybrid representations alongside optimization methods for port-Hamiltonian system identification to evaluate prediction accuracy and computational cost.

items.title: DRAP: Dynamics-Risk Adaptive Plasticity for Continual Learning in Physical AI
items.description: DRAP improves replay-free continual learning for physical AI by adaptively reducing plasticity of critical model components based on trajectory-amplification risk, enhancing retention of past behaviors without sacrificing new task learning.
items.ai_summary: Dynamics-Risk Adaptive Plasticity is a replay-free continual learning method that uses trajectory-amplification risk to scale learning rates and prevent catastrophic forgetting in physical AI agents.

items.title: RGB Photo Enhancement with Deep Learning on Smartphone GPUs: Mobile AI 2026 Challenge Report
items.description: On-device RGB photo enhancement is a popular task that is needed for quality improvement of photos captured with mobile devices as well as for retouching of images acquired through other sources.
items.ai_summary: This report presents deep learning models designed for fast, on-device RGB photo enhancement on smartphone GPUs while meeting strict mobile hardware constraints.

items.title: Finite Spectral Depth Controls Gaussian Entrance Rank and Avoidance of the First Gradient-Flow Saddle
items.description: Matrix factorization provides a simple model for studying the training dynamics of neural networks.
items.ai_summary: This paper demonstrates how a finite number of Newton-Schulz iterations controls rank selection and allows training trajectories to bypass the first gradient-flow saddle.

items.title: Rethinking GA2Ms: performance and out-of-distribution generalisation
items.description: Generalised Additive Models (GAMs) are a cornerstone of interpretable machine learning, offering transparent predictions through structured additive decompositions. Despite advances from classical GAMs to modern neural and spline-based variants, two notable gaps remain.
items.ai_summary: Composite Generalised Additive Model is a multi-resolution additive model that achieves competitive tabular prediction performance and superior robustness under out-of-distribution shifts compared to existing baselines.

items.title: Can saliency maps flag chest radiograph classifier errors at a new hospital? An external validation study
items.description: Saliency maps are offered as a safeguard for medical image classifiers, but whether they reveal individual errors at a new hospital remains largely untested.
items.ai_summary: This external validation study finds that saliency maps fail to reliably detect individual classifier errors at new hospitals, indicating that model confidence should anchor deployment monitoring instead.

items.title: Learned Smartphone ISP on Mobile GPUs: Mobile AI 2026 Challenge Report
items.description: With the increasing importance of mobile camera quality in modern smartphones, growing attention has been directed toward computational photography and advanced image signal processing (ISP) algorithms aimed at enhancing various perceptual attributes of captured images.
items.ai_summary: Deep learning models developed for the Mobile AI challenge reconstruct high-quality RGB images from RAW camera data on mobile GPUs in under 100 milliseconds.

items.title: When Category Means Move: A Paired-Support Audit of Recommendation Logs with Random Insertions
items.description: Content-category dashboards summarize production recommendation logs, although the serving policy selects the users, items, and contexts behind each mean. Using KuaiRand random-insertion impressions, we audit these summaries on the same 12,472 users and 5,486 videos in both logs.
items.ai_summary: An auditing framework for recommendation logs evaluates content-category dashboards using KuaiRand random-insertion impressions to quantify user-cluster differences.

items.title: ScoreDial: Precise Control of Visual Attributes in Image Generation via Regressor Guidance from Limited Human Ratings
items.description: Requested-value control is stricter than continuous steering: given $c$ on a human-rating scale, the generated image should attain that value from only limited ratings.
items.ai_summary: ScoreDial fits a differentiable regressor to human ratings and applies error-adaptive guidance during sampling to precisely control visual attributes in generated images.

items.title: Unifying and Beyond the Theory of Pervasive Capability Degradation in LLM Post-training SFT from Feature Interference
items.description: Pervasive Capability Degradation (PCD) refers to the phenomenon in which supervised fine-tuning (SFT), while adapting a large language model (LLM) to a target task, often erodes the general capabilities acquired during pre-training.
items.ai_summary: The AEGIS loss function constrains activation margin drift to prevent pervasive capability degradation during supervised fine-tuning of large language models.

items.title: Auditing Multi-Proxy Explanations of Web User Preferences: Identification Boundaries and Abstention
items.description: Web systems infer user preferences from behavior, ratings, text, and LLM-generated profiles, yet explaining a proxy may reveal its measurement process rather than the preference of interest.
items.ai_summary: An audit framework distinguishes point identification, partial identification, and abstention to evaluate how web systems explain user preferences derived from proxy data.

items.title: Exact Selective Inference for Spectral Clustering via Piecewise-Constant Graph Perturbation
items.description: Cluster labels are often used twice: first to discover groups, and then to test whether the discovered groups differ. This double use of the data makes ordinary two-sample $p$-values anti-conservative.
items.ai_summary: An exact selective inference method computes valid finite-sample p-values for spectral clustering by analyzing graph changes along one-dimensional perturbations.

items.title: ZEMA: confidence-calibrated signed descent with only one state
items.description: Recent work characterizes the Adam optimizer as sign descent modulated by gradient uncertainty: the update is the sign of the batch gradient, scaled by how strongly the batch supports that sign.
items.ai_summary: ZEMA is an optimization method that measures gradient support using per-coordinate z-scores and maintains a single exponential moving average state to improve fine-tuning and pretraining stability.

items.title: ProAlign: Progressive Positional and Prototype-Guided Alignment for Aerial-Ground Person Re-Identification
items.description: Aerial-Ground Person Re-Identification (AG-ReID) aims to match pedestrian images captured by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and ground-based surveillance cameras.
items.ai_summary: ProAlign is a progressive positional and prototype-guided alignment network that improves aerial-ground person re-identification by mitigating spatial distortions and cross-view semantic inconsistencies.

items.title: Scaling Laws For Data-Constrained Dense Retrieval
items.description: Dense retrieval models are typically obtained by fine-tuning pretrained language models on supervised retrieval data, where high-quality annotations or interaction logs are often limited and reused across many epochs.
items.ai_summary: A multiplicative power law models how the minimum achievable evaluation loss for dense retrieval models depends on model size and unique fine-tuning data under constrained data budgets.

items.title: GeoFaham: Domain-Specialized Multi-Agent Geospatial Analytics for Disaster Response
items.description: Real-world geospatial decision support requires more than single-step retrieval or code generation.
items.ai_summary: GeoFaham is a domain-specialized multi-agent system that coordinates specialist agents using a dual-ledger control loop to automate multi-step geospatial disaster analytics.

items.title: LLMs as MDP Designers: A Dependency-Aware Agentic Framework for Automated Robot Policy Generation
items.description: We investigate the automated generation of executable robot reinforcement learning (RL) policies from natural-language task descriptions.
items.ai_summary: ARPG is a dependency-aware agentic framework that automates the generation of executable robot reinforcement learning policies from natural-language task descriptions by structuring Markov decision processes and simulators.

items.title: Who is the Pronoun Pro? Comparing LLMs and Humans at Number-Disambiguation of 'they'
items.description: This study evaluates whether large language models (LLMs) can reliably replace or complement human research assistants in linguistically complex annotation.
items.ai_summary: Study evaluating large language models against humans in number-disambiguating the pronoun 'they' finds that top models achieve high accuracy, demonstrating viability for large-scale linguistic annotation support under human oversight.

items.title: An Agentic Framework for Quality-Aware and Scenario-Adaptive Image Compression
items.description: Despite decades of progress, image codecs remain difficult to adapt to diverse real-world compression scenarios for two main reasons. First, most image codecs are optimized for a specific objective and require substantial redevelopment when the compression goal changes.
items.ai_summary: PICA is a multi-agent framework that adapts existing image compression codecs to diverse user requirements and degraded inputs using collaborative perception, improvement, coding, and post-coding agents.

items.title: Lightweight graph transformers for clutter and target classification in automotive radar
items.description: Radar is a core sensor modality for scene perception to achieve higher levels of autonomy in automotive driving.
items.ai_summary: Tiny graph transformer network models classify radar clutter from stationary and moving targets in automotive scenes with high precision and recall while offering significantly smaller model sizes and faster inference.

items.title: Shuffled OPSD: When Semantic Consistency Hurts On-Policy Self-Distillation?
items.description: Knowledge distillation improves a student model's reasoning ability through supervision from a teacher.
items.ai_summary: Shuffled OPSD improves student reasoning accuracy in on-policy self-distillation by shuffling the words of the shared problem statement while preserving the teacher-only worked example.

items.title: Deep Neural Operator Learning for stochastic heat equations and applications
items.description: In this paper, we establish a universal approximation theorem for solution operators of semilinear stochastic heat equations in spatial dimension \(d\ge2\), extending deep neural operator approximation results to SPDEs with distribution-valued Gaussian forcing.
items.ai_summary: Universal approximation theorem establishes that deep neural operators can accurately solve semilinear stochastic heat equations with distribution-valued Gaussian forcing.

items.title: Artifact-to-Capability: Diagnosing Breaks in Capability Formation of Self-Evolving Agents in a Controlled Environment
items.description: Self-evolving agents write interaction experience into artifacts and reuse them in later tasks. Most work supports such methods with three proxy signals: artifacts accumulate, behavior changes once they are loaded, and metrics rise. We call this signal-based evaluation.
items.ai_summary: Diagnostic framework evaluates self-evolving agents across state, game, and lineage levels to determine whether genuine capability formation has occurred from accumulated artifacts.

items.title: DPAGait: Dynamic Pose-Knowledge-Aware Network for Robust Gait Recognition in the Wild
items.description: Gait biometrics aims at identity recognition by appearance or pose features captured during unconstrained human walking.
items.ai_summary: DPAGait is a dual-branch dynamic pose-knowledge-aware gait recognition network that combines pose-parsing cues with silhouettes and 3D SMPL models to improve robustness in the wild.

items.title: HERIT: Enabling Global Access to Hanja-to-English Historical Translation by Mitigating Temporal Bias
items.description: HERIT adapts machine translation to historical archives via retrieval-augmented pseudo-labeling, improving accuracy across time periods and unlocking global access.
items.ai_summary: HERIT is a domain-adaptation pipeline that uses retrieval-augmented generation to mitigate temporal bias and translate Hanja-Korean historical archives into English.

items.title: PATTS: Parallel-Aware Test-Time Scaling for Thought-Image Generation in Multimodal Discrete Diffusion LLMs
items.description: Test-time scaling (TTS) improves generative models by allocating additional inference-time computation to sampling, search, and verification. Existing image generation approaches, however, typically rank completed images or image-centric intermediate states.
items.ai_summary: PATTS is a parallel-aware test-time scaling framework that searches over intermediate thought-image states using cross-modal verifier signals to improve multimodal discrete diffusion language model generation.

items.title: How Well Does Webcam Eye Tracking Work "in the Wild"? A Large-Scale Validation of Chiasm and a Comparison with WebGazer
items.description: Webcam eye tracking can greatly accelerate data collection in basic and applied research by reaching large, diverse samples of participants online. However, its spatial performance is considered well below that of hardware-based systems, limiting its use.
items.ai_summary: Large-scale evaluation study of the Chiasm webcam eye tracker reveals its spatial accuracy and precision across diverse participants and recording conditions.

items.title: Learning Where to Look: Observation Policy Optimization for Thinking with Images
items.description: Complex visual question answering often requires vision-language models to think with images, i.e., actively acquire local visual evidence by zooming into informative regions of high-resolution images.
items.ai_summary: Observation Policy Optimization is a reinforcement learning algorithm that improves vision-language models by selectively branching and optimizing local image-cropping decisions.

items.title: Residual Attribute Leakage Is an Interface: Auditing Privacy Evaluation After Text De-identification
items.description: A privacy evaluation of de-identified text asks a language model (the adversary) to guess a person's protected attribute. We introduce a prior-normalised clipped leakage score of its confidence gain on the true value and audit the conclusions drawn from it.
items.ai_summary: A study on de-identified text privacy evaluation introduces a leakage score and demonstrates how varying the evaluation interface alters adversary conclusions.

items.title: HTNN-MSC: Multi-view Subspace Clustering with a Hyperbolic Tangent Tensor Low-Rank Surrogate
items.description: High-order dependencies among views can be modeled by tensor singular value decomposition (t-SVD) in multi-view subspace clustering.
items.ai_summary: HTNN-MSC is a multi-view subspace clustering method using a hyperbolic tangent tensor rank surrogate that achieves high clustering accuracy across multiple datasets.

items.title: Robustness Verification against Patch Attacks via Group-Lasso Semidefinite Relaxation
items.description: Robustness verification is essential for ensuring the safety and security of neural networks, but current methods focus heavily on norm-ball attacks, which do not adequately model typical real-world threats that present physical perturbations, known as patch attacks.
items.ai_summary: A robustness verification method uses Group-Lasso semidefinite relaxation to efficiently verify neural networks against physical patch attacks without enumerating patch positions.

items.title: KKKKhazix/agent-autoloop
items.description: 让你的命令行 Agent 在后台自己接活、自己跟进到底；平时不烦你，遇到拿不准的事才发卡片找你拍板。
items.ai_summary: Lightweight automation tool for managing command-line agents in the background and notifying users only when decisions are required.

items.title: FlowTranslator: Training-Free In-Image Machine Translation with Flow-Based Editing
items.description: FlowTranslator is a training-free framework for in-image machine translation that uses diffusion trajectory controls to generate accurate translated text within images without paired training data.

items.title: Is Forgetting Unified? Exploring Concept Unlearning in Unified Multimodal Models
items.description: Cross-pathway concept unlearning in unified multimodal models is addressed by a new benchmark and method that jointly suppresses target concept generation and recognition while preserving other capabilities.

items.title: Behind Video Generation: Observations and Insights on Multimodal Understanding from Kling
items.description: Kling's multimodal understanding stack links caption density, perceptual text encoding, reward modeling, and evaluation protocols to improve controllable video generation.

items.title: Near-Zero Token Embeddings Silently Stall Training in Gated Sequence Models
items.description: Near-zero input embeddings in untied gated language models cause extreme gradient amplification and training instability, which is addressed by GroupClip and GateFloor remedies.

items.title: PrimeSim: A Generalist World Model Simulator from Large-Scale Cross-Embodiment Demonstrations
items.description: PrimeSim is an action-conditioned multiview world model that uses progressive training, unified action representations, view-aware attention, and hierarchical memory to enable consistent, long-horizon robot simulation and policy optimization.

items.title: vixhal-baraiya/qwenFS
items.description: Qwen3.5-2B with a filesystem compiled and inserted directly into its weights.
items.ai_summary: Experimental Qwen model featuring an integrated filesystem compiled directly into its transformer layer weights.
