items.title: Evaluating Uncertainty Calibration in Probabilistic Time Series Foundation Models
items.description: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) are increasingly used for probabilistic forecasting across diverse domains, yet the reliability of their uncertainty estimates remains poorly understood.
items.ai_summary: Framework for evaluating uncertainty calibration in probabilistic time series foundation models that reveals systematic patterns of miscalibration across multiple horizons.

items.title: A Scaling Theory of Multi-Epoch Pretraining: Late-Time Overfitting and Ensembling
items.description: In the near future language model pretraining will become bound by total data rather than total compute. Such a regime requires revisiting scaling laws and scaling law theory.
items.ai_summary: Scaling theory and a dynamical mean-field theory for multi-epoch stochastic gradient descent show that ensembling reduces prediction variance in language model pretraining and improves compute-allocation laws.

items.title: 3D-BBDA: Backpropagation-Free Black-Box Domain Adaptation for Robust 3D Point Cloud Recognition
items.description: Robust 3D point-cloud recognition is critical for robotics, mapping, and urban sensing, yet point-cloud classifiers often suffer performance drops under domain shifts caused by sensor changes, environmental variation, and acquisition artifacts.
items.ai_summary: 3D-BBDA is a backpropagation-free black-box domain adaptation framework that adapts 3D point-cloud classifiers to unlabeled target data using only pseudo-label guided prototype alignment and logit fusion.

items.title: FedReady: Bounded Agents for Federation Formation
items.description: Federated learning (FL) runtimes standardize aggregation and deployment, but each new study still requires federation formation: selecting task-eligible sites and preparing their local data and task code for federated training or analysis.
items.ai_summary: FedReady is a system that uses bounded LLM agents to perform federated learning site discovery, contract proposal, and local eligibility verification.

items.title: Agentic backdoors via pretraining poisoning
items.description: Trending on Hacker News from arxiv.org. 103 points and 30 comments.

items.title: Sonar-MoE: In-Backward Expert Updates for Memory-Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Training
items.description: Most parameters of a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model belong to its experts, and standard training keeps every expert gradient in GPU memory until the optimizer step. This memory grows with the number and size of the experts, so it rises as MoE models scale.
items.ai_summary: Sonar-MoE is a memory-efficient training method for mixture-of-experts models that updates each expert tensor during the backward pass to lower peak GPU memory.

items.title: NitiBench+: A Temporal Thai Legal Question Answering Benchmark Across 17 Domains
items.description: Law changes over time. A court decides a case under the law in force on that day, and legal QA benchmarks grade answers against today's law. We checked 156,650 decisions of four Thai courts. Up to 67% of them cite law that has since been amended or repealed.
items.ai_summary: NitiBench+ is a temporal Thai legal question-answering benchmark comprising 1,670 items across 17 domains that tracks historical legal text versions and court decisions.

items.title: VeriHarm-Bench: Measuring Harmful Success in LLM Coding Agents Verifiably
items.description: Large language model (LLM) coding agents increasingly operate with shell access, allowing them to write scripts, move files, alter permissions, and modify system configurations.
items.ai_summary: VeriHarm is an automatic evaluation framework that minimally perturbs coding tasks to generate programmatically verifiable benchmarks measuring unintended harmful side effects in language model coding agents.

items.title: BISECT: Bilevel Spectral Decomposition for Low-Rank Continual Learning
items.description: Exemplar-free continual learning on pre-trained Vision Transformers increasingly relies on Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), yet prevailing methods govern the low-rank update space through strict subspace isolation.
items.ai_summary: BISECT is a continual LoRA framework for vision transformers that splits a fixed rank budget into an invariant carrier and a novelty complement to prevent spectral starvation.

items.title: PlantVLM-Edge: Quantized Vision-Language Models for On-Device Crop Health Diagnosis
items.description: Timely and accurate crop health diagnosis is essential for sustainable agricultural production, yet accurate diagnosis often requires expert knowledge that is not readily available.
items.ai_summary: PlantVLM-Edge is a quantized vision-language framework combining agricultural domain adaptation and post-training quantization for conversational on-device crop health diagnosis on edge hardware.

items.title: MCP Tool Poisoning in Agentic AI Frameworks: A Cross-Framework Measurement Study
items.description: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) lets agentic AI frameworks connect language models to external tool providers, but it carries attacker-controlled content (tool descriptions, schema fields, and response data) into model context without validation.
items.ai_summary: An open-source measurement study and tool called mcpvenom evaluate the susceptibility of 12 agentic AI frameworks to Model Context Protocol tool poisoning attacks that execute malicious instructions.

items.title: Nonparametric Intensity Estimation for Covariate-Driven Poisson Processes Using Deep Learning
items.description: We consider nonparametric maximum likelihood estimation of the intensity function of a Poisson process, allowing the intensity to depend on observed covariates.
items.ai_summary: Nonparametric maximum likelihood estimation using deep neural networks estimates the intensity function of covariate-driven Poisson processes without requiring intensities to be bounded away from zero.

items.title: Can LLM Agents Be Forward-Deployed Engineers? Requirement Discovery and Delivery for Enterprise Text-to-SQL
items.description: LLM coding agents can increasingly automate model post-training, but whether they can act as forward-deployed engineer (FDE) agents, discovering customer requirements and turning them into deployment decisions, remains unclear.
items.ai_summary: Study on LLM coding agents acting as forward-deployed engineers finds that the strongest models discover over 80 percent of requirements, but only 25 percent of execution runs pass all acceptance criteria.

items.title: Can LLM Agents Improve Imperfect Earth System Model Parameterizations?
items.description: Earth system models (ESMs) rely on parameterizations to represent unresolved processes such as convection, cloud microphysics, and turbulence.
items.ai_summary: Evaluation of AI agents synthesizing scientific literature and writing code shows that iterative feedback improves rollout error for most language models and enables them to produce executable parameterizations.

items.title: Variational Functional Neural Networks (vfNN)
items.description: We present a variational functional neural network (vfNN) algorithm that optimizes physically motivated continuum functionals in integral form (e.g., Lagrangian, Hamiltonian, or free energy) to find the states of a system.
items.ai_summary: Variational functional neural network algorithm optimizes physics-motivated continuum functionals using a quasi-Newton optimization method to find system states while bypassing differential equations of motion.

items.title: An Agentic Framework for Automated Power System Studies and Grid Connection Assessment
items.description: Connecting new generation and demand to the grid depends on two scarce skills: checking applications against a large, changing body of regulation, and running the network studies that decide where and how a project connects.
items.ai_summary: Grid Agents is an AI system that combines regulatory knowledge retrieval with power-system engineering tools to assist with grid connection assessments and studies.

items.title: CoLa3D: Composable Latent 3D Decomposition
items.description: We introduce CoLa3D, a simple and effective model for composable 3D scene decomposition that, given a single whole-scene latent from either a single image or an existing scene mesh as input, directly outputs a set of object meshes with consistent spatial layout that can be…
items.ai_summary: CoLa3D is a lightweight query-based transformer that decomposes whole-scene latents into consistent object meshes, improving scene-level consistency and object-level quality.

items.title: Preparing our next security sprint to harden OpenAI
items.description: OpenAI is preparing its next internal security sprint with Cathedral Systems to test and strengthen its defenses using AI.
items.ai_summary: OpenAI is preparing an internal security sprint with Cathedral Systems to test and strengthen its defenses using AI.

items.title: Rewarding defenders with bigger bug bounties
items.description: OpenAI is raising Security Bug Bounty rewards and introducing report quality, loyalty, and priority campaign bonuses for independent security researchers.
items.ai_summary: OpenAI is raising its Security Bug Bounty rewards and introducing additional bonuses for independent security researchers.

items.title: ParaDeAl: Parallel Descent Algorithms for Sparse Statistics
items.description: Best subset selection is a central problem in statistical regression, drawing increasing attention from the broader optimization and machine learning communities.
items.ai_summary: ParaDeAl is a GPU-accelerated proximal gradient descent approach that enforces sparsity constraints and incorporates penalties to solve statistical regression problems up to 15 times faster than CPU competitors.

items.title: Contrastive Adapter Training and Consensus Knowledge Distillation for Multi-Source-Free Domain Adaptation in Skin Cancer Diagnosis
items.description: Skin cancer diagnosis, particularly differentiating melanoma from benign nevi, is challenging due to the visual similarity between lesions.

items.title: Library of Layers (LoL): Adaptively Ordering Transformer Layers at Runtime
items.description: Library of Layers dynamically orders transformer blocks during inference to adapt computation to tasks, enabling parameter reuse, sparsity, and interpretable routing across reasoning, multilingual, and safety settings.

items.title: Grading the Unannotated: Insights from the WorkRB Skill Extraction Challenge at RecSys-HR 2026
items.description: Skill extraction benchmarks score models against a few human-annotated positives and treat every other skill in the vocabulary as equally wrong.
items.ai_summary: RecSys-HR 2026 challenge benchmark replaces binary skill extraction evaluation with graded relevance scores using a cascaded LLM judge and human validation to better penalize nonsensical predictions.

items.title: DistDebug-Bench: Can LLM Agents Diagnose Bugs in Distributed Systems?
items.description: LLM agents show strong potential in software engineering tasks such as competitive programming and code synthesis.
items.ai_summary: DistDebug-Bench is a benchmark evaluating AI agents on diagnosing complex code-level failures in real-world distributed systems.

items.title: PanoTac: A Dense Three-Axis Tactile Sensor for Robust Touch-Centric Manipulation
items.description: Contact-rich manipulation benefits from tactile feedback that captures both detailed contact geometry and interaction forces. When scooping grains, contact patterns help infer spoon orientation, while resistance transmitted through the grasp guides motion.
items.ai_summary: PanoTac is a low-cost, compliant tactile fingertip sensor providing dense three-axis feedback to improve contact-rich robot manipulation tasks.

items.title: VIAS: Value-Isolating Activation Steering for Multi-Value Alignment and Compliance for Organisations
items.description: Organisations increasingly deploy large language model agents that must follow organisational values.
items.ai_summary: Value-Isolating Activation Steering is a method that isolates individual organizational value vectors to improve multi-value compliance in language models.

items.title: Ask, Don't Equip: Question-Driven Coding Agents for Deep Kernel Optimization
items.description: A question-driven LLM agent improves CUDA kernels by asking targeted questions at decision points, achieving faster FlashAttention implementations than a tool-rich autonomous baseline.
items.ai_summary: KernelSeek is a question-driven coding agent that optimizes GPU kernels without operator-specific knowledge or reference implementations.

items.title: RASP: Read-All, Sparse-Plasticity Continual Learning in a Stationary-Size LoRA
items.description: Parameter-efficient continual learning on pre-trained Vision Transformers largely relies on a costly premise: preventing catastrophic forgetting requires either spawning a dedicated LoRA branch per session---causing adapter parameters to scale linearly with task horizon---or…
items.ai_summary: RASP is a parameter-efficient continual learning method for Vision Transformers that uses a stationary-size LoRA adapter with sparse gradient updates.

items.title: ST-GFM: Spectral-Temporal Graph Forecasting with Measured Perturbation Bounds and Masked Spectral Reconstruction
items.description: Graph forecasters for sensor networks are trained in one regime and deployed in others, where sensor coupling and signal frequency content both change. We split this spectral shift into an operator channel and a frequency channel, each with a dimensionless measure.
items.ai_summary: ST-GFM is a spectral-temporal graph forecasting model that uses Chebyshev and diffusion filters with masked spectral reconstruction to handle domain shifts.

items.title: A Cross-Domain Matrix Engine for Signal Processing and Deep Neural Net Inference
items.description: Matrix multiplication dominates both PHY signal processing and Deep Neural Network (DNN) inference, yet these domains place opposing demands on the matrix engine.
items.ai_summary: A cross-domain matrix engine dynamically reconfigures its architecture between a systolic array and a tensor unit to accelerate both signal processing and deep neural network inference.

items.title: Can AI Do Formal Demography? Why Vaccinating the Oldest Saves Both the Most Lives and the Most Years of Life
items.description: Can AI contribute to formal demography?
items.ai_summary: An experiment with the AI model Claude demonstrates how AI can simplify proofs in formal demography, specifically regarding COVID-19 vaccination strategies for older populations.

items.title: Online Label-Free Gradient Matching for Continual Language Model Training
items.description: Language models in customer-facing products must be continually updated, since the data they serve shifts over time.
items.ai_summary: OLGA is an online label-free gradient matching method that distills unlabeled text data streams to continually update language models efficiently.

items.title: Harder Than the Task: From Technical to Organizational Difficulty in AI Benchmarking
items.description: AI benchmarks have made remarkable progress in measuring the ability of AI systems to perform increasingly demanding cognitive and technical tasks.
items.ai_summary: A study on organizational task difficulty highlights that current AI benchmarks lack adequate coverage of the complex relational and structural conditions found in real-world work.

items.title: A Hybrid Visitor Prediction Framework using Interpretable Temporal features, Integrating IQR and Anomaly Detection in Lakes in Nebraska
items.description: For effective resource management, infrastructure planning, and sustainable tourism, it is really important to predict accurate visitors. This paper estimates the daily visitation of Nebraska lakes using spatial, basic temporal, and interpretable temporal features.
items.ai_summary: Hybrid visitor prediction framework that uses temporal features, anomaly detection, and ensemble methods to accurately forecast daily lake visitation numbers.

items.title: Identifying the Shear Piezoelectric Coefficient using Physics-Informed Neural Networks under Exact Boundary and Initial Constraints
items.description: The shear piezoelectric coefficient $e_{15}$ governs the shear-mode electromechanical coupling in piezoelectric micromachined ultrasonic transducers (PMUTs) and surface acoustic wave (SAW) devices, but measuring it typically requires destructive resonance testing on dedicated…
items.ai_summary: Physics-informed neural network that incorporates exact boundary and spatial constraints to non-destructively recover the shear piezoelectric coefficient from sparse wavefield observations.

items.title: Tilted Convexity and an Exact Offline-Online Separation
items.description: Convexity has three equivalent descriptions: support by affine functions, monotonicity of the subdifferential, and increasing secant slopes.
items.ai_summary: Mathematical framework that introduces a distortion parameter to generalize convexity concepts, establishing an exact separation between offline and online optimization complexity.

items.title: A Bayesian Framework for Safe Optimal Control of Unknown Systems from Input-Output Data
items.description: As control engineering is applied to increasingly complex systems, learning-based control, which uses empirical data to reduce the reliance on first-principles models, has emerged as a promising paradigm.
items.ai_summary: Bayesian framework that updates state-space representations from input-output data to provide probabilistic safety guarantees and robust optimal control for unknown systems.

items.title: HIVE-Diff: High Frame Rate HDR Video Reconstruction from a Single LDR Frame and Events
items.description: High frame rate HDR video is important in applications such as autonomous driving and scientific imaging, where rapid motion and extreme illumination often occur simultaneously.
items.ai_summary: Event-conditioned video diffusion framework that reconstructs high frame rate HDR videos from a single low-dynamic-range reference frame and event camera data.

items.title: Unrolled gradients in disguise: bridging interpolation-based and Jacobian regularization for stable neural dynamics
items.description: Hybrid models and neural differential equations (NDEs) are becoming increasingly important for modelling physical systems; however, they often encounter stability and accuracy issues during long-term integration.
items.ai_summary: Unified analytical approach showing that training on interpolated samples and Jacobian regularization both approximate unrolled gradient strategies to improve the stability of learned neural dynamics.

items.title: Bg-Mix: On Using Image Backgrounds for Data Augmentation in Electron Microscopy Images
items.description: Electron microscopy (EM) serves as a cornerstone in virology enabling the visualization of viral particles and is widely used in research, diagnostics and morphological characterization of pathogens.
items.ai_summary: Data augmentation method called Bg-Mix that decomposes electron microscopy images into foregrounds and backgrounds to create novel training images and improve object detection performance.

items.title: Online Class Posteriors for Interpretable and Controllable Discrete Diffusion
items.description: Discrete diffusion models remain far less understood than their continuous counterparts, despite recent breakthroughs across modalities, most notably in text.
items.ai_summary: Theoretical framework for discrete diffusion that tracks class-conditional posteriors online to provide interpretable token dynamics and precise logical guidance for generation.

items.title: Improving Hamiltonian Learning through Local Energy Decomposition
items.description: Hamiltonian neural networks provide a principled framework for learning conservative dynamics. A scalar Hamiltonian is parameterized by a neural network and the vector field is derived using Hamilton's equations.
items.ai_summary: Local Multiscale Hamiltonian Neural Network that decomposes energy into kinetic and potential components across interaction neighborhoods to improve Hamiltonian learning and long-horizon rollouts.

items.title: Intent2CAD: How Semantic-Parametric Supervision Shapes Text-to-CAD Generation
items.description: Text-to-CAD generation aims to make CAD modeling more accessible by generating executable CAD programs from natural-language descriptions.
items.ai_summary: Intent2CAD is a semantic-parametric supervision approach and dataset pipeline that generates editable, executable CAD programs from natural language descriptions while exposing reusable structure.

items.title: Error Accumulation in Second-Order Sequential Machine Unlearning
items.description: Machine unlearning seeks to remove the influence of deleted training data without full retraining. In the sequential setting, deletion requests arrive over time, and repeated updates can accumulate approximation errors.
items.ai_summary: Method for analyzing error accumulation in second-order sequential machine unlearning, which uses Newton-conjugate gradient updates to achieve efficient certification and vanishing population-risk degradation.

items.title: Subpolynomial-Query Proximal Sampling Beyond Log-Concavity
items.description: We study the gradient query complexity of sampling from a density $π(x)\propto\mathrm{e}^{-V(x)}$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, where $V$ has a $β$-Lipschitz gradient but need not be convex.
items.ai_summary: Proximal sampling algorithm that uses a high-order noisy conditional sampler to achieve subpolynomial gradient query complexity for sampling from non-convex densities satisfying functional inequalities.

items.title: Playing Dumb: How a Chess Transformer Simulates Users Across Skill Levels
items.description: Generative models increasingly simulate users at different skill levels in education and AI evaluation. Yet it remains unclear whether lower-skill behavior reflects less internal knowledge or a different use of retained knowledge.
items.ai_summary: Method for analyzing skill simulation in a chess transformer, demonstrating that lower-skill behavior can be transformed into best-move decisions by fine-tuning only the final output layer.

items.title: Align Once to Explain: Feature Alignment for Scalable B-cosification of Foundational Vision Transformers
items.description: Foundational vision models have become the de facto standard for many vision tasks due to their strong performance. However, they are notoriously opaque and remain hard to interpret.
items.ai_summary: ALOE is a one-time, label-free feature alignment method that converts foundational vision models into B-cos variants to provide efficient and interpretable downstream explanations.

items.title: Bridging Neural Tangent Kernel Analysis and Reinforcement Learning for Deep Function Approximation
items.description: Despite their widespread success across machine learning, the learning dynamics and generalization properties of neural networks remain poorly understood.
items.ai_summary: Temporal-difference flow formulation that extends neural tangent kernel theory to reinforcement learning, providing a closed-form solution for value function evolution and improving exploration efficiency.

items.title: Optimize the Harness, Not the Model: Fitting a Minimal Agent to a Self-Hostable LLM for Investigative Analysis
items.description: Government intelligence teams need LLM agents that can analyze large, messy evidence collections, but security and cost constraints often rule out hosted frontier models and broad, hard-to-audit tool surfaces.
items.ai_summary: CLEO is a method that fits a minimal agent harness to a self-hostable LLM, yielding a resource-efficient tool for evidence analysis in constrained environments.

items.title: A Living Leaderboard for Graph Machine Learning
items.description: Graph machine learning benchmarking results are scattered across papers that use quite different sets of datasets and baseline methods, making it difficult to tell whether a reported gain reflects architectural progress or merely an outdated comparison or weakly tuned baseline.
items.ai_summary: Living leaderboard for graph machine learning that extracts and organizes benchmark results from peer-reviewed papers to contextualize architectural progress and baseline comparisons.

items.title: Evaluating Depth-Augmented Visual Features for Cross-Dataset Lunar Traversability Estimation
items.description: Autonomous mobility is essential for sustained lunar surface operations, as communication delays and line-of-sight occlusions limit continuous teleoperation.
items.ai_summary: Framework that evaluates depth-augmented visual features for cross-dataset lunar traversability estimation, finding that training source choice dominates over naive geometric augmentation.

items.title: IdeaTaste: Do LLMs Share the Research Taste of Human Researchers?
items.description: IdeaTaste benchmarks LLM research proposals against future publications, revealing that AI agents match human communities in broad directions but fall far behind in concrete approaches and expected success.
items.ai_summary: IdeaTaste is a benchmark that evaluates how closely LLM-generated research proposals match human-published papers, revealing a significant gap in concrete research taste and execution.

items.title: Circumventing Magnitude Collapse via Modular Two-Stage Open-Set Recognition
items.description: Open-set recognition (OSR) requires neural networks to classify known classes while rejecting unknown samples, which is critical for real-world deployment.
items.ai_summary: Modular two-stage pipeline for open-set recognition that identifies magnitude collapse at scale and uses a magnitude-aware postprocessing baseline to achieve state-of-the-art performance.

items.title: Temporal Island Sparse Autoencoders for Interpreting Clinical Time-Series Models
items.description: Deep learning models for electronic health records achieve strong predictive performance but provide little insight into what clinical concepts they represent internally.
items.ai_summary: The Temporal Island Sparse Autoencoder learns a backbone-specific, patient-shared clinical concept dictionary from a frozen predictive model to produce structured, interpretable electronic health record representations.

items.title: Finite-Memory Control of POMDPs: Fundamental Limits and Efficient Design
items.description: Optimal control of partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs), in general, requires a complete history. The belief state, a distribution over hidden states, summarizes this history and provides the classical sufficient statistic to control POMDPs.
items.ai_summary: RECAP is a constructive quantization method that designs representative memory states for finite-memory partially observable Markov decision process controllers to improve control performance.

items.title: DeliverBench: Benchmarking AI Agents on Delivering Realistic Multi-Stage Professional Projects
items.description: LLM agents are judged by what they deliver, and in professional work what gets delivered is a project, not a task. A project pays off only if the whole package holds, and one weak part can limit the value of the rest.
items.ai_summary: DeliverBench is a benchmark testing whether large language model agents can successfully carry multi-stage professional projects from brief to final delivery across multiple tasks.

items.title: Low-Rank Clebsch--Gordan Coupling for Equivariant Spherical Forecasting
items.description: Spherical-harmonic neural operators provide an efficient representation for global forecasting, but their discretized pointwise nonlinearities can break rotational equivariance through aliasing.
items.ai_summary: LCG-SFNO combines low-rank Clebsch-Gordan tensor products with a sparse GPU implementation to enable efficient, exactly rotation-equivariant spherical forecasting at scale.

items.title: From Reactive to Agentic Resilience: Multi-Timescale AI-RAN Orchestration Under Signaling Storms
items.description: Next-generation open radio access network (Open RAN) and AI-RAN deployments turn the RAN into a disaggregated, compute-aware platform whose service continuity depends on many control loops acting at different timescales.
items.ai_summary: A three-tier agentic AI framework coordinates open radio access network control loops across timescales to anticipate and absorb mass-attachment signaling storms.

items.title: VidDub: Replacement-Aware Distillation for Two-Step Video Dubbing
items.description: VidDub is a two-step diffusion video dubbing model that uses replacement-aware cross-audio supervision to avoid conflicting source-mouth targets and achieves strong lip synchronization with high visual fidelity.
items.ai_summary: VidDub is a two-step video dubbing model that uses replacement-aware cross-audio supervision to synthesize accurate lip movements while preserving source video identity and background.

items.title: Image Guided Depth Upsampling using Anisotropic Total Generalized Variation
items.description: In this work we present a novel method for the challenging problem of depth image upsampling. Modern depth cameras such as Kinect or Time of Flight cameras deliver dense, high quality depth measurements but are limited in their lateral resolution.
items.ai_summary: An anisotropic total generalized variation method uses a high-resolution intensity image to guide fast and accurate depth image upsampling through convex optimization.

items.title: TaoMate-HD: Progressive-Resolution Autoregressive Audio-Video Generation
items.description: TaoMate-HD is an autoregressive streaming model that generates high-resolution audiovisual content in chunks with progressive denoising, history-based continuation, and optimized parallel deployment for faster, coherent long-form output.
items.ai_summary: TaoMate-HD is an autoregressive streaming model that uses progressive-resolution generation and continuation training to produce synchronized high-resolution audio and video efficiently.

items.title: TaoMate-FVSR:Audio-Guided Facial Video Restoration
items.description: An audio-guided framework restores facial details in AI-generated videos by combining reference-guided flow modeling with audio synchronization to resolve lip and dental ambiguity.

items.title: Progressive Multi-Scale Super-Resolution via Cascaded Bicubic Anchors and Inter-Scale Mutual Refinement
items.description: Super-resolution networks are trained for one magnification factor, so several output resolutions require several models.
items.ai_summary: PMS-SR is a progressive multi-scale super-resolution network that produces multiple output resolutions in a single forward pass using cascaded bicubic anchors and inter-scale mutual refinement.

items.title: CrowdForge: Effects of Audio and Visual Audience Participation Modalities on Agency, Collaboration, and Engagement in AI-Mediated MR Performances
items.description: Technology-mediated audience participation (TMAP) enables audiences to influence live performances, yet balancing interaction with meaningful agency remains challenging.
items.ai_summary: CrowdForge is an AI- and mixed-reality-mediated performance paradigm demonstrating that visual and audio audience participation modalities drive user agency, collaboration, and engagement during live shows.

items.title: LAND: Learning an Adaptive Number of Draws for Bayesian Best-of-N Selection
items.description: Best-of-N decoding improves generation quality by sampling multiple candidates and selecting the best, but it allocates equal compute to sources regardless of how much they benefit from additional sampling: the expected benefit is small for sources with low-variance score…
items.ai_summary: LAND is an adaptive best-of-N decoding method that dynamically allocates sample counts based on score distribution variance, improving compute efficiency across machine-translation tasks.

items.title: Claude Opus 5.5 Can Draw Permit-Level Architectural Drawings
items.description: Trending on Hacker News from stephenjgallagher.substack.com. 102 points and 34 comments.

items.title: Can We Stop the Backtest Yet? Anytime-Valid Promotion Tests for Adaptive Financial Research Agents
items.description: Financial research agents can generate and monitor trading rules faster than a human can document the resulting selection process. Candidates appear at data-dependent times, weak rules are abandoned, and promising ones are watched until they cross a reporting threshold.
items.ai_summary: PROMOTE is a protocol for financial research agents that bounds the probability of promoting false trading rules through predictable testing wealth and cost-aware e-processes.

items.title: ASCoR: Asymmetric Semantic-Spatial Learning for Remote Sensing Domain Generalization
items.description: Source-only domain generalization (DG) for remote sensing semantic segmentation seeks reliable predictions in unseen domains without target-domain data during training.
items.ai_summary: ASCoR is an asymmetric semantic-spatial framework for remote sensing domain generalization that uses SAM3 and dynamic adapters to achieve reliable predictions across unseen domains.

items.title: A Geometry-Informed Neural Operator surrogate of LISFLOOD-FP for rapid pluvial-fluvial flood forecasting: the case of Forlì, Italy
items.description: Physically based two-dimensional hydraulic models are too slow for real-time inundation forecasting and large ensembles.
items.ai_summary: Geometry-informed neural operator is a surrogate model for LISFLOOD-FP that accelerates real-time pluvial-fluvial flood forecasting and large ensemble simulations.

items.title: RangeFinder: Predicting Ligand Property Ranges from Protein Pockets
items.description: Identifying ligands for a protein target requires searching a vast chemical space for a comparatively small set of compatible molecules.
items.ai_summary: RangeFinder is an SE(3)-equivariant transformer model that predicts physicochemical ligand property ranges directly from protein binding pocket structures to narrow the molecular search space.

items.title: Same Outputs, Different Scores: Auditing the Unchecked Graders of Multimodal LLM Benchmarks
items.description: Every multimodal-LLM multiple-choice benchmark ends with a scoring rule that converts a model's response, often free-form text rather than a clean option letter, into a right/wrong verdict, buried in its code.
items.ai_summary: Study auditing multimodal LLM benchmark scoring rules finds that unexamined response-parsing methods can swing reported accuracy by up to 22 points.

items.title: Mixed-Methods Exploration of Sociotechnical Factors to Improve Adoption of Crime-Reporting Apps in Urban Communities
items.description: Crime-reporting mobile applications can enhance community safety and engagement in urban areas, yet their adoption remains low, partly because developers prioritize technological features over residents' social realities.
items.ai_summary: Study using a mixed-methods design identifies perceived value dimensions like safety and anonymity as the strongest predictors of crime-reporting app adoption and actual use.

items.title: Characterizing When Language Models Take Harmful Actions to Protect Their Assigned Goals
items.description: Recent language model (LM) safety failures have largely been studied as disparate phenomena. In agentic misalignment, a model blackmails an executive to avoid being replaced.
items.ai_summary: Methodology for analyzing language model safety failures formalizes the trade-off between assigned goals and harmful actions under different elicitation protocols.

items.title: EO-Jev: Decision Model for Earth Observation
items.description: Earth observation (EO) workflows require selecting among known outcomes, estimating confidence, and processing large volumes of imagery.
items.ai_summary: EO-Jev is a decision model adapted for Earth observation tasks through low-rank fine-tuning, improving accuracy, calibration, and transfer performance across public benchmarks.

items.title: Fuse To Align: Multimodal Representation Learning for Retrieval via Hypergraph Regularization
items.description: Multimodal retrieval must integrate complementary evidence from views that may be missing, noisy, or unequally informative. When a sample provides limited reliable evidence, learning from its views alone can hinder the acquisition of useful retrieval representations.
items.ai_summary: Training-time hypergraph fusion framework connects observed modalities within and across semantically related samples to improve multimodal representation learning for retrieval tasks.

items.title: Every Pixel Is an Option: A System One Model for Medical Ultrasound Biometry
items.description: Kev-Bio is a vision-language model that guides ultrasound landmark detection via clinical questions, generating spatial probability maps to derive measurements with reduced operator variability.
items.ai_summary: Kev-Bio is a vision-language model that uses clinical measurement questions to guide ultrasound landmark detection and produce spatial probability maps, improving biometry accuracy and reducing interoperator variability.

items.title: Multidimensional Suicide Risk Assessment with Machine Learning using Electronic Health Records
items.description: Suicide prevention remains a critical public health challenge, and electronic health records (EHRs) provide an opportunity to characterize suicide-related risk indicators using documented clinical, behavioral, medical, and social-contextual information.
items.ai_summary: A machine learning framework combines electronic health record data, age-matched cohort construction, and calibrated XGBoost models to estimate multidimensional suicide risk and identify key clinical and behavioral indicators.

items.title: Neural Actor--Critic Learning with Minimax Critics and Reflected Langevin Sampling
items.description: Actor--critic methods rely on critic gradients to improve continuous-action policies, yet finite-sample guarantees must control both value and gradient errors and their propagation through the actor.
items.ai_summary: A neural actor-critic procedure combines a regularized minimax Bellman estimator with a finite reflected Langevin sampler to establish finite-sample return guarantees and improve continuous-action policies.

items.title: Certifying Graph Neural Networks Against Label and Structure Poisoning
items.description: Robust machine learning for graph-structured data has made significant progress against test-time attacks, yet certified robustness to poisoning - where adversaries manipulate the training data - remains largely underexplored.
items.ai_summary: Deep Self-Training Graph Partition Aggregation is a semi-supervised learning framework that uses pseudo-labels and synthetic edges on graph partitions to certify neural network robustness against node-label and graph-structure poisoning.

items.title: NormMoX: A Normative Mixture of Experts for Explainable Autism Classification from Structural and Functional MRI
items.description: While structural and functional magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI, fMRI) offer profound potential for researching autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and understanding individual neurodivergence, current classifiers lack the explanatory power needed for scientific study, clinical use…
items.ai_summary: NormMoX is a normative mixture of experts model that uses healthy brain deviations to classify autism spectrum disorder from structural and functional MRI scans while identifying atypical brain regions and modalities.

items.title: FLAMIA: FLAsh MIcroscaling Attention for Fast and Causally Safe Training on Blackwell
items.description: FLAMIA accelerates Transformer attention on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs via MXFP8 and mixed-precision kernels that reduce quantization overhead, prevent causal leakage, and support variable-length packed documents.

items.title: ArabGeoText: Tool-Augmented Vision-Language Models for Arabic Geospatial Text Spotting
items.description: Geospatial text spotting involves locating and transcribing geographic labels, such as road names, district names, and landmarks, in raster maps. These labels are often small, densely arranged, and arbitrarily oriented.
items.ai_summary: A tool-augmented vision-language framework combines YOLO26 localization, crop rectification, and adapted Qwen3.5-4B recognition to spot and transcribe Arabic geospatial text in raster maps and remote sensing imagery.

items.title: The SIMPLE Law for Energy Cost of LLM Inference
items.description: A four-parameter analytical law predicts LLM inference energy across architectures, revealing quadratic prefill costs, GQA savings, and super-linear growth from reasoning budgets and agentic serving.
items.ai_summary: The SIMPLE inference model is a four-parameter law that calculates the energy cost of large language model inference using architectural hyperparameters, accurately predicting prefill and decode energy consumption without per-model calibration.

items.title: From FAIR to AI-FAIR Metadata-First Infrastructure for AI-Enabled Science
items.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies and their capabilities have advanced rapidly over the past few years, leading to widespread interest and adoption in the biological and ecological sciences.
items.ai_summary: An AI-FAIR metadata framework and agentic evaluation workflow extend traditional FAIR principles to provide bidirectional data integration and actionable feedback for missing metadata in AI-enabled ecological and biological sciences.

items.title: TrafficInstruct: A Multi-Task Network Traffic Dataset and Benchmark for Instruction Tuning
items.description: Instruction tuning for multi-task network traffic analysis requires data with clearly defined sources, supervision targets, and evaluation conditions.
items.ai_summary: TrafficInstruct is a multi-task network traffic dataset and benchmark featuring 55,000 structured supervised fine-tuning records across ten tasks to support instruction tuning for network traffic analysis.

items.title: Steering with Multilingual Lexicons for Sentiment Control in Low-Resource Languages
items.description: Activation steering offers a lightweight mechanism for controlling model behavior, but existing methods depend on sentence-level contrastive data that is unavailable for most of the world's languages.
items.ai_summary: Multilingual sentiment lexicons serve as a practical substitute for contrastive data in activation steering, offering a lightweight mechanism to control sentiment in low-resource languages while preventing linguistic collapse.

items.title: MultiInpaintCOCO: Fine-Grained Visual Understanding in Multiple Languages
items.description: Previous research shows that vision-language (VL) models struggle to understand fine-grained image details and tend to focus on the overall layout. Moreover, any weakness in English tends to be further amplified in the multilingual setting.
items.ai_summary: MultiInpaintCOCO is a multilingual benchmark of 953 minimal-pair examples across 13 languages designed to evaluate vision-language models on fine-grained visual details.

items.title: LLMs Depend on Specialist Tools for Out-of-Distribution Generalization in MS/MS Structural Elucidation
items.description: A frontier language model was recently reported to solve 1D NMR structural elucidation without tools.
authors: Devesh Shah Antonio H. de O. Fonseca
items.ai_summary: A study finds that large language models require specialist de novo structure generators to successfully perform out-of-distribution tandem mass spectrometry structural elucidation.

items.title: Calibrated Multiaccuracy: Deterministic and Randomized Sample Complexity
items.description: Calibrated multiaccuracy asks that a predictor be globally calibrated and multiaccurate with respect to a bounded test family $G$; that is, its residuals should be uncorrelated with every test $g(x)\in G$. This weakening of multicalibration suffices for many applications.
items.ai_summary: A research paper resolves the sample complexity of calibrated multiaccuracy, proving a separation in sample complexity between deterministic and randomized predictors.

items.title: EventGPT: Next-Event Pretraining on Banking Customer Histories
items.description: A model pretrained to predict a customer's next event can estimate the probability of future events without training on their labels and provide a reusable representation for supervised downstream banking tasks.
items.ai_summary: EventGPT is a hierarchical causal transformer pretrained on banking customer histories to predict future events and generate reusable representations for downstream tasks.

items.title: An Axiomatic Framework for Reinforcement Learning in Open Multi-Agent Systems
items.description: Open multi-agent systems, where only a subset of agents are controllable, are central to real-world domains such as smart grids, yet lack a principled foundation for reinforcement learning algorithm design.
items.ai_summary: An axiomatic framework for reinforcement learning in open multi-agent systems uses Shapley axioms to derive value function learning and improve learning efficiency.

items.title: SQLoom: Set-Contrastive Learning of Syntactic, Semantic, and Logical Dependencies for Text-to-SQL
items.description: Text-to-SQL translates natural language questions into SQL queries, enabling database access without writing SQL.
items.ai_summary: SQLoom is a constraint-aware fine-tuning framework that uses set-contrastive learning of syntactic, semantic, and logical dependencies to improve text-to-SQL generation.

items.title: Inferring Transferable Rewards via Active Inverse Reinforcement Learning
items.description: Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL) aims to recover expert rewards that transfer across environments with differing dynamics. Prior work has shown that such transfer is possible when gathering expert demonstrations across sufficiently different dynamics.
items.ai_summary: A two-phase active inverse reinforcement learning method selects environment dynamics to reduce uncertainty and minimize the expert demonstrations needed for transferable rewards.

items.title: ENGINE: Endogenous Variational MultiScale Optimization for Zeroth-Order LLM Fine-Tuning
items.description: Zeroth-order (ZO) optimization enables memory-efficient large language model (LLM) fine-tuning, and recent methods incorporate curvature-aware strategies.
items.ai_summary: ENGINE is a zeroth-order large language model fine-tuning method that uses variational multiscale optimization to reduce gradient variance and improve convergence speed.

items.title: Top-$k$ Retrieval Leaves Memory Value Undetermined
items.description: A memory-augmented agent must decide which memories to keep, merge and retrieve, and its only evidence of their value is its retrieval log: the memories it retrieved in each episode and whether it succeeded.
items.ai_summary: LEDGER is a memory retrieval and valuation method that estimates determined Shapley values with confidence intervals while identifying undetermined memory values.

items.title: Mesh-Agnostic Refinement Models for Latent Space Encoding of 3D Human Body Shapes
items.description: Parametric human body models such as the Skinned Multi-Person Linear (SMPL) model provide compact representations of human shape and pose, but their reconstructions remain affected by both errors in estimated latent parameters and limitations in the decoder's expressive…
items.ai_summary: A mesh-agnostic framework refines parametric 3D human body shape reconstructions by exploiting geometric discrepancies through latent varifold gradients, diffusion networks, and elastic optimization.

items.title: ReVA-HPE: Relative 6DoF Head Pose Estimation with Synthetic Pose Supervision and Personalized Virtual Anchors
items.description: Monocular head pose estimation is usually formulated as absolute regression from a single face crop, yet many applications observe the same person over time and can supply an explicit anchor image.
items.ai_summary: ReVA-HPE introduces a relative 6DoF head pose estimation method using synthetic pose supervision and personalized virtual anchors, achieving robust metric query poses without requiring ground-truth anchor poses at inference.

items.title: Specificity Bias and the Wikipedia Paradox: An xAI Analysis of AI Text Detectors under Domain Shift
items.description: The widespread adoption of Large Language Models (LLMs) demands reliable detection of human-authored versus synthetic text. However, current Transformer-based detectors often experience severe performance degradation during domain shifts and operate as opaque classifiers.
items.ai_summary: This paper investigates the robustness and interpretability of fine-tuned Transformer text detectors using SHAP, revealing systematic limitations like specificity bias and the Wikipedia paradox when handling out-of-distribution synthetic text.

items.title: On a Class of Non-Local Elliptic-Transport Systems in Score-Guided Probability Flow on $SE(3)$: Score-Singularity Resolution, Space-Time ADN Shift, and Markov Mean-Field Games
items.description: We establish mathematical foundations for optimal spatiotemporal vector fields governing continuous score-guided probability flows over bounded submanifolds $M \subset SE(3)$ on the Special Euclidean group $SE(3) \cong \mathbb{R}^3 \times SO(3)$.
items.ai_summary: This paper establishes mathematical foundations for optimal spatiotemporal vector fields governing score-guided probability flows on SE(3), resolving score drift singularities and extending the system to Markov Mean-Field Games.

items.title: Strictly proper scoring rules for node selection tasks on graphs
items.description: In node selection tasks, the goal is to identify a single unknown target node in a graph. We consider probabilistic supervised node selection, where the estimator outputs a probability distribution over the nodes of the graph and the ground-truth node is available for evaluation.
items.ai_summary: Two graph-aware scoring rules, the Resistance score and the Diffusion score, are introduced for probabilistic node selection tasks to detect meaningful estimation quality differences that classical metrics miss.

items.title: Diverse-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Generative Recommendation
items.description: Generative recommendation generates the semantic ID (SID) of the next item from a user's interaction history.
items.ai_summary: HERO is a diversity-aware on-policy distillation framework for generative recommendation that employs heterogeneous teachers and item rollout to mitigate popularity bias and improve recommendation diversity.

items.title: A Human-Verified AI Workflow for Annotating Environmental Sound Data
items.description: Large-scale annotation of environmental sound recordings presents significant challenges under time and resource constraints, particularly when sound categories are imbalanced and only part of a dataset has been labeled.
items.ai_summary: A human-AI workflow combining a fine-tuned Audio Spectrogram Transformer with human verification reduces environmental sound annotation labor by forty-one percent while maintaining high accuracy.

items.title: DeepWaveRL: Self-Supervised Full Waveform Inversion via Reinforcement Learning
items.description: Full Waveform Inversion (FWI) is a fundamental inverse problem in geophysics to estimate subsurface properties, such as velocity, from seismic measurements.
items.ai_summary: DeepWaveRL integrates reinforcement learning into self-supervised full waveform inversion, reformulating policy learning to estimate subsurface velocity maps from seismic measurements without accessing forward operator gradients.

items.title: The Cost of Mismatch: Noise Amplification in Zeroth-Order Reinforcement Learning
items.description: Zeroth-order (ZO) optimization has emerged as a promising approach for memory-efficient large language model (LLM) post-training, yet its reliable application to reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) remains largely unexplored.
items.ai_summary: ZO-BOLT applies zeroth-order optimization to a weighted SFT objective to improve memory efficiency and performance in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards for large language models.

items.title: Rethinking Fairness Metrics for Multi-Class and Multi-Group Assessment: Not Everything is Binary
items.description: Artificial Intelligence, and Machine Learning in general, is becoming pervasive across all domains and disciplines. By means of this data-driven approach, algorithms can learns complex task just by learning from samples.
items.ai_summary: This work proposes generalized multi-group and multi-class formulations of fairness metrics to overcome the empirical assessment distortions caused by forcing non-binary data into binary simplifications.

items.title: Poisson Super Learning For Survival And Competing Risks On A Discretized Time Scale
items.description: We introduce the Poisson Super Learner, a scalable ensemble method for survival and competing risks prediction with right-censored data. The approach exploits the correspondence between the likelihood of piecewise-constant hazard models and the Poisson likelihood.
items.ai_summary: The Poisson Super Learner is a scalable ensemble method for survival and competing risks prediction that combines interval-specific hazard learners under a common Poisson loss using right-censored data.

items.title: Anomaly-ranked confirmation slows new-class learning
items.description: Anomaly detectors rank unfamiliar examples for expert confirmation, and the confirmed examples teach a classifier to recognise a new class.
items.ai_summary: Empirical study showing that concentrating expert confirmations at the top of an anomaly ranking makes new-class learning less efficient across physics, medicine, and computer vision benchmarks.

items.title: R$^2$-Omni: Reducing Structural and Precision Redundancy in Omni-LLMs for Long-Form Generation
items.description: Omni-modal large language models (Omni-LLMs) typically process large numbers of multimodal tokens from audio-visual inputs, incurring substantial computational costs and a large memory footprint for the key-value (KV) cache.
items.ai_summary: Training-free framework called R^2-Omni reduces structural and precision redundancy in omni-large language models to improve long-form open-ended response generation.

items.title: A Common Language for Dynamic Graphs: Interaction Tokenization Enables Foundation Models
items.description: Dynamic graphs capture evolving interactions in Web systems, including online communication, user engagement, and recommendation. Graph foundation models aim to reuse predictive capabilities across networks, but extending this capability to dynamic graphs faces two challenges.
items.ai_summary: CL-DGFM is a common language dynamic graph foundation model that encodes interactions into tabular inputs for temporal link prediction without requiring target-graph parameter updates.

items.title: HyperFlow: Class-Incremental Semantic Change Detection via Hyperbolic Flow
items.description: Semantic change detection in remote sensing aims to identify and characterize land-cover transitions observed in pairs of satellite or aerial images.
items.ai_summary: HyperFlow is a hyperbolic flow method for class-incremental semantic change detection in remote sensing that models land-cover transitions as anomalies within a semantic embedding space.

items.title: Forecasting How RLHF Responds to Reward-Model Edits Before Training
items.description: Responses with headers, lists and greater length receive high scores from reward models (RMs), and RLHF policies learn to produce these features even when true quality does not improve.
items.ai_summary: Covariance-based predictor forecasts how reinforcement learning from human feedback policies will respond to reward-model edits before training begins.

items.title: ScienceCUA: Resource-to-Skill Construction and Execution-Guided Skill Evolution for Scientific Computer Use Agents
items.description: Computer-use agents for scientific software require application-specific expertise. Much of this expertise is documented in human-authored software manuals and web pages.
items.ai_summary: ScienceCUA is a two-stage framework that constructs executable skills from scientific software documentation and evolves them using execution feedback for computer-use agents.

items.title: Axion 1.0: Open Agent Foundation Models, Simplified
items.description: Axion 1.0 is an open agent foundation model trained via a concise three-stage pipeline of supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, achieving competitive agentic performance while fully releasing its data and training recipe.
items.ai_summary: Axion 1.0 is an open agent foundation model trained via a simplified three-stage recipe involving self-contained reasoning, tool-dependent task construction, and reinforcement learning.

items.title: Calibrating Multimodal Test-Time Adaptation under Reliability and Availability Modality Shifts
items.description: Multimodal test-time adaptation (TTA) enables pretrained multimodal models to accommodate distribution shifts during inference using only unlabeled test data, without recourse to the original training data.
items.ai_summary: AdaPGC is an adaptive probabilistic Gaussian calibration method that helps pretrained multimodal models handle reliability and availability modality shifts during test-time adaptation.

items.title: Bagel: A Fast Bayesian Online Changepoint Detection Algorithm for Linear Models via Posterior Merging
items.description: Bayesian online changepoint detection provides a natural framework for quantifying uncertainty about whether and when a change has occurred. It also enables the use of prior information which can increase detection power.
items.ai_summary: Bagel is a fast Bayesian online changepoint detection algorithm for linear models that uses posterior merging to maintain a constant computational cost over time.

items.title: CL3DOD: Understanding the Stability-Plasticity Dilemma in Outdoor Class-Incremental 3D Object Detection
items.description: Class-incremental learning (CIL) for outdoor 3D object detection remains largely underexplored. Existing outdoor studies are limited to single-benchmark evaluations, with SDCoT++ considering KITTI and CL2OD considering nuScenes under different incremental settings.
items.ai_summary: CL3DOD is a class-incremental 3D object detection framework that addresses the stability-plasticity dilemma in autonomous-driving benchmarks using pseudo-supervision, knowledge distillation, and temporal consistency regularization.

items.title: AnchorComplete: Recovering Complete Scene Meshes from Partial Point Clouds
items.description: AnchorComplete reconstructs complete scene meshes from partial point clouds by combining partial-point conditioning with metric-scale coarse-to-fine generation, improving reconstruction under sparse views.
items.ai_summary: AnchorComplete is a framework that reconstructs complete scene meshes from partial point clouds while preserving observed geometry and supporting scenes of varying scales.

items.title: What Structurally Breaks an Agent? Auditing Difficulty in Stateful Tool-Use Workflows
items.description: An aggregate task score does not distinguish failures of scheduling, state retention, and candidate selection.
items.ai_summary: An executable diagnostic instrument quantifies how dependency depth, candidate count, active state width, and state snapshots affect the structural stability and failure modes of stateful AI agents.

items.title: Do Agents Still Follow the Rules? Benchmarking Rule Compliance under Agent Context Compaction
items.description: LLM agents compact long histories to fit their context windows, but the compacted context must still carry the operating rules that govern later actions.
items.ai_summary: ARCBench is a configurable benchmark built on an open-source agent harness that measures rule compliance during execution and analyzes the sources of violations under context compaction and adversarial settings.

items.title: CERBO: Certified Recourse at a Requested Rate for Gradient-Boosted Trees
items.description: Recourse-aware learning trains models so that people who receive an adverse decision can reverse it with an affordable change.
items.ai_summary: Certified Recourse Boosting is a method for gradient-boosted decision trees that returns models with certified actions to guarantee a requested recourse rate for rejected individuals within a specified budget.

items.title: Can Coding Agents Sustain Continual Evolution without Forgetting?
items.description: Empirical study shows continual harness self-evolution across software engineering tasks causes severe catastrophic forgetting, with performance on earlier datasets dropping sharply after later evolution.

items.title: Reducing SNAP Payment Errors at Lower Cost With AI: A Simulation Study
items.description: New federal legislation will require states with high payment error rates in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) to pay a share of benefit costs, potentially costing some states over a billion dollars per year.
items.ai_summary: A simulation study demonstrates that combining AI-assisted preauthorization flags with risk-based reviews significantly reduces Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program payment errors at a much lower cost than risk-based review alone.

items.title: CFD-driven symbolic regression of RANS transition models
items.description: Laminar-turbulent transition governs skin friction, heat transfer and losses in turbomachinery, yet Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) transition models rely on empirical correlations and hand-calibrated activation functions whose structural deficiencies cannot be resolved…
items.ai_summary: A CFD-driven sparse symbolic regression framework learns interpretable, closed-form corrections for RANS transition models using gradient-free optimization and field surrogates.

items.title: DynSL: Resource-Adaptive Model Training across Heterogeneous Edge Devices
items.description: Training models over data distributed across edge devices presents a trade-off: centralizing data simplifies training but raises privacy and regulatory concerns, while full local training may exceed the devices' compute and memory capacity.
items.ai_summary: DynSL is a framework that dynamically allocates model layers between edge devices and a server by continuously monitoring system metrics to reduce training time in heterogeneous environments.

items.title: On the Convergence of Vanilla Adam under Heavy-Tailed Noise and Index Sampling
items.description: Understanding how stochastic gradient noise affects the convergence of Adam is an important problem in stochastic optimization, particularly when the noise exhibits heavy-tailed behavior.
items.ai_summary: An analysis of vanilla Adam in stochastic optimization establishes convergence guarantees under heavy-tailed noise and index sampling, showing how batch sizes and dataset characteristics affect convergence.

items.title: CISA: Retrofitting Dense Attention Models with Chunk-Indexed Sparse Attention
items.description: Long-context LLM inference is costly because attention repeatedly reads a growing key-value (KV) history. We introduce Chunk-Indexed Sparse Attention (CISA), which retrofits pretrained dense attention models without gradient updates.
items.ai_summary: Chunk-Indexed Sparse Attention is a method that retrofits pretrained dense attention models to accelerate long-context inference by selecting fixed-size key-value chunks using compact summaries.

items.title: Written Once, Read Differently How Language Models Own Answers Steer Their Next Ones
items.description: When a language model answers a yes/no question, that answer changes how it answers a different question about the same entity.
items.ai_summary: An empirical study of language model self-commitment shows that a model's first answer writes a commitment direction into the residual stream that shifts how it answers subsequent questions.

items.title: Dhārā Bench: An Evidence-Oriented Retrieval Benchmark for Indian Knowledge Systems
items.description: Dhārā Bench is a retrieval benchmark for Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS), with 325 questions in 12 categories and 60,121 text chunks from 15 source groups.
items.ai_summary: Dhārā Bench is a retrieval benchmark featuring 325 questions across 12 categories, useful for evaluating information retrieval systems on Indian Knowledge Systems.

items.title: MoSoLoco: Monocular 3D Human Localization through Visual Latent Features and Social Context
items.description: Estimating the metric 3D position of people from a monocular camera is important for robot navigation and motion prediction. Lightweight pose-based localizers are attractive for robotic hardware with limited computational resources because they operate on compact 2D keypoints.
items.ai_summary: MoSoLoco is a monocular 3D human localizer combining pose-detector visual features and social context, useful for efficient robot navigation and motion prediction.

items.title: ACTOR: Action-Centered Temporal Organization for Literary Role-Playing Agents
items.description: Large language agents for literary role-playing are typically modeled around dialogue generation, leaving characters' non-dialogue behaviors and their dynamic evolution over story time underrepresented.
items.ai_summary: ACTOR is an automated framework that constructs behavior trajectories from novels, useful for improving literary role-playing agents in generating character-consistent actions.

items.title: Auto-Research Agent on MSA Organization to Improve Protein-Protein Complex Structure Prediction
items.description: An autonomous agent adaptively designs target-specific multiple sequence alignments for AlphaFold 3 by reasoning over biological hypotheses and self-directed experimentation, improving protein interface prediction with fewer sequences.
items.ai_summary: Autonomous agent for MSA organization is a system that iteratively refines sequence selection and pairing, useful for improving protein-protein complex structure prediction.

items.title: CoworkOS:Scaling Agent Coworkers for Real-world Automation
items.description: CoworkOS is a long-horizon agent harness that separates strategy from execution, supports human-in-the-loop collaboration via shared artifacts, and improves model performance through sustained automated post-training.

items.title: CUA-Master: Scaling Computer-use Agents through Open-World Recursive Improvements
items.description: CUA-Master uses nested recursive loops with open-world data and feedback-driven retries to continuously improve computer-use agents across diverse benchmarks.

items.title: Lab2Sim: Turning Real-World Experiment Videos into Interactive Virtual Experiments
items.description: Lab2Sim introduces a benchmark for converting science videos into interactive virtual experiments, and EduVideo2Code improves apparatus fidelity by encoding procedures as state machines for verified code generation.

items.title: ImRevoltexee/gonka-autoinject
items.description: GonkaRouter account farm + 9Router auto-inject daemon. Full registration flow, key verification, systemd units. Zero dependencies — Python standard library only.
items.ai_summary: Automation pipeline and daemon that registers accounts on GonkaRouter and automatically injects the generated keys into a 9Router instance.

items.title: Measuring AI Agents as Teammates with Collaborative Intelligence
items.description: The Collaborative Intelligence Benchmark evaluates AI agents as teammates across 240 tasks, revealing that even top models have significant collaboration weaknesses unrelated to individual capability.

items.title: Zguoxu/tiny-transformer-from-scratch
items.description: A tiny Transformer built from scratch in PyTorch, with an English-to-Chinese translation demo | 用 PyTorch 从零实现的小型 Transformer，附英译中演示，帮助理解模型原理
items.ai_summary: Small Transformer implemented from scratch in PyTorch, featuring a complete training and English-to-Chinese translation demo in a single file.

items.title: DR Pixel: Page-Native Deep Research with Vision-Language Models
items.description: DR Pixel is an open-source multimodal agent that performs deep research directly on rendered document page images, improving retrieval and reasoning over scientific papers through counterfactual credit reweighting.

items.title: LEANGUARD: Lean-Verified Guardrails for Tool-Using Agents
items.description: LeanGuard is a verified runtime that blocks policy-violating tool calls by language-model agents and can repair them via proof-guided search, reducing unauthorized executions and prompt-injection success without harming benign task performance.

items.title: PhotoGuider: Composition-Aware Cropping and 360^{circ} View Framing with Explainable Photographic Assessments
items.description: PhotoGuider selects viewing directions and frames 360° panoramas using shared composition-aware tokens and produces camera-parameter outputs with explanation-conditioned scoring.

items.title: Avatar Intelligence: Amplifying Human Agency Through Persistent Personal Agents
items.description: Personal AI agents are increasingly capable of handling long-horizon tasks across applications, yet users often need to invest substantial effort in specifying goals, resolving ambiguity, and verifying outcomes.

items.title: When Does Latent Prediction Error Support Physical Surprise Claims in Video World Models?
items.description: The study evaluates frozen video representations to show that prediction errors reflect appearance and motion rather than reliably measuring physical surprise.

items.title: CrossSWE: Benchmarking Cross-Repository Joint Development for Coding Agents
items.description: CrossSWE introduces a multi-repository benchmark showing that current LLMs struggle with cross-repository consistency during joint software development.

items.title: SWE-Trail: History-Guided Trajectory Collection for Coding Agent Training
items.description: SWE-Trail improves trajectory collection for coding agents by using past rollouts to guide exploration without exposing history to the agent, yielding better-trained student models.

items.title: Advances in Agentic Computer Graphics
items.description: This report proposes a unified taxonomy and literature system for agentic computer graphics driven by large language models, analyzing trends and open challenges in human-agent collaboration and long-horizon planning.

items.title: Can Large Language Model Agents Learn by Watching Tutorial Videos?
items.description: Tutorial Agentic Learning enables LLM agents to continuously learn from instructional videos without parameter updates by building a structured tutorialbook memory and retrieving via reasoning-linked table-of-contents trees.

items.title: Democratizing Robot-Use Agents: A Unified Harness with Open Models
items.description: Uni-robot-agent enables open-weight robot-use agents to surpass proprietary models in zero-shot manipulation and suggests joint development of four core capabilities for future training.

items.title: NorthCUA Technical Report: Turbocharging Computer-Use Agents through Experience at Scale
items.description: NorthCUA scales computer-use agents via an experience flywheel, recursive self-improvement, staged learning, and reinforcement learning to achieve state-of-the-art open-source GUI and web interaction results.

items.title: modem-dev/boxery
items.description: Easiest way to give your coding agents VMs
items.ai_summary: Developer tool that lets coding agents create, fork, and manage their own Linux virtual machines across local, remote, and sandbox providers.

items.title: AKMaasif/Meta-Ai-Global-Hackathon-Ran-Sentinel-
items.description: RAN Sentinel: AI co-engineer for mobile networks
items.ai_summary: RAN Sentinel is an AI co-engineer prototype built on Meta Muse models to investigate degrading mobile network cells and propose fixes.

items.title: Wave Forcing: Towards Speed-of-Light Streaming Video Generation
items.description: Wave Forcing enables efficient continuous long-video generation with consistent appearance and natural motion through co-designed generation, training, and execution, achieving high throughput and quality.

items.title: MOSS-Image Character & Style Catalog
items.description: MOSS-Image Character & Style Catalog

items.title: ElysiumForge-Labs/elysium-chain-mcp
items.description: MCP server for AI agents to read and interact with Elysium, Kinetiq’s Arbitrum Orbit L2 on Hyperliquid
items.ai_summary: Model Context Protocol server that allows AI agents to read and interact with the Elysium Arbitrum Orbit L2 network via JSON-RPC.

items.title: TinyAstral: Transferring Self-Evolving Harnesses to Tiny Generalist Manipulation Agents
items.description: TinyAstral improves robot agent harnesses via recursive self-improvement and distills compact students that retain performance gains with lower compute.

items.title: BYOD: Build Your Own DLM - Efficient Autoregressive-to-Diffusion Language Model Conversion
items.description: BYOD converts autoregressive language models into diffusion models via parameter-efficient LoRA adapters, enabling parallel generation with minimal training cost while preserving base-model knowledge.

items.title: From Fragmentation to Fusion: A Survey and Roadmap for Omnimodal Embeddings
items.description: Embedding research across modalities is converging toward shared principles via contrastive learning and Transformers, and a framework of coverage, comparability, and compositionality is proposed to unify it through transformation, alignment, and joint embedding.

items.title: Self-Improvement with Auxiliary Rewards: Learning from Verified Traces and Evaluating Transfer
items.description: Auxiliary trajectory preferences based on entropy and confidence metrics improve small language model self-improvement and transfer by distinguishing learning value among equally correct reasoning traces.

items.title: DeFT-RAG: Decomposing Multi-Hop Questions into Self-Contained Sub-Questions with Reusable Answers
items.description: DeFT-RAG improves multi-hop question answering by generating self-contained sub-questions sequentially, offloading reasoning to rule-based updates and a lightweight decision model, and caching answers to reduce LLM usage.

items.title: Diagnosing the Reference Gap: What Visual Scaffolds Can and Cannot Fix in Multimodal Reasoning
items.description: Multimodal language models fail at multi-step visual reasoning due to a reference gap rather than perception, and task-matched external references like numbering significantly improve accuracy without training.

items.title: Where Do Vision Language Models Fail at 3D Reasoning?
items.description: Vision-language models often judge 3D object properties correctly but fail to recover and consistently apply exact per-color counts, motivating evaluation by exact correctness, consistency, and visual dependence.

items.title: WorldFlow: Joint Video and 3D Motion Prediction via Large-Scale Pretraining
items.description: WorldFlow is a generative world model that jointly predicts future video and 3D trajectories using continuous displacement tokens and a Mixture-of-Transformers backbone, improving physical dynamics prediction across diverse benchmarks.

items.title: MAServeBench: Benchmarking Multi-Agent LLM Serving Systems with Hierarchical Collaboration Workloads
items.description: MAServeBench evaluates LLM serving and hardware by modeling multi-agent collaboration as a configurable workload dimension with reproducible dependency traces.

items.title: TSFLab: A Self-Improving Agent-Agnostic Workbench for Time Series Forecasting Research
items.description: TSFLab is a self-improving agent-agnostic workbench that equips coding agents with shared resources to reduce costs and automate maintenance for time series forecasting research and benchmarking.

items.title: Cross-Primitive Consistency in Jev
items.description: Jev's cross-primitive consistency is benchmarked and improved via a residual calibrator that reduces inconsistency and boosts decision accuracy.

items.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Teacher Evolution
items.description: Teacher-Evolution Self-Distillation improves on-policy self-distillation by continuously enhancing self-teaching reliability through reward-guided teacher optimization and adaptive down-weighting of unreliable samples.

items.title: Multi-Agent Relay Thinking
items.description: MACR introduces a relay-based multi-agent framework that dynamically transfers reasoning between agents using confidence-guided triggering and bidding to improve accuracy with lower token overhead.

items.title: Lost in Recovery: Demystifying Recovery Behavior of Computer-Use Agents via Goal-Oriented Action Replay
items.description: ReTrace is a framework that evaluates recovery behavior in computer-use agents by formalizing transition-consistent recovery and demonstrating that autonomous model-based recovery improves long-horizon reliability.

items.title: ProVe: Proposer-Verifier Decoding
items.description: ProVe reverses speculative decoding roles by fine-tuning a large model to propose token blocks and verifying them with a smaller or identical model, achieving faster autoregressive generation with adjustable speed-accuracy tradeoffs.

items.title: When Morphs Look Better: Face Image Quality as a Training-Free Signal for Morphing Attack Detection
