items.description: Deep reinforcement learning (RL) is a powerful framework for sequential decision-making. Despite many high-profile successes in recent years, deep RL is known to be brittle. An emerging line of research attributes this brittleness to a loss of plasticity in neural networks.
items.ai_summary: Plasticity-preserving methods increase learning robustness in stochastic deep reinforcement learning environments, with their advantages growing alongside observation noise levels.

items.title: CausalWAM: Learning the Causes of Actions in World Action Models
items.description: Causal World Action Models enforce sparse routing to isolate action-relevant latent variables, ensuring identifiable causal structure without requiring temporal independence assumptions.

items.title: Rethinking Asymmetry in Self-Supervised 3D Geometry Learning
items.description: Self-supervised learning relies on asymmetry between what a model observes and what it must explain. Recent methods learn 3D geometry from unposed images by predicting cameras and scene structure, then rendering held-out views.
items.ai_summary: Self-supervised 3D geometry learning is improved by imposing asymmetry in the 3D representation space and aligning sparse-context features with dense-context features and vision foundation models.

items.title: nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-NVFP4
items.description: Vision-language model from nvidia. 1.5k downloads and 122 likes so far.

items.title: Cost-Aware Stopping for Freeze-Thaw Bayesian Optimization: When Does One-Step Lookahead Suffice?
items.description: Freeze-thaw Bayesian optimization (BO) evaluates candidates in resumable increments but usually stops at a budget or convergence test.
items.ai_summary: Freeze-thaw Bayesian optimization uses a cost-aware one-step lookahead stopping rule based on expected improvement to trade training increments for efficient candidate evaluation.

items.title: RangeSWA: Training-Free Length Extrapolation for Continuous Diffusion Language Models
items.description: Continuous diffusion language models show promising potential in text generation tasks, but are prone to problems such as text repetition, semantic drift, and generation quality degradation when the generation length exceeds the training length.
items.ai_summary: RangeSWA is a training-free length extrapolation method that combines local sliding-window attention, remote block summaries, and dynamic content retrieval to improve continuous diffusion language models.

items.title: Juneo-Lab/decision-forge
items.description: Compile organizational policy into verifiable decision training data.
items.ai_summary: Tool that compiles organizational policies into verifiable decision training data to build trustworthy AI agents.

items.title: Think in 360°: Benchmarking and Bootstrapping Panoramic Video Reasoning
items.description: A panoramic video captures all directions around the camera, but relevant evidence can appear in different directions and at different times. Understanding it requires models to connect observations across the viewing sphere and time.
items.ai_summary: PanoVideoReasoner uses a panoramic video benchmark and sphere-time-grounded reasoning datasets to improve cross-view tracking and evidence integration in panoramic video understanding models.

items.title: Differentially Private Synthetic Data from Sliced Chebyshev Moments
items.description: Research on practical differentially private (DP) synthetic data has largely focused on methods that approximately preserve low-dimensional marginals of a target distribution, and can thus only hope to preserve higher-dimensional, global structure as a lucky by-product.
items.ai_summary: SPLICE is a differentially private synthetic data algorithm that measures noisy sliced Chebyshev polynomial moments to achieve high-dimensional global distributional guarantees without dimension-dependent error scaling.

items.title: RAMA: Retrieval-Augmented Multi-Agent Routing with Episodic Memory for LEO Satellite Networks
items.description: Low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks present a challenging routing environment due to rapidly changing topology, traffic, and link conditions.
items.ai_summary: RAMA is a retrieval-augmented multi-agent deep reinforcement learning framework that uses episodic memory and auxiliary objectives to improve scalable decentralized routing in LEO satellite networks.

items.title: The Knowledge Layer Model (KLM): Evidence-Visible AI Output, Routing Diagnostics, and Negative Results
items.description: AI answers require more than apparent correctness: reviewers need to inspect their recorded basis.
items.ai_summary: The Knowledge Layer Model is an open specification for inference records that provides versioned epistemic assessments, evidence relations, and explicit unknowns for AI outputs.

items.title: PersonaChatBench: Evaluating Chat Assistants with Diverse Simulated Users
items.description: Conversational assistants are expected to help people with diverse backgrounds, preferences, and communication styles. Yet evaluations centered on a single cooperative user provide limited insight into how reliably an assistant serves users with different personas.
items.ai_summary: PersonaChatBench evaluates conversational assistants by pairing fixed tasks with multiple simulated users guided by diverse private persona cards to measure task competence and need fulfillment.

items.title: CRoS: Causality Reward on Scrambled CoTs Improves Accuracy and Reasoning Faithfulness
items.description: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become the standard method for training language models to reason. However, RLVR typically relies solely on outcome correctness, which does not guarantee that the CoT causally contributes to the final answer.
items.ai_summary: CRoS is a chain-of-thought causality metric that perturbs reasoning step order instead of content, improving accuracy, reasoning quality, and faithfulness in language models.

items.title: REA: A Routed Embodied Agent Runtime for Asynchronous Brain-Cerebellum Control
items.description: REA unifies deliberative and reactive policies in a single runtime with asynchronous coordination, achieving high success rates with reduced control overhead across simulated and real robot tasks.
items.ai_summary: REA is a routed embodied agent runtime that coordinates a deliberative brain, a router, and reactive policies asynchronously without letting fast execution wait on the brain.

items.title: Exact Theory and Optimal Stepsizes for Stochastic Gradient Descent in Smooth Convex Minimization
items.description: This work considers the design of stepsize schedules for stochastic gradient descent in smooth convex optimization. Throughout, we assume that gradient noise is conditionally zero-mean with bounded variance.
items.ai_summary: Exact worst-case analysis of stochastic gradient descent in smooth convex minimization provides minimax optimal stepsize schedules and proves their uniqueness under bounded variance.

items.title: A richness-sensitive Acoustic Biodiversity Index from species-level detections: classifier benchmarking, false-positive control and validation against standard soundscape indices in an African savanna and an urban zoo
items.description: Acoustic indices are widely used as rapid proxies for biodiversity, but they summarise the distribution of sound energy rather than the species producing it and often track richness poorly.
items.ai_summary: Acoustic Biodiversity Index (ABI_E) uses species-level detections and Shannon diversity to provide an acoustic index that correlates strongly with species richness.

items.title: Near-Optimal Second-Order Convex Finite-Sum Optimization under Individual Smoothness
items.description: We study the stochastic second-order oracle complexity of solving smooth convex finite-sum optimization with $n$ components.
items.ai_summary: This paper establishes a new lower complexity bound and designs a Taylor-corrected lazy Newton method for smooth convex finite-sum optimization under individual smoothness.

items.title: Same Question, Different Answers: Auditing Persona-Dependent Variation in Six LLMs on Smoking-Cessation Advice
items.description: Hundreds of millions of people now ask large language model (LLM) chatbots for health advice, which raises a question that is simple to pose and hard to answer: does everyone get the same advice?
items.ai_summary: An audit of six large language models on smoking-cessation advice reveals that responses vary significantly depending on user personas and demographic attributes.

items.title: Learning Clean Generative Processes from Noisy Measurements
items.description: We study how to learn a generative model of clean images using only noisy observations. Diffusion processes and their generalizations to non-Gaussian noise require posterior predictions at every noise level.
items.ai_summary: A learning method for clean generative models from noisy observations uses Noise2Noise regression and a consistency relation to repair predictions beyond training noise levels.

items.title: Any Forcing: Any-Step Generality and One-Step Stability for Autoregressive Video Generation
items.description: Autoregressive video generation enables efficient inference through streaming prediction.
items.ai_summary: Any Forcing is an autoregressive video generation framework that uses a unified adversarial discriminator and an adaptive memory selection mechanism to achieve stable one-step generation.

items.title: There Is No Free Loop: When Does Looping a Trained Model Pay for Its Inference Compute?
items.description: Looping re-applies a block of layers so that each token passes through the block more than once. Adding a loop to a trained model is attractive because it leaves the parameter count, and hence the disk size, the memory footprint and the training cost unchanged.
items.ai_summary: Evaluating looped models across different sizes shows that adding loops to pretrained models only improves performance for small models with fixed parameter budgets.

items.title: Empirical Evaluation of Quantum Kernel Methods for Classification: A Comparative Study with Classical Kernels
items.description: Quantum kernel methods are the most concrete near-term proposal for quantum machine learning on classical data, yet published benchmarks disagree on whether they outperform tuned classical kernels, and the disagreement cannot be resolved from the literature because the…
items.ai_summary: A comparative study of quantum and classical kernel methods reveals that quantum kernels are statistically indistinguishable from tuned RBF kernels when bandwidth is properly tuned.

items.title: CausalXRL: Explainable Reinforcement Learning through Causal Graph Reasoning
items.description: Reinforcement learning is a powerful paradigm for training autonomous agents and has achieved impressive performance in complex environments.
items.ai_summary: CausalXRL is an explainable reinforcement learning framework that uses causal graph reasoning to provide structured, multi-level explanations of agent decision-making.

items.title: A Neural Network Approach towards Real-Time Knot Point Density Estimates for the Nonlinear Quadrotor
items.description: Spline representations provide a compact way to approximate continuous trajectories using a finite number of parameters. When approximating trajectories generated by dynamical systems, the efficiency of a spline representation depends strongly on the placement of knot points.
items.ai_summary: A learning-based method uses a neural network to estimate local trajectory variations and construct adaptive, nonuniform knot distributions for B-spline approximations.

items.title: GhostPrefix: Synchronization-Free Universal Prefix Attacks for ASR Manipulation
items.description: We present GhostPrefix, the first synchronization-free universal adversarial prefix attack against automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems.
items.ai_summary: GhostPrefix is a synchronization-free universal adversarial prefix attack that prepends short audio segments to live speech to control automatic speech recognition outputs in real time.

items.title: Know When the Equation Is Wrong: Structural Uncertainty for LLM-Guided Symbolic Regression under Extrapolation
items.description: Large language models (LLMs) can help discover mathematical equations from data, but most LLM-guided symbolic regression methods focus on a single best equation without quantifying uncertainty over alternative functional forms.
items.ai_summary: LLM-SR-UQ is an uncertainty quantification framework for symbolic regression that preserves competing equation structures and uses their disagreement to define structural prediction intervals.

items.title: Asynchronous Flow Map Language Models
items.description: The order in which tokens are predicted in language modeling has a profound impact on the quality of generated sequences.
items.ai_summary: Asynchronous flow map language models incorporate token prediction order into one-step parallel generation by learning flow maps with state-adaptive schedules.

items.title: When Does Jacobian Fine-Tuning Stabilize Neural PDE Emulators?
items.description: Neural emulators of chaotic PDEs are trained on one-step prediction but deployed autoregressively, where their errors compound. Jacobian-based regularisers aim to curb this growth, but in a chaotic system part of the growth is physical and cannot be trained away.
items.ai_summary: Jacobian fine-tuning stabilizes neural PDE emulators by penalizing the model's error amplification along its own error direction in chaotic physical systems.

items.title: TurnTurk-GPT: Text-Based Turn-Taking Prediction for Turkish
items.description: TurnTurk-GPT, a Turkish turn-taking predictor fine-tuned from GPT-2, outperforms multilingual detectors and reveals that Turkish end-of-turn cues rely on verb-final morphology.
items.ai_summary: TurnTurk-GPT is a text-based turn-taking predictor for Turkish that uses a fine-tuned GPT-2 model to detect end-of-turn cues in verb-final morphology.

items.title: TradeWar: A Benchmark for Execution-Grounded Trade Negotiation with Adaptive LLM Agents
items.description: Multi-turn negotiation remains a challenging problem for large language model (LLM) agents.
items.ai_summary: TradeWar is a multi-country simulation benchmark that evaluates execution-grounded trade negotiation policies using an economic health index.

items.title: GeoFlip: Benchmarking Geometry-Sensitive Physics in Video Generation
items.description: Video generation models synthesize realistic motion, but can they respond correctly to changes in initial geometry? We introduce GeoFlip, a video generation benchmark centered on physical outcome flips induced by geometry.
items.ai_summary: GeoFlip is a video generation benchmark that evaluates how effectively models translate geometric changes in initial frames into correct physical outcomes.

items.title: AutoAnalysis: An automated, self-updating meta-analysis of human-AI collaboration
items.description: As generative artificial intelligence (AI) becomes more capable and widely used, understanding when and how humans should work with these systems is becoming increasingly important.
items.ai_summary: AutoAnalysis is an automated, self-updating meta-analysis tool that synthesizes empirical evidence on human-AI collaboration performance across multiple studies and tasks.

items.title: Less Loss, Fixed Weights: Logit Corrections for Forgetting
items.description: When a language model is fine-tuned to follow instructions, or further pretrained on a new subject, it often gets worse at predicting standard web text.
items.ai_summary: Fixed adjustments to a language model's final token predictions can recover a portion of the performance lost during fine-tuning or pretraining without altering model weights.

items.title: SecPO: Principled Adversarial Training for Prompt Injection Security
items.description: Recognized as a top threat to AI agents, prompt injection allows instructions from untrusted data (email, documents, websites) to manipulate the agent's operation.
items.ai_summary: SecPO is an adversarial training and loss framework that significantly reduces prompt injection success rates in language models and AI agents without harming their general utility.

items.title: On Statistical-Computational Gaps in Graph Combinatorial Testing Problems
items.description: We study high-dimensional graph combinatorial hypothesis testing problems in which a signal is supported on the edge set of an unknown subgraph drawn from a class invariant under vertex relabeling.
items.ai_summary: A study on high-dimensional graph combinatorial testing establishes sharp statistical and computational thresholds and new gaps for signal detection across various graph structures.

items.title: DAMI: Dual-Axis Memory Initialization for Enhanced Long-Context Retrieval in Gated Linear Attention
items.description: Dual-Axis Memory Initialization improves long-context retrieval in gated linear recurrent models by jointly configuring decay and sensitivity parameters before training.
items.ai_summary: Dual-Axis Memory Initialization is a memory configuration method that improves long-context retrieval accuracy in linear attention models without adding trainable parameters.

items.title: MoETok: Sparse Expert Routing for 1D Visual Tokenizers
items.description: Modern visual tokenizers aim to preserve fine-grained visual details while learning high-level semantic representations for downstream generation and understanding.
items.ai_summary: MoETok is a sparse expert routing method for 1D visual tokenizers that uses role-specialized paths to improve image reconstruction, semantic representation, and generation.

items.title: ID2Pattern: Pretraining Generalizable Identity Behavior Patterns for Transaction Risk Foundation Models
items.description: Large-scale behavioral pretraining offers a promising route to generalizable representations in online payment systems. However, high-cardinality identity fields such as card, device, and account IDs, though rich in behavioral signals, remain underexploited.
items.ai_summary: ID2Pattern is a pretraining framework that encodes identity behavior patterns into discrete sequences to improve transaction risk models and generalize to unseen users.

items.title: FoAViS: Analyzing Learned Fixation Strategies in a Foveated Active Vision System
items.description: Human vision is foveated and active: resolution is highest at the fovea and falls off towards the periphery, and fixations are actively directed to locations of interest.
items.ai_summary: FoAViS is a foveated active vision system that uses learned fixation policies to select task-specific image locations, improving performance on classification and semantic segmentation.

items.title: TwinPast: Benchmarking Historical Evidence Use in Streaming Video Understanding with Evidence Contrastive Video Pairs
items.description: High accuracy on streaming video benchmarks does not establish whether a model uses visual history.
items.ai_summary: TwinPast is a benchmarking framework using contrastive video pairs to evaluate whether streaming video models properly use historical visual evidence rather than relying only on recent frames.

items.title: New Lower Bounds for Private PAC Learning
items.description: We study realizable PAC learning under approximate differential privacy, and give a framework for proving lower bounds on its sample complexity.
items.ai_summary: A new framework for private PAC learning establishes lower bounds on sample complexity using the Independent Class Packing parameter, yielding tight bounds for several geometric concept classes.

items.title: When Does Test-Time Search Help World Action Models? An Empirical Audit of Candidate Selection and Simulator Integrity
items.description: World-action models increasingly apply test-time scaling, spending extra inference computation on candidate selection and adaptive allocation to improve control.
items.ai_summary: An empirical audit of test-time search in world-action models reveals limitations in candidate selection signals, realized speedups, and evaluation integrity due to rendering corruption.

items.title: Prune Gradually, Adapt Sparsely: Efficient Pruning of Large Language Models at Extreme Sparsity
items.description: Weight pruning can reduce the storage and inference cost of large language models (LLMs), but preserving quality at high sparsity levels remains challenging. Existing methods face a quality-cost trade-off in this regime.
items.ai_summary: ETAPS is a pruning framework for large language models that gradually removes weights in stages and adapts sparsely, achieving lower perplexity and drastically reduced computational cost compared to existing methods.

items.title: When Is a Game a Markov Decision Process? Correspondences Between Game Theory and Reinforcement Learning
items.description: Reinforcement learning and game theory describe the same object from two sides. Game theory says what a rational outcome of a strategic interaction is; reinforcement learning says how an agent could reach one through experience.
items.ai_summary: A new monograph bridges game theory and reinforcement learning by establishing formal mathematical correspondences that prove every standard class of game can be viewed as a Markov decision process.

items.title: Robust Learning of Multi-Index Models under Logconcave Distributions via Weak Partial Learners
items.description: We develop a new algorithmic framework for learning Boolean concept classes under logconcave distributions. Our framework applies to broad families of multi-index models and yields significantly faster robust learners than were previously known in these settings.
items.ai_summary: A new algorithmic framework uses weak partial learners and recursive moment-based partitioning to efficiently and robustly learn Boolean concept classes and multi-index models under logconcave distributions.

items.title: WASABI: Wasserstein Sampling via Bridge Interpolants
items.description: Sampling from Boltzmann distributions is a fundamental problem in physics, chemistry, and biology.
items.ai_summary: WASABI is a diffusion model training method that minimizes KL divergence using Wasserstein gradient flows to generate samples from a target Boltzmann distribution using only the energy function.

items.title: Chronos-2: A foundation model for multivariate time series forecasting
items.description: Accurate forecasting with uncertainty quantification is critical in a variety of scientific applications ranging from epidemiology and economics to energy systems and earth sciences.
items.ai_summary: Chronos-2 is a multivariate time series foundation model that performs zero-shot probabilistic forecasting by modeling interactions between multiple time series and heterogeneous covariates.

items.title: Shock Loading Accesses Reaction Pathways beyond Accelerated Thermolysis
items.description: Thermolysis and shock loading can produce similar major stable products in energetic materials, despite different chemical evolution and reaction pathways.
items.ai_summary: EMFF-MACE is a reactive machine-learning potential that enables simulations of energetic materials, revealing that shock loading accesses distinct reaction pathways and structural states compared to thermolysis.

items.title: Aligning MLLMs with the Latent Structure of Human Cognition via Behavior-Derived Semantic Dimensions
items.description: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have achieved impressive performance across a wide range of reasoning tasks, yet it remains unclear whether their internal representations and decision criteria align with the latent structure of human cognition.
items.ai_summary: A novel framework aligns multimodal large language models with human cognitive representations by using behavior-derived semantic dimensions and dimension-grounded linguistic rationales from human similarity judgements.

items.title: Optimizing Stochastic Policy Geometry for Few-Step Flow Reinforcement Learning
items.description: Few-step flow models generate samples through a handful of large denoising transitions.
items.ai_summary: Geo-FSRL is a geometry-optimized reinforcement learning method for few-step flow models that selects stochastic policies by minimizing a conditional KL divergence geometry factor.

items.title: Sensorium: An Open-Source Multimodal Data Collection and Curation Library for Embodied Surgical AI
items.description: Embodied surgical AI requires reliable multimodal data, yet surgical data collection remains costly, difficult to repeat, and strongly dependent on the hardware setup.
items.ai_summary: Sensorium is an open-source Python library for recording, processing, annotating, and curating multimodal surgical data from configurable robot and sensor streams.

items.title: Observable-Specific Validity Tests for Scientific AI: Controlled Approximations and Intervention Response
items.description: An approximation can reproduce an energy while missing its response, or satisfy an error tolerance without being certified by a given bound.
items.ai_summary: Observable-specific validity records for scientific AI link model reductions to reference models, error measures, and intervention responses to provide checkable guarantees of controlled approximation and physical transfer.

items.title: Binary Sparse Codes: Where are we on Energy Efficient Representations?
items.description: Biological neural systems achieve impressive computational capabilities under tight metabolic constraints, relying on sparse cortical representations that minimise total neural activity.
items.ai_summary: Metric framework that formalises information preservation as similarity preservation for evaluating binary sparse codes and quantifying the trade-off between sparsity and informational structure.

items.title: Variance Reduction for Decentralized Stochastic Optimization with Multiple Local Updates
items.description: Multiple local updates are widely used in decentralized optimization to enhance communication efficiency, often in conjunction with stochastic gradients when exact gradient computation is costly.
items.ai_summary: Primal-dual-based decentralized optimization algorithm that integrates variance reduction with multiple local updates to achieve faster convergence and larger stepsizes while reducing communication costs.

items.title: IGDA-ICMH: an Importance Guided Feature and Network Dual Adaptation Framework towards Image Compression for Machine and Human Vision
items.description: With the surge of machine vision applications, image compression for both machine and human vision (ICMH) has become an important research area.
items.ai_summary: Importance Guided Feature and Network Dual Adaptation framework that uses implicit neural representations and low-rank adaptation to improve image compression for both machine and human vision.

items.title: Recommendation Feedback Loops Shape Urban Income Segregation and Venue Visitation
items.description: Location-based recommender systems shape where people go in cities and learn from the visits they steer, forming a human-AI feedback loop. This feedback loop shapes whom people share places with across income groups and which venues keep attracting customers.
items.ai_summary: Long-term simulation framework using fine-grained human mobility data to study how recommender systems and their retraining shape urban income segregation and venue visits.

items.title: Structure-Aware Skill Retrieval and Arbitration for Optimization Modeling
items.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) can turn natural-language optimization tasks into solver-checked answers, but current agents remain brittle under narrative rewrites and often store reusable experience at the instance level.
items.ai_summary: ArchOR is an archetype-centric skill agent utilizing centroid-aware representation learning and signature-guided retrieval to improve large language model performance on natural-language optimization tasks.

items.title: Completeness and Cost of Retrieval Structures for Multi-Tool Requests in LLM Agents
items.description: An agent that must call several tools to fulfill a request fails when the tool retriever omits any one of them, yet tool retrievers are mostly built and evaluated on queries requiring a single tool.
items.ai_summary: Study evaluating six retrieval structures across multi-tool testbeds to measure the completeness and computational costs of retrieving required tool sets for large language model agents.

items.title: Statistical Foundations of Reinforcement Learning: A Non-Asymptotic Perspective
items.description: Reinforcement learning (RL) embodies a foundational paradigm for sequential decision-making in the face of uncertainty.
items.ai_summary: Comprehensive monograph presenting a non-asymptotic statistical treatment of reinforcement learning focused on sample complexity analysis, minimax-optimal algorithm design, and finite-sample regimes.

items.title: ReX-GG: a LLM Ensemble Pipeline for Relation-extraction and Graph Generation
items.description: Current LLM ensemble frameworks focus on multi-step setups with additional modules for answer ranking, often opting for token and span analysis rather than structured outputs, leading to heavyweight architectures with potential fail states along the pipeline.
items.ai_summary: Customizable lightweight ensemble workflow of coordinated large language models that uses JSON-structured outputs and peer-review ranking for relation extraction and generating interactive causal graphs.

items.title: Using Machine Learning to Measure Self-Efficacy Belief Through Learners' Interaction Traces in Technology-Enhanced Learning
items.description: Self-efficacy beliefs play a critical role in learners' performance, academic choices, and, more broadly, in their future career trajectories.
items.ai_summary: Machine learning approach that analyzes learners' interaction traces in technology-enhanced learning environments to detect low self-efficacy beliefs and support early remedial practices.

items.title: General-purpose foundation models surpass specialized ones on chemical property prediction tasks
items.description: Foundation models (FMs) learn reusable representations from large collections of unlabeled data. In chemistry the corresponding data mainly consists of molecular structures, which are abundant, whereas experimental measurements are scarce.
items.ai_summary: Study comparing foundation models showing that general-purpose foundation models outperform specialized chemical foundation models on physicochemical and quantum-chemical regression tasks when experimental data is scarce.

items.title: On k-nearest-neighbor regression in metric spaces
items.description: We study mean squared consistency of k-nearest-neighbor regression for metric space valued features.
items.ai_summary: Study on the mean squared consistency of k-nearest-neighbor regression for metric space valued features that provides separate conditions for approximation error and conditional response variance.

items.title: Automated Keyword Generation Using LLMs in a High-Volume Data Virtualization Service
items.description: In modern data infrastructure, a data virtualization service (DVS) allows users to create many versions of source datasets for different processing tasks.
items.ai_summary: Study on automated keyword generation for virtual datasets using large language models and five text selection strategies to improve search engines in data virtualization services.

items.title: On-Chain Behavioral Signatures for Classifying Centralized Exchange Addresses on Ethereum Using Proof-of-Reserves
items.description: Centralized exchanges (CEXs) are key gateways between traditional finance and digital asset markets, yet identifying their blockchain addresses remains challenging.
items.ai_summary: Classification framework using LightGBM and Proof-of-Reserves disclosures to identify and screen centralized exchange addresses on the Ethereum blockchain.

items.title: Learning Nonlocal Interactions in Large-Scale Heterogeneous Metamaterials through Scientific Machine Learning
items.description: In multiscale systems, nonlocal interactions among spatially distributed constituents can unlock collective, potentially emergent behavior irreducible to individual constituent responses.
items.ai_summary: Domain-decomposition attention neural operator that learns configuration-dependent interactions in heterogeneous multiscale systems from field data alone to enable scalable design of optical metasurfaces.

items.title: How Much Can Tool Calls Reveal About You? Privacy Leakage from Tool-Call Traces
items.description: Large language model (LLM)-based agents interact with external tools through protocols such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP), producing tool-call traces that may expose behavioral signals about users.
items.ai_summary: Benchmark called PrivacyTrace demonstrating that large language model tool-call traces can expose behavioral signals and facilitate user profile inference without access to conversations.

items.title: Text as an Index for Zero-Shot Cross-Domain Knowledge Tracing
items.description: Knowledge tracing (KT) predicts a student's next response from their history. New platforms often have question texts but no response logs for training, motivating zero-shot cross-domain KT.
items.ai_summary: Zero-shot cross-domain knowledge tracing method that uses question texts as an index and separates behavioral sequence modeling from domain-local historical evidence construction.

items.title: Fuzzy selective state model for forecasting the dynamics of consumer preferences
items.description: We consider forecasting the dynamics of consumer preferences of retail chain customers. A customer's preference is described by a triangular fuzzy number.
items.ai_summary: Mamba-type selective state space model using fuzzy numbers to forecast retail customer preferences without accumulating forecast vagueness over time.

items.title: Movens-Zero: Scaling Humanoid Motion Foundation Models with Large-Scale Human Videos
items.description: Scaling humanoid motion foundation models is constrained by the scarcity of diverse, robot-executable data and by the difficulty of jointly learning from heterogeneous multimodal inputs while supporting real-time closed-loop control.
items.ai_summary: Motion foundation model architecture trained on millions of human and humanoid motion sequences to enable multimodal motion generation and real-time closed-loop execution.

items.title: AI evaluators favor job applications written by certain AI models, independent of candidate quality
items.description: Job applicants increasingly use large language models (LLMs) to write cover letters, while employers deploy LLMs to screen them. In this all-AI setting, we ask whether the \emph{choice of model} affects hiring outcomes independently of candidate qualifications.
items.ai_summary: Multi-model auditing framework revealing that AI evaluators exhibit systemic preferences for job applications generated by specific large language models independently of candidate qualifications.

items.title: Learning to Interact and Direct: Co-Evolving Video Director Agents
items.description: Video director agents orchestrate multistage production to realize users' creative visions. Emerging research on their self-evolution advances screenplay planning effectively. However, the mutual reinforcement between directing and user interaction remains largely overlooked.
items.ai_summary: Co-evolutionary framework comprising a director agent, simulated user, and meta engineer that improves the interaction and production capabilities of video director agents.

items.title: SimXAI: A Simple Drop-in Layer Increases Interaction Quality and Understanding in Conversational XAI
items.description: Conversational explainable AI (ConvXAI) agents often use GUS-style architectures with separate modules for intent recognition, dialogue management, and template-based response generation.
items.ai_summary: SimXAI is a lightweight conversational layer that connects large language models to external explainable AI resources, improving response quality and task completion accuracy.

items.title: Iterated Integrals as Lexical Fingerprints: Path Signature Embeddings for Lexical Similarity
items.description: While sentence embeddings are primarily designed for semantic generalization, their latent geometry implicitly encodes surface-level lexical properties, a relationship that remains poorly understood.
items.ai_summary: Path signature embeddings constructed from Word2Vec trajectories use iterated integrals to explicitly capture sequential and lexical sentence structures.

items.title: Dynamical Memory Transformer: Selective Recurrent Memories with Constant Cost Attention
items.description: Transformers retain an explicit history of the sequence, allowing attention to directly retrieve past representations. However, the size of the KV-Cache and the cost of a new token increase with the context length.
items.ai_summary: Dynamical Memory Transformer is a hybrid architecture featuring parallel dynamical memory units that separate sequence encoding from information reading to improve context handling.

items.title: Open-Weight MLLMs Cannot Compare What They Cannot Name
items.description: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) are increasingly capable of understanding images and performing complex visual reasoning, suggesting the possibility of using them to automate biological image analysis.
items.ai_summary: Open-weight multimodal large language models struggle with basic visual comparisons when semantic recognition fails, revealing a limitation where recognition gates visual reasoning.

items.title: ReuScope: Auditing Data Reuse and Evaluation Sensitivity in Capsule Vision 2024
items.description: We develop ReuScope, a protocol for auditing data reuse and evaluation sensitivity, using Capsule Vision 2024 as a case study.
items.ai_summary: ReuScope is a data reuse auditing protocol that uses cross-split overlap measurements and data removal experiments to evaluate dataset leakage sensitivity.

items.title: ObjectGuidedMap: An Object-Aware Model for Robust Bird's Eye View Map Prediction in High-Occlusion Scenarios
items.description: Accurate BEV map prediction is a critical component of autonomous driving systems, enabling downstream planning and control. Recent approaches such as Mask2Map achieve strong performance by predicting vectorized, instance-level map elements directly from multi-view images.
items.ai_summary: ObjectGuidedMap is a multitask architecture that jointly predicts bird's-eye view maps and 3D objects, improving map prediction accuracy in heavily occluded scenes.

items.title: PGGT-Loc: Primitive-Grounded Geometry Transformer for Feed-Forward Camera Localization
items.description: Camera localization methods are mostly multi-stage pipelines relying on dedicated and complex maps that are costly to construct, store, and maintain over time.
items.ai_summary: PGGT-Loc is a geometry transformer network that estimates camera poses by matching query images directly to planar map primitives for feed-forward camera localization.

items.title: Overcoming the Representational Limitations of Amplitude Encoding for Quantum Neural Networks
items.description: Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs) offer a framework for learning functions from classical data, but their expressive power depends critically on how inputs are encoded into quantum states.
items.ai_summary: A fixed nonlinear feature map for amplitude encoding in quantum neural networks distinguishes all real inputs and improves classification accuracy over conventional encodings.

items.title: Trainable Vector Quantization for Large Language Models
items.description: Vector Quantization (VQ) is a rapidly evolving technique for compressing Large Language Model (LLM) weights, reducing memory usage, and speeding up inference.
items.ai_summary: TVQ is a trainable vector quantization method that uses gradient descent-based optimization to compress large language model weights while maintaining high performance.

items.title: ElTab: Elastically Looped Tabular Transformers
items.description: Tabular transformer models such as TabPFN achieve strong predictive performance but incur substantial inference costs, making them difficult to deploy in resource-constrained settings.
items.ai_summary: ElTab is a tabular transformer model trained with elastic-depth supervision that adapts to various computational budgets while maintaining strong predictive performance.

items.title: DIFFNAS: Predictor-Free Neural Architecture Search via Diffusion Model and Zero-Cost Evaluation
items.description: Neural Architecture Search (NAS) has advanced the automated design of deep networks, but remains computationally expensive due to reliance on model training or performance predictors.
items.ai_summary: Diffnas is a predictor-free neural architecture search framework using a discrete graph diffusion model guided by zero-cost performance proxies to efficiently find optimal deep networks.

items.title: A Patch is More Than a Token
items.description: Vision Transformers represent each image patch through a canonical token produced under one observation condition. That token is a powerful interface, but it is still one realized state of the patch.
items.ai_summary: Pmtt is a patch representation framework that extends image patches from a single canonical state to a structured family of representation states using frozen vision transformer backbones.

items.title: RECAST: REconstruction of Chain-of-Thought via Auditable Structured Traces
items.description: Large closed-source reasoning models expose only their final answers. The intermediate reasoning that produces those answers is hidden behind API surfaces, tool-call policies, and safety filters.
items.ai_summary: Recast is an open-source reconstruction framework that conditions a decoder on a question and a closed-source model's final answer to generate first-person structured rationales and training data.

items.title: Continual Reinforcement Learning Is an Integration Problem
items.description: This paper presents an opinionated set of ten desiderata intended to inform the design and evaluation of reinforcement-learning agents that learn continually throughout a continuing lifetime. We use these desiderata to examine a representative selection of existing approaches.
items.ai_summary: This paper presents ten integration desiderata and a persistent-world scenario to guide the design and evaluation of reinforcement-learning agents that learn continually throughout a lifetime.

items.title: Exploring Bad Minima in Transfer Learning
items.description: Transfer learning is a highly successful learning paradigm in deep learning which leverages knowledge from one task and applies it to another. Despite its success, the necessary conditions for knowledge transfer are unclear and require further research.
items.ai_summary: This dissertation explores bad minima in transfer learning through adversarial attacks, showing a strong empirical relationship between source-task generalization and target-task transferability.

items.title: Backpropagation-free Deep Learning for Time-Series Classification
items.description: Deep neural networks for time series classification (TSC) are trained almost exclusively by error backpropagation, which imposes update locking and the weight-transport problem.
items.ai_summary: This paper adapts three backpropagation-free learning rules to univariate time series classification using 1D convolutional architectures and evaluates them across 112 datasets.

items.title: What Standard Evaluations Hide About Detectors of Hijacked LLM Agents: Rare Attacks, Unseen Tools and Benchmark Transfer
items.description: Detectors can flag hijacked large language model (LLM) agents from the traces of the tools they call.
items.ai_summary: This paper evaluates detectors and monitors of hijacked LLM agents, demonstrating how attack rates, tool coverage, and dataset shifts significantly impact detection precision and performance.

items.title: Bethe Hessian Recovery through the Kesten-Stigum Regime
items.description: We show that outlier eigenvectors of the Bethe Hessian achieve weak recovery in the stochastic block model down to the Kesten-Stigum threshold, for every fixed common expected degree $d>1$. This extends previous recovery guarantees, which required $d$ to be sufficiently large.
items.ai_summary: Outlier eigenvectors of the Bethe Hessian achieve weak recovery in the stochastic block model down to the Kesten-Stigum threshold for every fixed common expected degree greater than one.

items.title: Towards Out-of-Distribution Uncertainty Quantification for Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials via Pre-Training
items.description: Informative uncertainty quantification (UQ) is essential for the practical deployment of machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs), as it provides insight into their reliability across chemical space.
items.ai_summary: Pre-trained uncertainty estimators provide viable zero-shot uncertainty estimates and reliable error correlations for machine-learned interatomic potentials across diverse materials science datasets.

items.title: On-device Detection of Wearer-induced NLOS on Chest-worn UWB Tags: Machine Learning, Link Indicators, or Both?
items.description: Ultra-wideband (UWB) enables high-accuracy distance estimation (ranging), but performance degrades in non-line-of-sight (NLOS) conditions.
items.ai_summary: This study analyzes on-device machine learning and radio link indicator classifiers for detecting wearer-induced non-line-of-sight conditions on chest-worn ultra-wideband tags under tight energy constraints.

items.title: Accurate and Auditable ECG Classification via Visibility Graph Neural Networks
items.description: Physicians read electrocardiograms (ECGs) from waveform shape and timing, yet accurate deep-learning classifiers rarely show which waveform regions drive their predictions.
items.ai_summary: LYNX-ECG is a graph neural network that represents heartbeats as sparse visibility graphs, achieving accurate and auditable electrocardiogram classification.

items.title: Whose Values, Which Contexts, and What Signals? Grounding Cultural Value Alignment with Re3Culture
items.description: Cultural value alignment requires not only model optimization but also a well-specified target grounded in real-human evidence.
items.ai_summary: Re3Culture is a large-scale dataset linking representative communities, realistic scenarios, and revealed value signals to ground cultural value alignment in human evidence.

items.title: Implicit Assumptions About Tasks in Continual Learning
items.description: Continual learning is the study of how a model accumulates knowledge from data received over time, rather than all at once. In practice, this is typically achieved by dividing a dataset into tasks and presenting them sequentially.
items.ai_summary: A study on continual learning investigates how partitioning trajectories at different granularities, presentation orders, and similarity structures affect model outcomes.

items.title: Different Models, Shared Failures: Auditing Frozen-Encoder Pools for Medical Segmentation
items.description: Average segmentation accuracy and model count do not reveal whether models fail on the same cases. We present CoFailMed, an audit of correlated failures in pretrained-encoder pools for medical segmentation.
items.ai_summary: CoFailMed audits correlated failures in pretrained-encoder pools for medical segmentation, showing that checkpoints within the same encoder family remain highly correlated.

items.title: Hard Sample-Conditioned Decorrelated Attention for Robust Face Recognition
items.description: ViT-HarDis conditions attention head disentanglement on sample difficulty, applying stronger decorrelation to hard face-recognition samples and only in final transformer layers to improve recognition without architectural changes or extra inference cost.
items.ai_summary: ViT-HarDis is a vision transformer for robust face recognition that conditions attention head disentanglement on sample difficulty to improve specialization.

items.title: Peeling the Matryoshka: Extracting Ontological Structure from Retrieval Embeddings
items.description: Taxonomy construction is essential for knowledge-intensive NLP yet remains costly: clustering-based methods (i) need careful per-corpus tuning and yield unstable hierarchies, while LLM-based pipelines (ii) depend on expensive task-specific training that does not transfer across…
items.ai_summary: PEEL is a minimal probe that extracts explicit parent-child taxonomies from the prefix-length granularity gradient of Matryoshka Representation Learning embeddings.

items.title: Clinical-Protocol-Aware Cyber Resilience for Connected Clinical Technologies Under AI-Enabled Adversarial Conditions
items.description: Healthcare increasingly relies on connected medical devices, clinical information systems, cloud services, and distributed-care technologies, creating cybersecurity risks across clinical workflows.
items.ai_summary: A proposed clinical-protocol-aware cyber-resilience framework uses bounded micro-networks to limit compromise propagation and evaluate cybersecurity risks in healthcare.

items.title: WorkIng: A Real-World and Synthetic Highway Work-Zone Benchmark Dataset for Autonomous Navigation
items.description: Highway work zones are critical edge cases for autonomous vehicles (AVs), combining atypical geometries and jurisdiction-specific regulations that existing benchmarks fail to capture: real-world datasets lack 360° multi-modal, full-scene 3D work zone annotation, and no single…
items.ai_summary: WorkIng is a dual-domain benchmark featuring real-world highway data and procedural simulations to improve autonomous vehicle navigation in work zones.

items.title: Stepwise-Querying: Distilling Reasoning without Access to Teacher Chain-of-Thought
items.description: Reasoning distillation is widely used to transfer the reasoning capabilities of large language models to smaller students through teacher-generated supervision.
items.ai_summary: Stepwise Querying is a reasoning distillation method that elicits step-specific explanations from black-box teacher models without requiring access to their internal chain-of-thought traces.

items.title: Measuring What Matters: A Causal Reliance Score for Histopathology Image Segmentation
items.description: Reliable histopathology segmentation requires models that rely on pathology-relevant structures rather than spurious background correlations.
items.ai_summary: The Causal Reliance Score is a causality-inspired evaluation metric that quantifies the sensitivity of histopathology segmentation models to foreground versus background variations.

items.title: Multimodal In-Context Learning with Explicit Rule Induction
items.description: A central challenge in multimodal in-context learning (MICL) arises from tasks that are ill-defined without context and require uncovering the underlying rules from demonstrations.
items.ai_summary: Explicit Rule-Induction for Multimodal In-Context Learning is a unified framework that improves multimodal in-context learning by inducing latent rules from demonstrations using multi-modal large language models.

items.title: Latent-Lens: Visual Perception in Small Language Models Through Latent Communication
items.description: Bridging independent vision-language models (VLMs) and small language models (SLMs) in a modular multi-agent system typically forces them to exchange information as discrete text, which creates a lossy bottleneck for spatial and fine-grained details.
items.ai_summary: Latent-Lens is a lightweight codec that bridges representation gaps between vision-language models and small language models in latent space, improving performance on visual question answering and image captioning.

items.title: Do LLMs Know When They Are Wrong About Molecules? In-Context Property Prediction with Self-Reported Uncertainty
items.description: Large language models (LLMs) are used in many domains, but molecular property prediction with them is still little explored.
items.ai_summary: A study evaluating frontier large language models on molecular property prediction finds that model accuracy improves with context on clean datasets while self-reported uncertainty weakly correlates with prediction errors.

items.title: Task Vectors Can Be Linearly Decomposed into Interpretable and Controllable Components
items.description: Task Vectors (TVs) provide a compact way to steer large language models, but they are typically treated as atomized directions merely extracted from hidden states, leaving their internal functional structure poorly understood.
items.ai_summary: A decomposition method separates task vectors into task recognition, task learning, and residual components using candidate-label unembeddings, providing more interpretable and controllable steering for large language models.

items.title: Search When Needed, Proceed When Reliable: Metacognitive Reliability Supervision for Efficient Agentic Search
items.description: Efficient agentic search requires large language models (LLMs) to determine whether they can reliably proceed with their current knowledge or need additional external evidence.
items.ai_summary: A metacognitive framework trains large language models to decide whether to search for external evidence based on the reliability of their intermediate reasoning states.

items.title: Locality-Controlled Out-of-Distribution Guidance for Robust Regulatory DNA Sequence Design
items.description: Designing regulatory DNA sequences for targeted gene-expression control is an important challenge.
items.ai_summary: LOCOGEN is an out-of-distribution guidance method for regulatory DNA sequence design that uses locality-based learning to protect motif positions while allowing exploration in background regions.

items.title: Leakage-Controlled Structure-Preserving Augmentation and Template-Aware Evaluation for Bangla Symptom-Based Disease Prediction
items.description: Bangla symptom-based disease prediction is commonly evaluated on a small, imbalanced structured benchmark containing many profiles that differ by only one or two symptoms.
items.ai_summary: A study on Bangla symptom-based disease prediction finds that train-only asymmetric Bernoulli perturbation improves the performance of boosted-tree models like XGBoost and LightGBM.

items.title: From Training Exposure to Membership Evidence: A Controlled Study of OLMo 2
items.description: Whether a language model was trained on a document matters for copyright, privacy, and benchmark contamination.
items.ai_summary: A controlled study using OLMo 2 evaluates membership inference in language models and shows that training exposure raises document likelihood and that matched counterfactual references improve detection accuracy.

items.title: SAR-TS-BERT: Physics-Guided Self-Supervised Pre-Training With Polarimetric Features for SAR Time-Series Crop Classification
items.description: Multitemporal synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery provides continuous, cloud-free observations of crop phenology for agricultural monitoring in cloudy and rainy regions, yet high-accuracy classification typically requires extensive labeled samples.
items.ai_summary: SAR-TS-BERT is a physics-guided self-supervised pre-training framework that integrates backscatter intensities and polarimetric features into a Transformer architecture for high-accuracy crop classification using synthetic aperture radar time-series imagery.

items.title: Leveraging Quantum Measurement Randomness for Shot-Efficient Diffusion Models
items.description: In quantum computing, the readout always carries finite-shot sampling noise. Suppressing this noise through repeated measurements raises the cost of a quantum neural network (QNN).
items.ai_summary: A quantum-enhanced diffusion method repurposes quantum measurement sampling noise as stochastic sampler noise, achieving comparable generation quality with significantly fewer shots.

items.title: UpLoop: Training Looped Transformers via Upcycling at No Extra Pretraining Compute
items.description: Looped language models can strengthen reasoning through repeated computation with shared weights, increasing execution depth without adding independent parameters.
items.ai_summary: UpLoop is a pretraining schedule for looped Transformers that uses upcycling to increase execution depth without increasing final parameter count, training tokens, or FLOPs.

items.title: Simple Features Beat Most AI Control Monitors
items.description: AI control relies on monitors to catch a capable model that sabotages its work. These monitors are evaluated on their ability to differentiate honest from backdoored code.
items.ai_summary: Simple features based on author style and problem characteristics can outperform most AI control monitors in detecting backdoors without running the code.

items.title: Hierarchical Residuals: A Minimalist Decoupling of Residual Width from Compute Width
items.description: Residual connections underpin Transformers, but they implicitly tie the residual width carried through depth to the compute width used inside each layer.
items.ai_summary: Hierarchical Residuals is a minimalist architectural change that decouples residual width from per-layer compute width to improve the FLOPs efficiency of Transformers.

items.title: Advancing Clinical Trial Outcome Prediction with Domain-Specific Large Language Models
items.description: Clinical trial failures are a major barrier to efficient drug development, incurring substantial costs and delaying patient access to effective therapies.
items.ai_summary: Domain-specific language models like BioBERT and BioMistral can predict clinical trial outcomes from trial registrations with higher ROC-AUC and PR-AUC than structured methods.

items.title: Nereus: A Large-Scale Underwater Dataset for Fine-Grained Attribute Understanding and Grounded Counting Perception
items.description: Underwater imagery records rich ecological information and supports applications such as science communication, fishery monitoring, ecological conservation, and oceanographic research.
items.ai_summary: Nereus is a large-scale underwater dataset containing 88,000 images and 2.68 million question-answer pairs for fine-grained marine organism perception and grounded counting.

items.title: GraphNIAH: A Benchmark for Long-Context Reasoning over Real-World Graphs
items.description: The needle-in-a-haystack (NIAH) benchmark was introduced as a test for measuring a model's ability to find small relevant facts within a very large body of input text.
items.ai_summary: GraphNIAH is a dynamic, automated benchmark built from real citation relationships to evaluate long-context reasoning over real-world graphs without benchmark contamination.

items.title: Precision--Recall Trade-off on the Inference Level for LLMs in Grammatical Error Correction
items.description: Large language models (LLMs) have recently been adopted for Grammatical Error Correction (GEC), achieving strong performance via both full fine-tuning and prompt-based approaches.
items.ai_summary: Repetition penalty parameters in large language models enable controllable adjustment of the precision-recall trade-off for grammatical error correction at inference time.

items.title: TSBPO: Tree-Structured Branching for Policy Optimization in Interactive Language Agents
items.description: Training interactive language agents from terminal outcomes poses three coupled problems: which task and state continuations to sample, how to assign delayed feedback to decisions, and how to aggregate token losses for multi-token actions.
items.ai_summary: TSBPO is a tree-structured sampling-to-update paradigm that improves the training of interactive language agents across multi-turn tasks.

items.title: From fleet trajectories to single-cell promises: hierarchically weighted conformal prediction for battery SOH monitoring
items.description: Interval predictions from conformal prediction are usually read as "90% coverage", but on nested battery data that number promises the fleet average, not the individual cell.
items.ai_summary: Hierarchically weighted conformal prediction repairs coverage gaps in battery state-of-health monitoring by using frozen side information to provide reliable individual cell intervals.

items.title: Retrieval-Augmented Initialization with Dual-Guided Inversion for Flow-Based Inverse Problem Solvers
items.description: Flow models have recently emerged as powerful generative priors for solving inverse problems. Despite their success, most existing flow-based inverse problem solvers initialize the reconstruction process with random Gaussian noise.
items.ai_summary: Retrieval-Augmented Initialization with Dual-Guided Inversion improves reconstruction fidelity in flow-based inverse problem solvers by generating better initial noise.

items.title: From WSIs to Bulk, Spatial and Single-Cell Transcriptomics via Multi-Scale Graph Neural Networks
items.description: Understanding the spatial distribution of gene expression is key to studying complex diseases like cancer. While Spatial Transcriptomics (ST) and Single-Cell Transcriptomics (scT) provide high-resolution insights, they remain expensive and scarce.
items.ai_summary: Multi-scale graph neural network predicts bulk, spatial, and single-cell gene expression directly from standard whole-slide images to aid cancer diagnosis and survival analysis.

items.title: Does Reasoning Make Language Models Agree?
items.description: Language models face two opposing concerns: monoculture, in which models err in correlated ways, and multiplicity, in which equally accurate models make conflicting decisions.
items.ai_summary: Study on language models finds that prompting models to reason increases output agreement, whereas observing longer reasoning traces signals conflicting predictions.

items.title: When the Past Shapes Action: Understanding Embodied Memory
items.description: Recent advances in generative foundation models have expanded the capabilities of embodied AI, enabling increasingly general navigation, manipulation, and long-horizon task execution.
items.ai_summary: Comprehensive survey categorizes embodied memory mechanisms and benchmarks in generative foundation models to support reliable and adaptive long-horizon AI agents.

items.title: OT-CAL: Optimal-Transport-Guided Adaptive Sample Selection for Efficient Visual Learning
items.description: Deep neural networks for image recognition are typically trained using mini-batches, with a forward pass to compute predictions and losses followed by a more computationally expensive backward pass to update model parameters.
items.ai_summary: OT-CAL is an optimal-transport-guided adaptive sample selection method that reduces training computation in deep neural networks by automatically choosing informative visual examples.

items.title: Radial Kernel Attention for Long-Range Modeling in Polymer Machine Learning Force Fields
items.description: We introduce Radial Kernel Attention (RKA) for long-range modeling in polymer machine learning force fields. Local neighbor graphs constrain communication across polymer chains and their surrounding environments, while explicit all-pair attention incurs quadratic cost.
items.ai_summary: Radial Kernel Attention is an attention mechanism for polymer machine learning force fields that achieves linear computational scaling while significantly improving energy and force predictions.

items.title: Towards Trustworthy Multi-stakeholder Recommender Systems
items.description: Recommender system (RS) nowadays has to reflect, combine, and solve often contrasting requirements and expectations from dozens of stakeholders.
items.ai_summary: Paper highlights key open challenges and questions for building trustworthy multi-stakeholder recommender systems that balance competing user and provider objectives.

items.title: A Self-Supervised Pose Estimation Approach for Construction Machines
items.description: Pose estimation is a computer vision task used to estimate a skeleton of dynamic systems to predict future movements. Most of the research in this direction is based on a supervised learning approach which requires a massive amount of labeled datasets.
items.ai_summary: Self-supervised three-stage contrastive learning model estimates the pose of heavy construction machines from unlabeled video data, improving real-image accuracy over baseline methods.

items.title: OpenVIO: A Versatile Open-Source Visual-Inertial Odometry System
items.description: Visual-inertial odometry (VIO) is a fundamental topic in robotics research. Beyond research, VIO has been adopted in a wide range of products. In this manuscript, we present OpenVIO, an open-source VIO system for research and practical applications.
items.ai_summary: OpenVIO is an open-source visual-inertial odometry system supporting pinhole, fisheye, and stitched 360-degree cameras for robotics research and practical applications.

items.title: Breaking Information Islands in Sparse Tuning via Small-World Connectivity
items.description: Sparse tuning is widely used to adapt large language models due to its parameter efficiency. However, its effectiveness depends not only on the number of trainable parameters, but also on the feature-interaction topology of the sparse update's structural support.
items.ai_summary: Small-World Induced Fine-Tuning framework uses block-diagonal sparse updates and scattering permutations to improve feature interaction and parameter-efficient language model adaptation.

items.title: microsoft/Mage-VL-Cowork
items.description: Vision-language model from microsoft. 752 downloads and 125 likes so far.

items.title: WeFair: Fidelity-Aware Alignment from Human Feedback for Personalized Query Rewriting in Short-Video Search
items.description: WeFair improves personalized query rewriting via fidelity-aware human feedback stages—demonstration, preference, and verification—to reduce intent drift and boost search effectiveness in short-video platforms.

items.title: HALO: Human-Grounded Granular Evaluation of Proactive Agents
items.description: HALO introduces a human-annotated benchmark and dataset to evaluate proactive agents, revealing that over-proactivity is the dominant failure mode.

items.title: Apriel Voice 27B Preview: An Open Model for Speech, Reasoning, and Tool Use
items.description: Apriel Voice 27B Preview is an open speech-language model that integrates speech understanding, reasoning, and tool use within a shared backbone, achieving strong results on audio benchmarks through a two-stage training procedure with online distillation.

items.title: On the Origin and Evolution of Training-Inference Mismatch in LLM Reinforcement Learning
items.description: On-policy reinforcement learning for large language models suffers from training-inference mismatch due to numerical discrepancies and policy lag, and a derived discrepancy-lag correction stabilizes training by centering errors, clipping importance ratios, and resynchronizing…

items.title: CaPtain: A Pipeline for Post-Training Code-as-Policy Robot Agents
items.description: CaPtain trains small open vision-language models via supervised fine-tuning and multi-turn reinforcement learning with a physical critic to perform robot manipulation through code, achieving strong results without frontier models or vision-language-action backbones.

items.title: Does Scaling Toward AGI Depend on What System-1 Lets System-2 Execute?
items.description: Co-designing a resource-heavy reasoning system with a lightweight predictive evaluator can reduce execution costs by filtering interactions, with efficiency governed by the density of useful interactions.

items.title: WorldBridge: Bridging Video and Action for Task Generalization in World Action Models
items.description: WorldBridge improves robot task generalization by combining video prediction with sparse action supervision via separate video and action experts, achieving state-of-the-art results across manipulation benchmarks.

items.ai_summary: Self-hosted server application that allows an entire company to access Claude Code and Codex through a browser interface using shared company files and permissions.

items.title: FrameForge: Harnessing Priors of Video Foundation Models for Unified Image Generation
items.description: FrameForge enables adaptive conditional image generation by modeling variable condition-target relationships through dynamic temporal experts and intermediate reasoning pathways in pretrained video models.

items.ai_summary: Recursive self-improvement framework that couples world generation with agent harness evolution to train multimodal agents across tasks.

items.description: CEPO improves multi-agent prompt optimization by separating shared coordination from agent-specific execution, boosting performance across benchmarks and scaling efficiently with more agents.

items.description: R²Orch uses recursive self-play with learnable task selection and skill withdrawal to train orchestrators without hand-designed curricula, improving performance across reasoning and interactive tasks.
